## Diff-minimization assessment

RETAIN: Retain generated fixture boundaries and shared producers; reconcile existing secret, provenance and corpus owners. Assigned JSON is branch-added generated data, not an inherited policy body. Shared host/Kotlin normalization and native D1/D2 metadata producers own generation; moving generated fields into inherited engine files has no reduction payoff. No inherited reduction credit

## Context and observations

Complete frozen and available current bytes for every assigned path were mechanically parsed with duplicate-member and nonfinite rejection, including recursive overflowed floats. Validated mission declared level counts and unique level/secret identities, D1/D2 games, recognized route statuses, diagnostics for failed/partial routes, sequential step indexes and present numeric/text travel pairs. Baseline records additionally have unique keys, consistent declared/status counts and 64-hex hashes; sidecars have schema-v1, nonempty titles and unambiguous basic selectors. These structural checks do not establish route playability, geometric clearance, generator completeness or cryptographic source trust. Root mission status may describe loading rather than every route; failed routes under an ok header are not admitted as a new generic finding

ACTUAL maintained test_mission_metadata_travel_times.ps1 PASS for 2639 current rows and test_mission_metadata_json_normalization.ps1 PASS for numeric precision, canonical order, variant paths and idempotence. These checks were run once for the combined 711-714 surface; travel oracle BR-0667 still skips absent fields, so its PASS does not close that owner. Full BR-0623, BR-0667, BR-0668 and BR-0670 were reconciled with the earlier producer/comparer survey. All seven assigned sidecars were fully read; unchanged bytes, slot/name domains and source filenames were checked, without rerunning audio fingerprints or independent credits verification

ACTUAL independent SHA-256 and size inventory of 108 unique assigned local mission archives, 724576956 bytes: all 94 recorded archives match both frozen and current manifests; 14 sources are absent from both manifests, extending BR-0623 rather than allocating a duplicate. All readable ZIP directories have descriptors and HOG/loose-level payloads. Four 7Z interiors were not decoded because neither 7z/7za nor py7zr is available; their complete source bytes were hashed. CD-source manifest and resolver correlate the five CD outputs to extracted disc source directories; no CD disc re-extraction or complete proprietary-source/license audit ran

Ulterior frozen four missions/80levels includes a two-level TEST descriptor and three identical-named platform variants; current one mission/26levels identifies REBIRTH/ULTERIOR.MN2. Current shared Kotlin preference is Rebirth, DOS, D2X, with XL unsupported; host masks only recognized paired identical descriptors and paired TEST content. Static policy explains intentional selection, but 7Z interior and regeneration were not executed here, so variant equivalence is not independently certified

## Diff-minimization assessment

RETAIN: Retain local historical planning records; reconcile publication scope with BR-0002 instead of duplicating product owners. This is a mechanical historical-document batch. Planning prose does not execute engine policy and does not justify moving or broadly deduplicating inherited D1/D2 behavior. The source-review queue owns concrete product reductions. No inherited reduction credit and no local planning-file deletion

## Scope and method

Every complete frozen blob was decoded as UTF-8 and fingerprinted; complete available current bytes were compared separately. Mechanically parsed headings, checklist markers, code fences, URL hosts and scoped private-key/token patterns. Title/status/checklist projections for every assigned path were inspected. This is document provenance/content classification, not a claim that every prose line was manually reread or that historical commands were executed. Checkmarks and result claims remain dated claims until independently validated at the product owner

ACTUAL frozen git grep with all1361 historical basenames, excluding the plan tree, returned seven outside references: pkg_reader format comment, paired joy.c key-map comments, two outstanding_bugs pointers and two ledger-generator references. Thus historical documents cannot be blanket-classified as unconsumed or deleted. Canonical ledgers/process documents remain authoritative campaign inputs; format-reference and source-comment dependencies need an explicit maintained-document decision before any publication exclusion. BR-0002 owns upstream allowlisting/reviewability; this campaign preserves local evidence. Scoped pattern scan found zero candidates, but is not the required complete-history secret investigation GQI-0001

## Batch reconciliation

Asset/import/DXA/metadata histories. Reviewed all title/status/checklist projections and fully read the DXA parallel-speed survey. Its21 unstarted rows are staged performance proposals with estimates, not benchmark evidence or accepted safety-free parallel work. Preserve serial ZIP ownership and correctness constraints. Two-pack container, PIG info and missing runtime checks are historical feature/validation proposals; do not turn them into cleanup fixes merely because they remain unchecked. Existing source reviews own import limits, variant selection, metadata, extraction, proprietary corpus and DXA transaction/provenance risks

Batch totals: 40 paths, 234284 frozen bytes, 4645 lines, 36 literal unchecked markers and 33 current changed/missing paths. Changed live planning prose and formatter drift remain explicitly inventoried for final live-delta reconciliation; no frozen result is substituted for that required gate

## Diff-minimization assessment

RETAIN: Retain local historical planning records; reconcile publication scope with BR-0002 instead of duplicating product owners. This is a mechanical historical-document batch. Planning prose does not execute engine policy and does not justify moving or broadly deduplicating inherited D1/D2 behavior. The source-review queue owns concrete product reductions. No inherited reduction credit and no local planning-file deletion

## Scope and method

Every complete frozen blob was decoded as UTF-8 and fingerprinted; complete available current bytes were compared separately. Mechanically parsed headings, checklist markers, code fences, URL hosts and scoped private-key/token patterns. Title/status/checklist projections for every assigned path were inspected. This is document provenance/content classification, not a claim that every prose line was manually reread or that historical commands were executed. Checkmarks and result claims remain dated claims until independently validated at the product owner

ACTUAL frozen git grep with all1361 historical basenames, excluding the plan tree, returned seven outside references: pkg_reader format comment, paired joy.c key-map comments, two outstanding_bugs pointers and two ledger-generator references. Thus historical documents cannot be blanket-classified as unconsumed or deleted. Canonical ledgers/process documents remain authoritative campaign inputs; format-reference and source-comment dependencies need an explicit maintained-document decision before any publication exclusion. BR-0002 owns upstream allowlisting/reviewability; this campaign preserves local evidence. Scoped pattern scan found zero candidates, but is not the required complete-history secret investigation GQI-0001

## Batch reconciliation

Music and installer format/extraction histories. Fully read frozen PKG_PARSER_PLAN.md, which is referenced by pkg_reader.c: it explains XAR/gzip/cpio streaming and API ownership, so any upstream exclusion requires a maintained format-reference replacement rather than blind deletion. Existing source surveys own bounds, budgets, catalog integrity, output containment and file-extension policy. Old unified-music phase6 migration prose is superseded by current disposable prerelease format instructions; do not create compatibility readers from that historical proposal. ISO/device, Mac-media and TV smoke checkboxes remain validation claims/gaps, not independently rerun results

Batch totals: 40 paths, 228011 frozen bytes, 4542 lines, 23 literal unchecked markers and 24 current changed/missing paths. Changed live planning prose and formatter drift remain explicitly inventoried for final live-delta reconciliation; no frozen result is substituted for that required gate

Every complete frozen blob was decoded as UTF-8 and fingerprinted; complete available current bytes were compared separately. Mechanically parsed headings, checklist markers, code fences, URL hosts and scoped private-key/token patterns. Title/status/checklist projections for every assigned path were inspected. This is document provenance/content classification, not a claim that every prose line was manually reread or that historical commands were executed. Checkmarks and result claims remain dated claims until independently validated at the product owner

ACTUAL frozen git grep with all1361 historical basenames, excluding the plan tree, returned seven outside references: pkg_reader format comment, paired joy.c key-map comments, two outstanding_bugs pointers and two ledger-generator references. Thus historical documents cannot be blanket-classified as unconsumed or deleted. Canonical ledgers/process documents remain authoritative campaign inputs; format-reference and source-comment dependencies need an explicit maintained-document decision before any publication exclusion. BR-0002 owns upstream allowlisting/reviewability; this campaign preserves local evidence. Scoped pattern scan found zero candidates, but is not the required complete-history secret investigation GQI-0001

## Batch reconciliation

Diff-minimization and tooling/BR histories. Fully read frozen May14 code/test cleanup, CRLF normalization and Aug11 chunked DMR round plans. Current .gitattributes already places *.bat after the generic LF rule, so that unchecked historical fix is stale. Do not execute its git add --renormalize proposal against the mixed foreign worktree. Producer-owned stable JSON is the current instruction; broad post-run normalization cannot substitute for it. DMR round closure rules agree with final path accounting and platform validation, while old EGL/kconfig smoke gaps stay explicit. Source reviews, not plan checkmarks, own logging hot paths, test discovery, native headers and parser boundaries

Batch totals: 40 paths, 83036 frozen bytes, 1400 lines, 12 literal unchecked markers and 16 current changed/missing paths. Changed live planning prose and formatter drift remain explicitly inventoried for final live-delta reconciliation; no frozen result is substituted for that required gate

## Diff-minimization assessment

RETAIN: Retain local historical planning records; reconcile publication scope with BR-0002 instead of duplicating product owners. This is a mechanical historical-document batch. Planning prose does not execute engine policy and does not justify moving or broadly deduplicating inherited D1/D2 behavior. The source-review queue owns concrete product reductions. No inherited reduction credit and no local planning-file deletion

## Scope and method

Every complete frozen blob was decoded as UTF-8 and fingerprinted; complete available current bytes were compared separately. Mechanically parsed headings, checklist markers, code fences, URL hosts and scoped private-key/token patterns. Title/status/checklist projections for every assigned path were inspected. This is document provenance/content classification, not a claim that every prose line was manually reread or that historical commands were executed. Checkmarks and result claims remain dated claims until independently validated at the product owner

ACTUAL frozen git grep with all1361 historical basenames, excluding the plan tree, returned seven outside references: pkg_reader format comment, paired joy.c key-map comments, two outstanding_bugs pointers and two ledger-generator references. Thus historical documents cannot be blanket-classified as unconsumed or deleted. Canonical ledgers/process documents remain authoritative campaign inputs; format-reference and source-comment dependencies need an explicit maintained-document decision before any publication exclusion. BR-0002 owns upstream allowlisting/reviewability; this campaign preserves local evidence. Scoped pattern scan found zero candidates, but is not the required complete-history secret investigation GQI-0001

## Batch reconciliation

Further touch-control histories and palette/texture diagnostic retrospective. Fully read203-line frozen coop texture retrospective, recovering the output-truncated fixed-log opening. It distinguishes D2 late palette invalidation evidence from merely symmetric D1 hazard prevention, centralizes optional Android visual policy while retaining mission-required data, and later records removal of forensic/target-specific overrides with generic tap diagnostics retained. Intermediate partial labels are superseded by later continuation/reduction notes. No historical GPU hash/log is a new current runtime measurement, and no broad logging purge or speculative palette/cache fix follows from old target-specific investigations. Existing source/graphics owners retain actual cache lifetime, concurrency, rendering and instrumentation acceptance

Batch totals: 40 paths, 168214 frozen bytes, 2579 lines, 7 literal unchecked markers and 33 current changed/missing paths. Changed live planning prose and formatter drift remain explicitly inventoried for final live-delta reconciliation; no frozen result is substituted for that required gate

## Diff-minimization assessment

RETAIN: Retain local historical planning records; reconcile publication scope with BR-0002 instead of duplicating product owners. This is a mechanical historical-document batch. Planning prose does not execute engine policy and does not justify moving or broadly deduplicating inherited D1/D2 behavior. The source-review queue owns concrete product reductions. No inherited reduction credit and no local planning-file deletion

## Scope and method

Every complete frozen blob was decoded as UTF-8 and fingerprinted; complete available current bytes were compared separately. Mechanically parsed headings, checklist markers, code fences, URL hosts and scoped private-key/token patterns. Title/status/checklist projections for every assigned path were inspected. This is document provenance/content classification, not a claim that every prose line was manually reread or that historical commands were executed. Checkmarks and result claims remain dated claims until independently validated at the product owner

ACTUAL frozen git grep with all1361 historical basenames, excluding the plan tree, returned seven outside references: pkg_reader format comment, paired joy.c key-map comments, two outstanding_bugs pointers and two ledger-generator references. Thus historical documents cannot be blanket-classified as unconsumed or deleted. Canonical ledgers/process documents remain authoritative campaign inputs; format-reference and source-comment dependencies need an explicit maintained-document decision before any publication exclusion. BR-0002 owns upstream allowlisting/reviewability; this campaign preserves local evidence. Scoped pattern scan found zero candidates, but is not the required complete-history secret investigation GQI-0001

## Batch reconciliation

Gameplay compatibility/cache and renderer performance histories. Fully read233-line Original Homing plan and88-line route-cache audit, recovering truncated ranges. Retail/source/thread interpretations and old trajectory/test results are historical attribution, not freshly verified external facts. Smart-child repetition remains an explicit Original-mode feature follow-up with RNG consumption and paired deterministic-test requirements; it is not automatically admitted as a cleanup defect. Existing BR-0386 owns recording/replay algorithm parity. Cache proposal versionCode identity and mutable state hashes are superseded by current generation/profile/topology design reviewed in0706/0707; do not restore the obsolete key or add compatibility readers. Persistent canonical route versus transient live guidance ownership remains appropriate, with actual BR-0332 and cache-generation lifecycle acceptance still open. Old adaptive-recorder estimates and warm-route timings are not current performance measurements

Batch totals: 40 paths, 206851 frozen bytes, 3731 lines, 3 literal unchecked markers and 22 current changed/missing paths. Changed live planning prose and formatter drift remain explicitly inventoried for final live-delta reconciliation; no frozen result is substituted for that required gate

## Diff-minimization assessment

RETAIN: Retain local historical planning records; reconcile publication scope with BR-0002 instead of duplicating product owners. This is a mechanical historical-document batch. Planning prose does not execute engine policy and does not justify moving or broadly deduplicating inherited D1/D2 behavior. The source-review queue owns concrete product reductions. No inherited reduction credit and no local planning-file deletion

## Scope and method

Every complete frozen blob was decoded as UTF-8 and fingerprinted; complete available current bytes were compared separately. Mechanically parsed headings, checklist markers, code fences, URL hosts and scoped private-key/token patterns. Title/status/checklist projections for every assigned path were inspected. This is document provenance/content classification, not a claim that every prose line was manually reread or that historical commands were executed. Checkmarks and result claims remain dated claims until independently validated at the product owner

ACTUAL frozen git grep with all1361 historical basenames, excluding the plan tree, returned seven outside references: pkg_reader format comment, paired joy.c key-map comments, two outstanding_bugs pointers and two ledger-generator references. Thus historical documents cannot be blanket-classified as unconsumed or deleted. Canonical ledgers/process documents remain authoritative campaign inputs; format-reference and source-comment dependencies need an explicit maintained-document decision before any publication exclusion. BR-0002 owns upstream allowlisting/reviewability; this campaign preserves local evidence. Scoped pattern scan found zero candidates, but is not the required complete-history secret investigation GQI-0001

## Batch reconciliation

Codec, checkpoint and recorder/replay phases plus dated desync notes. Fully read22-line codec dependency-swap plan; current input_demo_codec.cpp includes base64.h/picosha2.h and consumes the shared dependency APIs, so its five unchecked proposal rows cannot prove the swap is absent. No new dependency-pin or build verification credit. Existing source reviews own codec bounds, malformed payloads, checkpoint allocation and recorder result truthfulness. Manual device recording, forcefield/checkpoint and non-headless render hypotheses remain dated gaps; route/save/input serialization layouts remain native-owned and current disposable Android-format instructions supersede obsolete compatibility proposals

Batch totals: 40 paths, 202505 frozen bytes, 3126 lines, 8 literal unchecked markers and 30 current changed/missing paths. Changed live planning prose and formatter drift remain explicitly inventoried for final live-delta reconciliation; no frozen result is substituted for that required gate

## Diff-minimization assessment

RETAIN: Retain local historical planning records; reconcile publication scope with BR-0002 instead of duplicating product owners. This is a mechanical historical-document batch. Planning prose does not execute engine policy and does not justify moving or broadly deduplicating inherited D1/D2 behavior. The source-review queue owns concrete product reductions. No inherited reduction credit and no local planning-file deletion

## Scope and method

Every complete frozen blob was decoded as UTF-8 and fingerprinted; complete available current bytes were compared separately. Mechanically parsed headings, checklist markers, code fences, URL hosts and scoped private-key/token patterns. Title/status/checklist projections for every assigned path were inspected. This is document provenance/content classification, not a claim that every prose line was manually reread or that historical commands were executed. Checkmarks and result claims remain dated claims until independently validated at the product owner

ACTUAL frozen git grep with all1361 historical basenames, excluding the plan tree, returned seven outside references: pkg_reader format comment, paired joy.c key-map comments, two outstanding_bugs pointers and two ledger-generator references. Thus historical documents cannot be blanket-classified as unconsumed or deleted. Canonical ledgers/process documents remain authoritative campaign inputs; format-reference and source-comment dependencies need an explicit maintained-document decision before any publication exclusion. BR-0002 owns upstream allowlisting/reviewability; this campaign preserves local evidence. Scoped pattern scan found zero candidates, but is not the required complete-history secret investigation GQI-0001

## Batch reconciliation

Launcher controller/admin-tray, preference/autoselect and metadata-preview histories. Fully read75-line gamepad-admin completion and57-line autoselect refactor. Pilot weapon ordering stays canonical in playsave/weapon/text owners, with Kotlin consuming native APIs rather than copying binary offsets; a prose650-to250 estimate is not new inherited-diff reduction credit. Old hardcoded admin indexes, Start/Select overrides and polling proposal do not authorize restoring aliases or overriding current September controller/profile work. Mouse tuning, Play update-check proposal, autoselect test commands and bounded lint timeout remain historical gaps, without live device/JVM/build credit

Batch totals: 40 paths, 147816 frozen bytes, 2399 lines, 11 literal unchecked markers and 32 current changed/missing paths. Changed live planning prose and formatter drift remain explicitly inventoried for final live-delta reconciliation; no frozen result is substituted for that required gate

## Diff-minimization assessment

RETAIN: game-owned mutations, render-owned synth tuning and published UI projections have distinct owners. Preserve shared Android implementations and small paired game hooks; do not broadly deduplicate original engine code or replace newer foreign graphics/controller work. One generic queue alone would not fix audio-render ownership or cross-process pilot transactions

## Current reconciliation

Full active BR-0029 was read against current ranges. Music now uses a mutex-protected64-entry queue containing complete command records; rejected capacity is exposed through JNI return values. Engine apply handles source, track, play order, volume, pause and persistence, then publishes a mutex-protected snapshot. Paired D1/D2 game draw and idle hooks call it. This supersedes the obsolete volatile source/type/preference tuple and UI-side songs teardown claim for these paths. No per-command sequence/completion or lifecycle admission was established; BR-0244 delivery and source publication acceptance remain coordinated

Both SDL event loops call android_overlay_game_tick. Weapon, marker, network, coop, teammate, video and warp getters copy synchronized published arrays; warp mutations are requested atomically and executed in the game tick. Bomb publication uses a side-effect-free choice rather than which_bomb. Player and secondary-ammo bounds are checked at publication; the dedicated BR-0080 recheck will reconcile bounds acceptance. Do not reapply old UI traversal of these now-published arrays

Gain/voice setters submit render tuning commands, with finite gain admission and bounded voice count. The render thread drains commands before rendering; no active render applies configuration snapshots without mutating the synth. Guidebot default, persistent-message preference and diagnostic visibility use atomics in their implementations. These are actual repairs, not evidence that every UI-to-native call is still unsynchronized

Residual BR-0029 paths remain concrete: escort owner/player/callsign and buddy-released getters directly inspect engine state and companion identity, and MainActivity installs them as touch providers. Active routing reads live mode/network state. Debug JNI still writes renderer/debug globals, including merely volatile gfx/aniso/MSAA paths. Gamma getter reads live palette state; graphics JNI retains direct fallback to android_graphics_set_option, whose gamma branch mutates palette/config and persists. New graphics safety queue is mutex-protected and must be preserved; do not replace it wholesale while finishing options outside its inventory and the existing snapshot contract

Music snapshot first-publication null allocation remains the already admitted GQF-0233/GQR-0218: fallback malloc may fail before unconditional strlen. Track list caching only keys type and total, so same-count replacement still needs the previously recorded producer-generation trace in final live review. Complete file hashes below are provenance; only listed ranges were freshly reviewed in large units

## Validation and limits

Static current source/caller tracing only. No native build, sanitizer, device stress or thread assertion suite ran. Acceptance must cover repeated overlay polling through level/player/song replacement, command admission and completion, render teardown, allocation failures, unchanged query-only weapon preferences and coherent settings at frame boundaries. Existing cross-process pilot/input/IME additions in broad BR-0029 remain governed by their completed source surveys and later sweeps; this focused recheck does not claim their terminal closure. Final live delta and all remediation remain pending

## Diff-minimization assessment

RETAIN: repeated optional overlay delivery belongs in android_jni_overlay, with conversion in existing jni_string/utf8_codec. Keyboard input has additional requested-state semantics; sharing attachment/reference cleanup is reasonable only with explicit callback failure policy. Do not replace original engine text policy or create Kotlin/native parallel converters

## Current reconciliation

Full active BR-0044 and archived BR-0065 were read. Complete current overlay helper/header and shared JNI conversion implementation were reviewed, plus exact keyboard/caller/startup ranges below. The overlay helper now checks JNI_EDETACHED separately, checks attachment return, rejects bad GetEnv status, initializes references, checks class/method/string presence, clears an exception for optional delivery, deletes both local refs and detaches only on successful attachment. The original repeated track/level/rewind class-reference leak is repaired in this helper and must not be blindly reapplied

Remaining BR-0044 callback boundary: no entry check prevents new JNI operations with a preexisting pending exception, and the final best-effort clear cannot distinguish an incoming required-operation exception from one caused by this callback. Each JNI step needs its explicit failure/cleanup contract. Raw NewStringUTF still consumes native overlay text; the shared strict UTF-16 converter exists and should be used with checked optional-failure behavior. Coordinate this exact regrowth with GQF-0037 rather than reopen archived BR-0065's entire previously repaired import/startup corpus

Keyboard show/hide still assume AttachCurrentThread succeeds, leak the Activity class local ref in the long native game invocation, perform unchecked class/method/string/callback operations and leave exceptions pending. Show sets requested state before callback success; hide resets native state regardless of failed Java delivery. Kotlin methods enqueue UI work, so JNI-call success means admitted delivery, not observed IME visibility. Repair native requested-state policy coherently with existing lifecycle/IME ownership rather than treating asynchronous UI execution as synchronous success

Host migration still obtains an undeleted class and calls method lookup without class/exception checks. Dormancy notification deletes its class and checks attachment but leaves callback exceptions pending. Skip-intro preference callback also lacks cleanup/failure handling; its per-JNI-return class is not the same unbounded long-call accumulation schedule. Startup helper references were inspected to distinguish finite setup references from repeated callbacks; this report does not infer that every undeleted setup local overflows during one launch

## Validation and limits

Read complete existing exception-safety and strict-UTF Python contract tests. They check selected source text for import, preview, reconnect, startup, SAF and MIDI conversion; neither exercises optional overlay/keyboard callbacks or JNI failures. They were not run in this recheck and are not CheckJNI/race evidence. Required acceptance remains thousands of callbacks in one game invocation plus attachment, lookup, allocation, malformed/non-BMP text and Java callback failure, preservation of incoming exceptions, bounded refs, correct detach and deterministic keyboard admission. No build/device/instrumented JNI test ran. Final current delta and remediation remain open

nativeGetTeammateStatus now copies a mutex-protected snapshot. The producer validates the local Player_num before local weapon/coop indexing and checks each secondary weapon before indexing ammo. Invalid secondary selection leaves zero ammo in the zeroed projection; UI label uses getOrElse and displays question mark. Safe memory access is implemented; explicit unavailable sentinel and active-slot semantics still need acceptance. WeaponState parses a bounded array with guarded optional fields. Keep independent producer bounds even after packet validation

Transport-origin gap within the same root: net_udp_process_mdata computes authenticated_sender from socket address, and the host forwards the original datagram to peers before local dispatch. A non-Retro client accepts only the master socket, hence receives authenticated_sender=host for a peer-origin ship-status payload. Both decoders reject every nonnegative sender not equal to buf[1], with no authorized-host relay exception or carried original identity in the inspected dispatch. The world stamp scopes world state, not original player identity. This can discard legitimate remote status on client/observer routes while direct Retro packets take another path. Reconcile exact origin and relay policy without weakening direct-peer authentication or trusting arbitrary inner bytes

Decoder admission checks MAX_PLAYERS but not active N_players/connection membership. Recovery validates array/life/serial only when active and otherwise returns true. Local wrappers intentionally use sender-1; they must not become a network bypass. Preserve existing bounds and frozen-world barriers while covering direct, host-relayed, local and observer policies explicitly

## Current reconciliation

Full active BR-0090 read. The old main-source PlayGamesAuth path is absent; complete current flavor implementations and ClientIdentity were read. directInstall deliberately has no Play configuration/code. playServices checks its configured ID and GITHUB_RELEASE, initializes SDK and requests a server code asynchronously. Matchmaking captures the connection and uses withConnection before publishing authentication. These later repairs are retained, not overwritten by the frozen source design

When unconfigured, unavailable or timed out, sendAuthenticate still sends a dev token instead of keypair proof. The token is UUID.randomUUID per app process, not a durable account. ClientIdentity uses checked committed preferences for a durable UUID, but has no public/private cryptographic key. AuthenticateMsg lacks public_key/auth_timestamp/auth_signature; its PowChallenge model exists but handler only logs that PoW is unimplemented. No client solution message or bounded cancellable solver was established by source search. Thus direct release clients cannot complete the server's configured production authentication without Play Games

Current server Authenticate explicitly accepts keypair public key, timestamp and signature. It checks timestamp within120seconds and verifies Ed25519 over callsign:timestamp. Known registered keys complete authentication; new keys get a challenge and connection-local pending registration. PowSolution checks that challenge, SHA256 of challenge string plus solution string against leading zero bits, then registers the key and clears pending state. protocol.rs defines corresponding optional fields and POW_SOLUTION. This is an existing protocol the client has not implemented, not authorization to invent a competing wire format

pow.rs was fully read, including low-difficulty and Ed25519 roundtrip source tests; none ran here. Exact server authentication range was read, not the complete websocket file or all server security policy. Repeated authentication/pending-state admission and fail-closed development configuration belong to their subsequent existing rechecks. Do not treat this fallback work as closure of those owners

It also runs total_unique_players and total_games_played synchronous SQLite COUNTs under the shared DB mutex, converting errors into0

ServerState has no bounded/cached status snapshot; configuration max_connections applies to websocket sessions, not public HTTP admission. This establishes missing explicit application budgets, not a claim that every underlying HTTP library default is limitless. Simple status uses only atomic counters and health reads counters/map length, preserving cheap alternatives. Health's unconditional ok despite listener failure belongs to BR-0128 supervision, not solved by making status cheaper

Current harness bypasses production runner and starts axum directly on ephemeral ports. Reviewed tests check one empty/small response, protocol/count shape, simple integer and uptime. They neither populate maximum lobby metadata nor stress bursts/concurrency/slow readers/headers or concurrent DB/WS operations. No complete integration-file coverage or measured amplification is claimed

No Cargo/build, HTTP load, memory/socket or slow-client test ran. Finish bounded normalized status snapshot/cadence with compact/pageable metadata and cached asynchronous aggregates, explicit per-effective-client/global HTTP admission and read/write deadlines, and response-size policy. Validate max population, bursts, keepalive, slow headers/readers, aborted requests, direct/proxy IPv4/IPv6 and simultaneous DB/matchmaking work, requiring bounded resources and responsive legitimate probes. Full BR-0127, complete state/atomic stats and exact current admission/auth/cleanup/harness/reconnect paths reviewed. max_connections checks sessions.len before upgrade; sessions contains authenticated players only. Authenticate and PowSolution remain top-level dispatch after player_id is set. Authentication is not terminal: same/different identity can replace connection-local player_id, while pending_pow can be replaced or survive another path. complete_auth blindly sessions.insert(pid), increments online and STUN reference count on every success, without closing/rejecting old generation or transferring owned lobby state. Old sockets continue dispatch using pid and can mutate current registry state

Disconnect looks up current pid's lobby then removes sessions by pid, decrements online and effective TCP-IP STUN count without proving ownership. It can delete a newer session/lobby state. Separate STUN check/remove/decrement operations also race. Atomic counters do not make these multi-resource ownership changes atomic or exactly once. Current drop(tx) and await send_task with bounded queue/send timeout improves send teardown but cannot fix stale registry references or account switching

## Cross-cutting JNI boundary sweep

Fresh attach/acquisition/encoding inventory across current native owners, full strict codec and overlay helper reads, selected current array/keyboard/crash/startup/cooperative save bridges. The completed numbered surveys and 50 rechecks remain detailed evidence for other bridge owners. This sweep adds linkage and current ownership reconciliation; it does not award whole-file coverage for the 1210-line current resume bridge, large native input/introspection/automation sources or outstanding tail/live-delta work

## Retain corrected boundaries

Shared jni_string.c explicitly converts UTF-16 to strict null-free standard UTF-8 with checked capacity, acquired character release, first-exception preservation when throwing, and NewString UTF-16 output. Existing SAF/MIDI repair remains valid within its tested scope. Preview generation, staged native configuration, bounded reconnect verification and repaired JNI owners are retained. Avoid another codec or blanket weakening of completed validation

Overlay helper correctly distinguishes JNI_EDETACHED, checks attach, tracks detach ownership and releases class/string locals. It still uses NewStringUTF for ordinary native text and unconditionally clears exceptions, while borrowing unsynchronized global Activity. BR-0044/BR-0029 already own these remaining contract/lifecycle issues. The later graphics callback additions use this same helper and inherit its lifetime/encoding boundary

## Remaining acquisition and publication defects

nativeJoystickAxes bounds batch cardinality and validates matching array lengths, but acquires all three arrays before checking the first failure. A pending exception from one acquisition therefore does not stop subsequent JNI calls. Release-on-partial-failure exists and must be retained, while transactional acquisition and publication belong to GQR-0170. Native float conversion also lacks local finite/range admission; existing input boundary review remains applicable rather than inventing an unrelated float policy here

Keyboard show/hide call AttachCurrentThread without checking success, then dereference env, acquire classes without null/exception gates, leak class locals and use Modified UTF-8 for initial text. BR-0044 owns attachment/reference/encoding cleanup. Show sets keyboard state before callback admission; failure must not leave misleading requested state

Crash installation obtains directory then header without short-circuiting a pending exception, and getters use NewStringUTF for native diagnostics. GQR-0167 owns strict conversion, bounded scalar-safe diagnostics and acquisition cleanup. No new crash shim or alternate codec is needed

Current CoopSaveCompatibility_nativeSlotPath and nativeCompatibilityStatus at the top of jni_resume_save.cpp use unchecked GetStringUTFChars, an unguarded second acquisition, native std::string allocation across JNI and NewStringUTF output. These additions are outside the older repaired eight-owner set. Extend GQR-0170 to these actual current entry points: use strict strings, stop at first exception, scope all acquisitions/file handles, contain native allocation failures, and publish only after successful path/format validation. Preserve engine-owned save compatibility logic and paired version minima; do not duplicate save-body knowledge in Kotlin

jni_main publishes g_activity before graphics storage initialization; startup_failed resets engine to IDLE without deleting or withdrawing that global reference. Existing startup/lifecycle recheck owns this remaining leak/publication gap. Process exit on normal/fatal engine shutdown is intentional existing policy, but startup failure is retryable and needs its own cleanup. The checked fatal attach/strict string improvement is retained; do not equate process-exit cleanup with normal scoped callback ownership

native-lib.cpp still contains a duplicate helloFromNative skeleton, while maintained definition is in jni_main.c and CMake inventory has no native-lib registration. GQR-0163 can remove the orphan after confirming both target linkage; no forwarding wrapper

## Required validation

No JNI/device/build test executed. Production partial-acquisition and allocator faults must preserve the first exception, release every prior resource and prevent partial state publication. CheckJNI covers null, malformed/embedded-NUL/supplementary Unicode, detached callback threads, recreation/startup failure and retry. Shared native producer exception containment remains GQR-0173. Complete Android ABI and paired native builds are acceptance gates. No duplicate finding was added; remaining frozen tails and full current delta still require review

## Lifecycle sweep method

Link current Activity/launcher launch, suspend/resume/destroy, cancellable file-work ownership, transient handoff and SAF permission boundaries to the completed numbered surveys and remaining remediation owners. Fresh exact selected spans are recorded above. No claim of complete semantic reread of the very large Activities, full import workflow or current controller/graphics deltas. Selected permission/launch files are complete where spans reach EOF; all final tail/live-delta gates remain

## Current guards and retained improvements

SetupActivity launch captures owner identity, checks it after preparation, rechecks network attempt on main before startActivity and rejects finishing/destroyed state. onDestroy stops route coordinator, cancels route scope, removes refresh/launch-timeout callbacks and unregisters owned receivers. onPause stops route precompute and clears controller diagnostics. Preserve these admission and cancellation gates

LaunchPreparationWork runs blocking work on IO under a shared writer Mutex, uses runInterruptible and cancels the child on caller timeout. Its explicit process-owned scope keeps file ownership until a non-cooperative writer returns; timeout alone is not authority to start a concurrent writer. Do not replace this with a helper that unlocks while native I/O still writes

MainActivity onStop suspends UI polling, gyro and route-facing state, releases controller keys and axis meta keys, releases initialized InputMixer and cancels/reset touch overlay before native background pause. onResume restores only suspended UI work and refreshes preferences. onDestroy cancels startup scope/route job, closes audio PFDs, disconnects runtime/service and unregisters debug receivers. These later changes narrow some old lifecycle evidence; BR-0202 still needs actual paired menu/listbox focus-loss and direct/mixer release integration, not assumptions based on an older tracker.clear implementation

surfaceCreated marks gameStarted before awaiting playlist preparation, then launches a raw native-start thread. surfaceDestroyed withdraws native surface. startupScope cancellation on destroy prevents a suspended await resuming, but the already-started native thread has independent lifetime. Coordinate native start state and global Activity publication under BR-0078/BR-0044; do not claim cancelling a Coroutine owns the engine thread or that this source inventory proves a crash. A slow playlist/surface stop/start/recreation case remains a required integration boundary

## Remaining current owners

Setup produceState still synchronously calls ResumeSaveBridge.findOptions and repeats up to20 times with500ms delay when empty. Delay is suspending, but native root walks before each delay execute on the Compose producer context. GQR-0084 remains current and also owns cooperative card discovery. Move bounded discovery to cancellable IO snapshots keyed to current game/storage/generation without dropping save admission checks

PendingResumeLaunch still uses one fixed .tmp, unsynced rename/direct-write fallback and swallowed publication errors. Token comparison, stale check and later pathname deletion are separate operations; an older consumer can remove a newer generation. GQR-0216 remains current across launcher and game processes. AtomicFile/process-local Mutex alone cannot make compare-and-consume safe across processes; launch admission must observe publication failure. Disposable launcher schema may be replaced directly

Service delayed expiry inventory still posts forceBackgroundShutdown without a captured game generation; detailed GQR-0209 source/barrier evidence remains applicable. Replacement game and retained LAN lease must survive old-session grace cleanup

## Permissions and touch operation

SafUriPermissions acquires exact or owning-tree read permission, scopes access probes with use, deduplicates explicit releases and avoids releasing permissions still covered by retained tracked URIs. ImportLocationManager uses app-private external paths without runtime permissions; this is separate from SAF grants. Preserve managed-copy import and the explicit BIN-URI selection contract. The current import chooser offers direct file and folder actions with ordinary clickable buttons, and TV focus is additive. No source basis here for requiring a controller to operate the chooser. Revocation/provider disappearance and restored-picker results remain actual import integration cases, not permission success inferred from the helper alone

## Acceptance

No Activity, JVM, device or build test executed in this sweep. Required actual integration includes background release before/after long-hold, surface loss/recreation during preparation, slow/empty/large resume roots and stale completion, cross-process handoff failure/replacement, expired-game replacement and retained LAN lease, revoked SAF access and touch-only launch/import. Current graphics/controller edits are external concurrent work and remain preserved. No duplicate finding or blanket lifecycle clean bill was added

## Files/data cross-cutting sweep

Reconcile completed per-parser/import/save surveys and current rechecks with shared budgets, portable output projection, atomic publication and actual save-slot adapters. Exact fresh spans identify source read; complete hash is state identity only. This sweep is not complete reread of all parser/launcher code, 54 outstanding frozen tails or the final full current delta

## Retain established extraction ownership

ArchiveFiles ZIP enumeration registers each entry in ExtractionBudget before list materialization, closes archive on admission error and keeps handles owned by the readable archive. SevenZ builder applies decoder memory limit. Output projections normalize relative components, reject escaping parent sequences/empty outputs and preflight NFC/case-folded file/file and file/directory collisions. Mission plan includes generated descent.sng in collision admission. Actual extraction registers declared and actual byte budgets and scopes input/output streams. Canonical descendant check uses a separator; do not reduce it to bare prefix matching

Do not treat collision normalization as physical no-follow containment or a complete cross-platform filename policy. Some invalid projected outputs are skipped by the actual canonical descendant gate rather than reported. Detailed existing mission/extractor owners retain truthful publication/completeness requirements. Completed native ISO physical containment, complete CD attempt, Inno/STi2 memory/work limits, direct Setup ZIP accounting, RAR terminal policy and process supervision remain repaired within their exact scopes

Mission extraction still deletes/recreates stageRoot and publishes ordinary output files sequentially; outer store/cache transaction and final registry remain BR-0103 and its current reconciliation. Preserve managed-copy publication and source before/after verification; final crash/restart and payload/manifest generation consistency still require actual fault cases. Generated aliases must be charged in complete reservation/progress, not only registered at the late copy

## Current config and storage admission

ConfigImportLoader retains1MiB byte cap, strict UTF-8 decoder, tree/cardinality/slot limits and IO worker. validateLexicalLimits recognizes only double-quoted strings and does not reject negative/unbalanced depth before the permissive JSONObject parser recursively materializes input. GQR-0210 remains: accepted grammar and lexical resource gate must be one strict contract before tree creation, preserving disposable format policy and valid quoted values

ImportStorageGuard adds50MiB headroom without checked addition and sums positive archive declarations without overflow admission. GQR-0183 remains current; impossible lengths may wrap reservation. Zero available bytes deliberately allows transactional writer when measurement unsupported; do not change this into guaranteed failure merely because StatFs is unavailable. Checked arithmetic must distinguish unknown/negative declarations, positive overflow and real valid boundary sizes

## Durable publication and recovery

AtomicFilePublication uses unique siblings, synced payload writes and a process-local transaction lock. writeBytesBatch snapshots originals, then publishes targets. A rollback replaceLocked failure aborts restoration of earlier entries and finally deletes every backup, including recoverable originals. Current publishFiles retains backups on failed restoration, but configuration still uses the separate writeBytesBatch path. Existing GQF-0141/GQR-0128 explicitly covers this branch from earlier source evidence; no duplicate root. Cleanup must remain generation-owned until rollback or explicit durable recovery is proven

Native android_file_pair_publish retains prior primary/companion in backups and stages companion before primary. It refuses preexisting backups but ignores backup deletion and rollback rename/delete outcomes. State production uses deterministic .bak/.tmp paths. Single-file publication first deletes deterministic backup and ignores restore result. GQI-0006 remains an investigation requiring interruption after each rename and restart/retry/cleanup-failure matrix; current source proves incomplete recovery contract, not irreversible loss in every failure. Preserve backups while establishing admitted same-generation save/companion/manifest selection

Engine source remains canonical for save slot/path/scope/version/body knowledge. android_save_set sanitizes mission/pilot components and bounds slots; launcher should call native contracts rather than duplicate layouts. Sanitization is lossy and mission hash is applied only after overlength sanitized names; existing GQF-0096 mission identity owner remains. BR-0082 still owns complete save-body admission; trailer metadata alone is not proof that engine will load the body. BR-0417 and GQF-0098 own selected-set cleanup and conditional deletion generation, distinct from pair publication

## Validation gates

No import/save/native/JVM/device test executed in this sweep. Actual hostile paths, duplicate projections, declared/actual byte boundaries, source replacement, missing/invalid archive, every publication/rollback/sync fault, process interruption/restart and retry must preserve prior accepted generation and produce explicit failure. Native game compatibility stays preserved; Android launcher/config schemas may be replaced directly. Deployed server identity/moderation database is separate durable state. Complete final tail/live-delta audit remains open

## Production network sweep

Join current public router, supervisor, authenticated registry, outbound writer, external identity flow, relay protocol and actual Android consumers. Fresh source spans and symbol inventories supplement the complete targeted server/client rechecks0009/0014..0039, which contain config/DB/auth/pair allocation/terminal path detail and pinned-library contracts. Not a blanket reread of every source/fixture or final current-delta coverage

## Startup, admission and terminal ownership

Production main logs required HTTP/admin/relay/STUN task errors inside detached tasks and continues serving other endpoints. WS failure is logged but main returns success after aborting handles. public health is router availability, not proof required components bound. Test build_state and direct ws_handler/http_api startup are not production main supervision coverage. BR-0128 owns first-failure signaling, awaited cleanup and nonzero status. BR-0106 startup config/credential gates and GQR-0204 deployment JSONC publication must precede service admission

Upgrade cap counts only authenticated sessions and uses non-atomic check; preauth sockets are uncounted. Reauthentication can replace identity-keyed sessions, while disconnect owns only player ID. BR-0127 owns connection reservation plus exact generation compare/remove. Per-IP connection throttle exists but trusted-proxy identity is not established, so nginx loopback collapses clients under BR-0114. RateLimiter per-key action deques are bounded, but stale-key snapshot/remove race can erase newly refreshed state under BR-0118. record_auth_fail remains a declared API without production auth-failure admission under BR-0117

Bounded outbound channel256 and10s send deadline are retained local improvements. try_send failure is ignored by callers; writer termination does not cancel reader/session ownership. BR-0144 requires one terminal owner and truthful reliable/replaceable message policy, not merely increasing channel depth. Whole auth operation deadline and byte/work/concurrency budget are separate from120s read-idle reset; Google verification constructs an unbounded-default reqwest client and reads complete error bodies before slicing possibly inside UTF-8. BR-0125 owns both external phases and scalar-safe diagnostic limits

## Identity and protocol parity

Rust CURRENT_PROTOCOL/MIN_CLIENT_PROTOCOL and Android current protocol are2, retaining corrected parity. Authenticate checks lower bound only, admitting arbitrary future u32 values under BR-0119. Keypair proof still needs actual per-connection challenge bound to one canonical signed identity/callsign/auth transcript; repeated callsign/timestamp signatures do not establish freshness under BR-0143. Equivalent hex public keys must not accidentally fork deployed DB identity under BR-0113

Direct APK PlayGamesAuth returns no Play code, Play flavor is conditional Google auth, ClientIdentity is persistent installation UUID rather than cryptographic key, and MatchmakingService only logs PoW challenge as unimplemented. Existing BR-0090 remains actual non-Play authentication owner. Preserve Google path while adding exact server-compatible key/challenge flow; do not substitute UUID or disable server proof policy

DB moderation checks unwrap failure as false after some durable registration paths, friends workflow can mutate unauthorized/stale states and admin ban does not revoke live session. BR-0137/0121/0123 own deny/error/generation semantics. SQLite std Mutex and synchronous calls remain inside async workers under BR-0139; explicit bounded blocking owner should also make workflow transactions and cleanup consistent. BR-0140 durable retention and BR-0131 log byte/free-space reserve remain independent budgets. Android disposable-schema instruction does not authorize deleting deployed identities/moderation

## Relay and cross-map locks

Relay now receives up to65535 bytes, preserving large engine sync fix. Its five-byte header is shared token plus destination slot; sender is learned/rebound from endpoint using destination inference and session-wide IP set, with empty set permissive. Sparse actual game slots are not represented by expected_players=2 index range. Android deliverIncoming strips five bytes without token/source proof and shared unknown-sender mapping is not authenticated. BR-0132 owns actual pair/role/slot proof on both producers and consumers. Completed engine reconnect transcript/route-proof/rate-limit repairs must be retained but cannot authenticate a server relay frame by themselves

Capacity check/insert, repeated start, partial allocation and terminal release remain BR-0133. Absolute2hour created_at retention can reap active games and leave ended sessions consuming capacity until cleanup. Per-packet log and allocation rates remain unbudgeted. Existing initial allocation rollback improvement remains preserved

ConnectivityOk retains outer sessions.get(player_id) guard, takes lobby write guard, drops lobby and then calls sessions.get_mut(player_id) before outer guard ends. Thus current late-join path still has same-key read/write self-deadlock under pinned DashMap contract. Other session/lobby/broadcast order must be normalized across BR-0153 rather than fixing only one line. Copy owned IDs/projections before second-map operations and network/DB effects; do not hold guards across await or recursive broadcast

## Actual acceptance matrix

No server process, UDP socket, Android multiplayer test or build executed. server/tests symbol inventory shows direct test harness and UDP/STUN/NAT tests but no relay::run invocation; detailed existing recheck records distinguish synthetic token retention from actual relay proof. Required new integration executes production main with each listener conflict and shutdown, bounded stalled/failed identity phases, concurrent cap/re-auth/old disconnect, future-version and repeated challenge rejection, friends/ban DB faults, slow outbound reader/writer cancellation, actual relay forged endpoint/token/role/sparse-slot/rebind cases, terminal allocation release and late join under strict deadlines. Paired D1/D2 reconnect controls and configured Android flavors/ABIs remain required. Full current delta and unresolved tail gates stay open

## Concurrency and resources sweep method

Cross-domain ownership reconciliation from the complete numbered surveys, current rechecks and first five sweeps, with fresh input mailbox, native surface references/EGL exits, audio producer/consumer publication, music snapshot and JVM preview resource-owner reads. Exact fresh spans carry semantic coverage; symbol inventories or complete-file hashes do not grant missing tail/current-delta coverage

## Input and Activity ownership

Axis mailbox holds one mutex for coherent raw/touch/generation publication, uses one generation per producer batch, snapshots state, drains threshold transitions through snapshot generation, and acknowledges only the applied generation. Latest continuous state is bounded/coalesced, but button_transitions is an unbounded deque of threshold-region changes. flush intentionally does not discard releases or short pulses. Retain that correctness policy while resolving GQI-0005 by measuring actual supported consumer stalls; pending_axis_count does not measure retained transition storage. No arbitrary cap/drop policy is admitted without final-release/short-pulse order evidence

Native/JVM input and Activity callback ownership remains BR-0029/0044 plus GQR-0170. JNI strict conversion and early failure cleanup must not call into a pending exception or publish only part of an input vector. Coroutine cancellation and engine thread lifetime remain different owned resources; late completion must be bound to current Activity/game/surface generation

## Surface references and GL resources

nativeSetSurface derives one ANativeWindow reference, swaps window and generation under g_surface_mutex and releases the replaced reference. acquire_snapshot copies generation/pause and acquires the window while locked; release_snapshot releases once and clears the borrowed field. Native cleanup increments generation and releases held window. Preserve this corrected lifetime policy

EGL initialization uses acquired snapshot, releases it after surface creation and has snapshot_owned guard on error; swap releases on paused/no-surface/recreate-failure and normal result. Recreate binds current window generation; failed swap reports graphics safety failure. These local paths correctly retain the window while another thread withdraws/replaces it. They are not evidence that all GL objects survive a lost context or that shader startup succeeded: gles3_shim_init still has no checked success admission in examined caller under GQR-0174/BR-0251. Existing MSAA/texture/cache/context roots and concurrent graphics edits remain intact, with actual loss/retry allocation and render tests required

## Audio completion and snapshot atomicity

MIDI/HMP and PCM render helpers set g_source_finished before returning the produced frames. Render thread later calls pcm_ring_write. Audio callback sees finished plus an empty ring and sets g_playing=0/song_finished=1, allowing it to strand the final returned chunk. Existing GQF-0167/GQR-0154 remains current in fresh source. Publish final ring write before EOF in one producer order, retain explicit stop/replacement and loop behavior, and barrier-test MIDI/PCM exact tail bytes through actual callbacks

Render thread uses atomic running/playing/pause state and background condition-variable wait; existing command/tuning ownership improvement remains. Do not broadly replace these controls with volatile fields or rely on a test-only callback schedule. Stop/join and resource release must remain exactly-once for current source generation

Music getters hold g_music_snapshot_mutex while copying native data, then convert copied UTF-8 after unlock. Publisher stages tracks outside mutex but fallback malloc can fail; strlen(g_music_snapshot_tracks) remains unchecked while locked. Reallocation can also leave older inadequate capacity. GQF-0233/GQR-0218 owns complete snapshot failure/publication semantics. Mutex excludes concurrent writers but cannot make null allocation or inconsistent generation safe; preserve prior complete JSON or explicit failure and release every lock on faults

AudioPreviewResourceOwner replaces current before releasing old resource, ignores stale expected releases and clears current before owned release. Initialization failure releases the attempted current resource. Preserve these late-callback/exactly-once guards; actual dialog/MediaPlayer lifecycle needs caller integration, not a new overlapping owner

## Remaining lifetime families and acceptance

GQR-0172/0173 scope native JSON/acquired buffer lifetime through allocation/parse/dump faults; GQR-0176 bounds aggregate retained replay/recording/trace allocations, not just each leaf. GQR-0179 separates file-index path ownership from miss-cache eviction; GQR-0198 binds decoded resource and hash to same immutable source. Existing process-tree supervision, debug pipe error-before-close, attempt-owned extraction and save backup recovery remain distinct terminal ownership contracts. Paired game EVENT close can longjmp; BR-0345 cleanup cannot assume an ordinary C++ destructor runs across native nonlocal exit

No runtime, sanitizer, device or build ran. Required tests inject producer/consumer barriers, cancellation after real start, old completion after replacement, allocation at every ownership transfer, repeated surface/context loss and JNI attach failure, release counts and native longjmp exits. Cross-map DashMap self-deadlock remains BR-0153 with strict runtime deadline. Complete live delta/frozen tails and three investigation gates remain open. This sweep maps existing owners and adds no duplicate remediation

# Ordinary investigation measurements 20261006

## GQI-0005 scope and result

PARTIAL, no new defect admitted. Compiled the unchanged production android_axis_mailbox.cpp with a bounded measurement driver using pinned NDK r30, x86_64-linux-android26, C++17, -O2 and static libc++. Ran four short serial processes on the Android API-34 emulator; every driver assertion uses explicit return values and remains active in optimized builds

- The driver submits batches of three axes through the real production API, simulating consumer absence by postponing dequeue. It does not sleep for the modeled duration or drive actual Android UI/sensor events
- Synthetic held input and threshold crossings cover 1,800 or 14,400 samples, with an explicit final zero batch. The loop verifies exact transition count, nondecreasing generation, legal axis identity, final snapshot release and final queued release
- Payload bytes are count times sizeof(transition), excluding deque/allocator overhead. VmRSS is a coarse process measurement; it is not exact queue allocation accounting. Drain time includes mutex/dequeue and probe assertions, but excludes real SDL handlers, introspection and rendering
- Current MainActivity publishes normalized controller axes at offset 16; the mailbox records transitions only below axis 13. The controller case therefore exercises latest-state coalescing and creates no transition backlog
- MainActivity.onStop pauses gyro sampling and calls InputMixer.releaseAll; InputMixer suppresses unchanged mixed values and sends final zeros. These are static lifecycle observations, not a measured background sensor rate
- Touch/gyro channels and automation still can queue crossings; the container has no explicit bound. The measurements alone do not establish harmful growth during a supported real loading/suspend scenario

| 30s at 60Hz held | `frames=1800 axes=3 offset=0 crossing=0 transitions=6 payload_bytes=144 rss_before_kib=2968 rss_queued_kib=2968 drain_us=8 ordered=1 final_released=1` |
| 30s at 60Hz crossings | `frames=1800 axes=3 offset=0 crossing=1 transitions=5400 payload_bytes=129600 rss_before_kib=3068 rss_queued_kib=3068 drain_us=87 ordered=1 final_released=1` |
| 120s at 120Hz crossings | `frames=14400 axes=3 offset=0 crossing=1 transitions=43200 payload_bytes=1036800 rss_before_kib=2956 rss_queued_kib=3872 drain_us=652 ordered=1 final_released=1` |

### Existing mailbox regression

- Both normal Windows mailbox executables printed passed, but inspection of buildd2/build.ninja confirmed /DNDEBUG with no /UNDEBUG. Their assertion checks are disabled; do not count those runs as behavioral validation. This remains existing BR-0662 ownership
- Independently rebuilt the unchanged maintained test plus unchanged mailbox with MSVC x86 /O2 /UNDEBUG, then ran it to terminal exit 0: android axis mailbox tests passed
- An assertion-enabled NDK test binary compiled successfully, but the emulator disappeared before its push. adb devices then returned an empty list. No on-device unit-test execution or restart is claimed; the earlier four completed measurement processes remain valid

### Remaining GQI-0005 decision

Observe actual producer activity during a supported loading stall and full engine drain cost if needed. Do not invent an overflow policy that drops short pulses or final releases based only on an unbounded container. Any future admission must distinguish touch/gyro transitions from current normalized controller channels

# GQI-0006 native save-pair interruption evidence 20261006

## Result and scope

Confirmed native-helper interruption/retry and cleanup/rollback failure behavior; broader GQI-0006 generation policy remains OPEN. This extends the existing BR-0235/GQI-0006 publication scope, not a new unrelated defect

- Compiled unchanged android_file_pair_transaction.c with MSVC x86 /O2 /W4 and a small host driver. Final compilation has no warnings
- Each case uses six synthetic ordinary files under its own repository-local scratch directory. No game save, player, manifest or user config was opened or modified
- The production helper receives actual host filesystem exists/rename/remove callbacks. The probe intentionally returns failure for specified operations; after a selected successful rename it terminates its own process with _exit(99), preventing helper rollback
- A fresh process then stages a distinct retry pair and invokes the same unchanged helper with no injected faults. All child executions have ten-second deadlines and checked exit codes
- The Windows C-runtime callbacks are a test backend for the production operations interface. Actual Android PhysicsFS and full launcher/native restore paths were not run; no claim of filesystem power-loss durability is made
- Normal publication and a second save both succeed. All four interrupted states reject the next save because a deterministic backup exists; retry deletes its own temporary pair and preserves the earlier remnants
- Failed backup cleanup reports publication success while retaining both backups, then rejects the next save. Failure of primary publication followed by failure restoring its backup leaves primary absent, old companion live and old primary in backup; retry again rejects
- No tested case permanently loses the old primary. A recoverable backup and an unusable current slot are different outcomes; do not describe them as proven permanent loss

## Actual filesystem states

Values O/N denote old/new generation, dash means absent. Retry staging uses a third generation. Each state below was read from disk after the child terminated

| Case | First exit | Live primary | Live companion | Primary backup | Companion backup | Retry exit |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| normal | 0 | N | N | - | - | 0 |
| cut_1 | 99 | - | O | O | - | 1 |
| cut_2 | 99 | - | - | O | O | 1 |
| cut_3 | 99 | - | N | O | O | 1 |
| cut_4 | 99 | N | N | O | O | 1 |
| cleanup_failure | 0 | N | N | O | O | 1 |
| rollback_failure | 1 | - | O | O | - | 1 |

## Production linkage and policy constraints

- state_android_publish_save_slot stages a secret companion, then supplies primary.tmp / primary / primary.bak and companion.tmp / companion / companion.bak to the shared helper through PhysicsFS callbacks
- The helper refuses any existing backup before recording prior state. Success ignores backup-delete results; rollback ignores delete/restore results. No recovery entry point exists in its interface
- A repair must resolve interrupted generations before a new save or restore attempt, preserve recoverable bytes through cleanup/rollback failures, distinguish committed companion absence, and avoid mixing an old main save with a new companion
- File existence alone is ambiguous after partial rollback: primary may be restored while companion rollback still fails. Blindly removing backups whenever primary exists cannot establish a coherent generation
- Prefer an explicit branch-owned transaction/generation identity and recovery state, with the main/companion/retained manifest/progress inventory contract reconciled before implementation. Preserve the native save formats; Android transaction metadata can use one current pre-release schema
- Cleanup failure after an already committed pair must not make every later save fail without recovery. Failed recovery must preserve useful remnants and return actionable status rather than discard the only old copy
- This report does not choose a complete journal/pointer design or claim retained restart/progress inventory admission is covered. Those remaining parts must be reviewed and validated before GQI-0006 closes

# GQI-0006 recovery policy and remediation admission 20261006

## Disposition

CONFIRMED and assigned GQR-0236 under existing BR-0235, with restore admission coordinated with BR-0206. Do not allocate another GQF for the same incomplete-generation publication root. The preceding imported actual-file interruption report proves the retry/rollback failure; this report completes ownership and recovery-policy preparation, not implementation validation

## Current producer and consumer review

- Read complete retained restart persistence and load paths in coop_level_restart.c, the progress publisher/reader in coop_save.c, shared fixed-slot and single-file publication in state_android_shared.c, the native pair helper and its existing test
- Retained restart writes a temporary save and manifest, renames save first, manifest second, and deletes temporary files on failure. Its keep-highest decision reads the old manifest level and tests only save existence
- A failure between retained-save and manifest renames can leave a new save beside an old manifest. Launcher readCoopLevelStartEntries already validates mission, client membership, containment, size and checksum; preserve those checks
- Native coop_level_restart_load_retained_and_request opens the fixed save name, validates length/read, then labels the in-memory buffer with the current level/campaign/mission without reading the committed manifest or verifying its checksum/identity
- CoopSaveCompatibility.selectedPath resolves the selected manifest path and native compatibility status, while hostRevision polls path/length/mtime. Neither replaces generation admission in the native restore path
- Progress inventory writes mission-scoped and root copies independently. Its single-file publication duplicates the deterministic backup/delete/unchecked restore algorithm in state_android_shared.c. The reader validates format/version/length/checksum and mission/preceding level, but backup remnants have no recovery admission
- Native save bodies and engine-owned schema/semantic restore checks remain in the native engine. The selected repair belongs in branch-added Android publication/restore owners; no broad inherited refactor is justified

## Accepted recovery policy

1. Define a committed generation before exposing its save, required companion-presence state and advertisement. A coherent old generation must remain recoverable until the new commit is established
2. For fixed native slot names, record enough branch-owned transaction state to distinguish interrupted forward publication from partial rollback. Recover before read/restore and before another write. Existence of primary alone is insufficient, as the earlier fault matrix demonstrates
3. For retained restart, the manifest is the generation authority: stage the owned save generation, publish its validated manifest last, and require native and launcher consumers to agree on mission/level/size/checksum and selected identity before use. Retain the previous complete generation until commit; do not add a second competing source of save metadata
4. Progress inventory recovery preserves the last complete payload and requires scope/generation consistency before exposing progress state. Reconcile scoped/root publication policy explicitly; a failed scoped commit cannot silently advertise unrelated root inventory
5. Check rename, delete, flush/close and recovery outcomes. Cleanup failure after commit must remain retryable and distinguishable from failed publication. Never discard the only useful backup merely because its deterministic name already exists
6. Preserve native D1/D2 save formats and desktop behavior. Android transaction metadata is pre-release: use one current schema with no historical migration framework. Prefer extending shared branch-added ownership over copying transaction bodies into original engine files
7. Serialize the actual readers/writers across launcher and game lifetimes as required by the existing ownership model. Keep source/manifest generation binding through validation and selection; do not implement recovery by racing an uncoordinated launcher scan

## GQR-0236 implementation and validation boundary

- Owners: android_file_pair_transaction.c/.h, state_android_shared.c, coop/coop_level_restart.c, coop/coop_save.c, their native/JNI selection seams and launcher retained checkpoint consumers where needed
- Existing controls to retain: checked native body/trailer/close results, native compatibility validation, launcher checksum/size admission, companion staging before main publication, pointer publication only after save commit, failed-save suppression of history/peer success
- Extend maintained native transaction tests with actual restart states, cleanup failures, failed rollback and retry; include explicit companion absence and preservation of all recoverable prior bytes
- Add ordinary interrupted-publication integration for manual/autosave slots, retained restart and progress inventory: after every publication step, restart/reopen through production readers, require exactly one complete accepted generation, and then require another save to succeed
- Inject or simulate write/flush/close/rename/delete failures through maintained interfaces; verify surfaced status, unchanged prior generation on uncommitted failure, and no success advertisement of an unaccepted generation
- Run paired D1/D2 native and Android integration, relevant launcher tests and scoped formatting; preserve original-format compatibility and record inherited diff metrics
- Power-loss filesystem durability and security reproduction are separate claims; do not infer them from orderly process termination or include deferred security probes

## Evidence and limitations

The actual host process-cut matrix is in GQI-0006 native save-pair interruption evidence 20261006. Broader retained/progress conclusions above are current-source tracing. Their end-to-end fault matrix is required fix validation, not already executed work. GQI-0006 can leave hypothesis status because the root is proven and policy/ownership are chosen; GQR-0236 and BR-0235 stay TODO/OPEN until implementation and full validation

NEW CANDIDATE GQF-0252/GQR-0237: the two automap EVENT_WINDOW_DRAW blocks duplicate the identical recorder/replay/network route-adoption decision. The exact duplicate gate-plus-call block SHA-256 is 1bdf8a9d8f4884cdbb2e8b720c810d5cf77a11bca6623d217c8bb2c09d852fc6. automap_metadata_update_route has only these two callers and explicitly discards player_objnum. Move eligibility into this existing per-game compiled shared owner, remove the unused player parameter, internalize allow_adoption and replace each inherited block with one no-argument call under its current Android guard

An in-memory textual model removes 12 D1 lines and 9 D2 lines (21 net inherited lines), including D1's two now-unneeded input-demo includes and only the replay include in D2. D2 still uses the recorder for map markers and must retain that include. This is a proposal, not an applied or tested patch.
