Shared boss HUD, difficulty, recovery, graphics safety and menu translation already hold the branch feature policy; compact call sites do not need another facade

## Common current-delta observations

- Read complete assigned deltas against GQ1, both paired config/automap/reactor/credits changes and the named owner functions. The source tables record frozen identities; inspected working copies match after checkout line-ending normalization
- Config read now uses signed wide file length, reserves the terminator, bounds PHYSFSX_fgets and rejects an absent strtok token. Retain these local read corrections. Android effects defaults use the shared AUDIO_DEFAULT_EFFECTS_VOLUME contract; desktop retains eight. These changes do not establish allocation-failure or arbitrary-config safety
- Config write acquires the graphics-store snapshot before opening descent.cfg. Snapshot failure releases its lock internally and reports not-ready; open failure and ordinary completion release the acquired lock. Exactly the ten graphics-store field keys use GRAPHICS_CONFIG_VALUE; desktop expands it to the existing value. Existing unchecked native write/close behavior and broader publication/concurrency owners are not claimed fixed by this serialization
- Automap idle consumes pending reactor/matcen actions on the game thread. Route cache adoption is disabled during recording, loaded replay and multiplayer; the shared updater throttles pending-cache checks and counts revision changes. Readiness drawing uses existing shared presentation logic. D1 keeps its initial route rescan; D2 removed that synchronous rescan. The proposed extraction changes neither distinction nor drawing order
- Reactor pause requires an active positive countdown, updates seconds-left consistently, returns before shake/timer work while paused, and resets on destruction/level initialization. Shared meta actions check map-cheat accessibility and dispatch multiplayer toggles through the network path. Source references also show reset at native restore/host migration; this is static lifecycle tracing, not pause/save/network runtime validation
- Boss HUD activation now uses actual weapon collisions instead of AI fire/teleport or generic damage. The shared owner checks target/weapon roles and the robot-parent signature; local cooperative collision sites send the dedicated HUD-shot action. This retains a small collision hook rather than repeating boss identification in the engines
- Cooperative pickup records before/after inventory around do_powerup, checks recovery provenance first, and keeps ordinary native pickup semantics. Mine accounting receives the actual creation result and increments only for successful, active recovery. The shared owner retains identity, remaining-quantity and idempotency policy; full recovery protocol coverage is a separate scope
- The MAX_PLAYERS comparison now rejects equality before indexing last_player_bump. Credits translate only the two accept/back controller buttons into a stack-owned key event whose lifetime covers the synchronous handler call; translation policy already resides in android_menu_navigation.h

## D1-specific observations

- AI constants and awareness_event move into the owning ai.h together with runtime externs for shared replay observation. Their values and fields remain native. init_ai_objects clears pending prior-mine events before rebuilding AI. difficulty_refresh_runtime_parameters retains the original D1 Gate_interval expression in the existing shared difficulty owner
- AI restore's appended awareness/last-position vectors now use PHYSFSX_readVector, matching the explicit little-endian PHYSFSX_writeVector writer; scalar event fields retain native/swap handling. Preflight still reads an equally sized temporary vector only to check consumed bytes, so that temporary decoding does not reject by vector value. Preserve native save formats; no cross-endian runtime test ran
- gamedata_android_reset_tbl resets the private installed/count/parser state after shared asset teardown calls gamedata_close and before baseline initialization. The implementation remains local to those private statics and exposes only one reset entry
- custom.c computes final PIG/POG offsets in PHYSFS_sint64 and rejects negative relative offsets, positions outside the file and final int overflow before storing the native custom_info offset. Header reader failures release their allocated array; the new metadata caller closes the file. Existing raw header/platform assumptions are not newly certified
- piggy_read_level_bitmap_flags reuses the engine's custom-header readers for pg1/dtx precedence, initializes an explicit flags array, distinguishes a missing optional file from an unreadable existing one, bounds DPOG header allocation, rejects unsupported PPIG remapping, skips negative/non-bitmap identities and returns failure before publishing a complete metadata result. Its secretarea consumer keeps a texture-completeness result rather than inventing a second Kotlin parser. Retain native format ownership even though this body is relatively large; moving it would duplicate private header readers or expose their internal layout
- HXM model replacement now invokes the canonical polymodel reader instead of reading the runtime structure as a disk record. This is a narrow format-owner correction, not full transactional HXM admission or proof about truncated model input. Existing asset/save admission findings keep their own validation boundaries

Snapshot failure releases its lock internally and reports not-ready; open failure and ordinary completion release the acquired lock. Exactly the ten graphics-store field keys use GRAPHICS_CONFIG_VALUE; desktop expands it to the existing value. Existing unchecked native write/close behavior and broader publication/concurrency owners are not claimed fixed by this serialization
- Automap idle consumes pending reactor/matcen actions on the game thread. Route cache adoption is disabled during recording, loaded replay and multiplayer; the shared updater throttles pending-cache checks and counts revision changes. Readiness drawing uses existing shared presentation logic. D1 keeps its initial route rescan; D2 removed that synchronous rescan. The proposed extraction changes neither distinction nor drawing order
- Reactor pause requires an active positive countdown, updates seconds-left consistently, returns before shake/timer work while paused, and resets on destruction/level initialization. Shared meta actions check map-cheat accessibility and dispatch multiplayer toggles through the network path. Source references also show reset at native restore/host migration; this is static lifecycle tracing, not pause/save/network runtime validation
- Boss HUD activation now uses actual weapon collisions instead of AI fire/teleport or generic damage. The shared owner checks target/weapon roles and the robot-parent signature; local cooperative collision sites send the dedicated HUD-shot action. This retains a small collision hook rather than repeating boss identification in the engines
- Cooperative pickup records before/after inventory around do_powerup, checks recovery provenance first, and keeps ordinary native pickup semantics. Mine accounting receives the actual creation result and increments only for successful, active recovery. The shared owner retains identity, remaining-quantity and idempotency policy; full recovery protocol coverage is a separate scope
- The MAX_PLAYERS comparison now rejects equality before indexing last_player_bump. Credits translate only the two accept/back controller buttons into a stack-owned key event whose lifetime covers the synchronous handler call; translation policy already resides in android_menu_navigation.h

- aistruct.h widens the runtime path index and attaches D1 saved-only fields to the runtime records, using the compact branch-owned d1_in_d2_ai_storage.h. Native ai_static_rw/ai_local_rw records remain separate. The native save writer dispatches d1_in_d2_ai_write_object before the D2 field conversion. - tmap_info_read_n exposes an existing native decoder used by the Guide-Bot asset reader. Editor HAM writers now call robot_info_write_n and check its result instead of dumping widened runtime robot_info records. The serializer prechecks widened sound IDs and writes explicit fields/endianness; the diagnostic reports the 480-byte native record size. The sound loader selects 22K only for the corresponding configured rate, otherwise 11K. No editor-format round trip or audio playback ran
- D1 reactor behavior is selected through existing semantics helpers before native D2 behavior; the helpers retain D1 countdown/strength/fire/effects calculations and fall through for ordinary D2. Reactor link loading compacts valid segment/side links before the final validator, preserving supported released-mission handling rather than moving this native-format policy into an Android reader
- collide.c removes two local D1 explosion-position implementations in favor of the existing D1 semantics owner, relocates the existing homing-bump environment helper to input_demo_hooks.c while retaining its body and collision call, and delegates D1 contact/weapon/boss decisions through narrow APIs. The homing helper remains live under the loaded-replay/desync-probe gate; this is relocation, not dead-code removal. Inspected selected helper bodies and D1 native counterpart ordering: D1 wall shove randomness precedes its rotational kick, while D2 retains its original ordering. Runtime replay parity remains a separate required oracle
- Final-boss route confirmation intercepts only an active confirmation exit step before ordinary endlevel dispatch. Cooperative travel blocks accepted player damage at its existing freeze policy boundary. These hooks retain branch-owned decision logic; full route/travel protocol review remains separately queued

## Current-source observations

- 3d.h declares the existing CPU-only projection owner with the same signature as the paired setup.c definitions. The earlier completed GQ2-CHUNK-0156/0171 reports established the projection-body equivalence and unchanged drawing wrapper order; this declaration is necessary for the shared visibility caller
- args.h exposes ReadCmdArgs(void), matching the existing per-engine definition. A repository-wide source search found real calls in android/tests/test_args_defaults.c: the maintained test poisons GameArg, calls the function with no arguments and with -netlog, then verifies desktop defaults/override. Retain this declaration; absence of ordinary gameplay calls does not make it unused
- gr.h places batch begin/end beside the native 2D primitive API, with OGL declarations and non-OGL no-op macros. The existing shared ogl_2d_batch.c owns bounded storage, flushing and actual begin/end definitions, and both arch/ogl CMake targets include it. This is the completed September lines/rectangles boundary, not a second copy to extract. GQR-0185 remains the separate pending textured-glyph/automap-line candidate
- ogl_init.h now declares the bitmap-name argument present in each implementation. The inspected entry resolves a NULL name with piggy_game_bitmap_name; the ordinary texture-load call passes NULL. Retain the public native signature; this does not complete the separately queued texture loading implementation review
- rbaudio.h replaces eight duplicate branch-specific prototypes with the existing shared rbaudio_bin.h include. A mechanical comparison verifies every removed signature in the shared header after whitespace normalization. Paired root CMake includes already expose the shared directory. Preserve the completed header consolidation and existing C/C++ caller linkage conventions; no new runtime behavior is inferred
- strutil.h includes stddef.h for its size_t-based non-Windows string APIs. This is header self-containment and should remain local
- xmodel.h adds explicit polygon/powerup identity and the existence query, matching xmodel_xlate, xmodel_show_if_loaded and xmodel_exists in both engines. Translation rejects negative/out-of-range input indices and unknown kinds; paired powerup callers use XM_POWERUP while polyobj uses XM_POLYOBJ. Preserve the native typed interface. Translation-table contents, asset loading and all draw outcomes remain separately scoped
- Existing BR-0197 Android enhanced-model mipmap issue remains in the context loader (legacy GL_GENERATE_MIPMAP under OGLES, explicit generation excluded there). This header change neither creates nor fixes that separately owned implementation issue. Archived BR-0196 remains separate; no new finding or false closure
- interp.h adds G3_MODEL_COLOR_INDEXED = 0x8000 with the explicit RGB15/indexed contract. GQ2-CHUNK-0171 already checked the matching interpreter and D1-asset producer: retaining a palette index is explicit runtime encoding, not format guessing. Keep the constant beside the native interpreter API

## Platform/input/lifecycle observations

- The paired virtual joystick limit increases from 8 to 16; desktop enumeration clamps the count before SDL_Joysticks indexing. JOY_MAX_AXES/BUTTONS scale with that limit; the local label buffer grows to 64. Keep the native device inventory and individual mapping policy local. Existing event index-admission concerns are not certified by this enumeration clamp
- Android joystick setup now calls the existing shared android_virtual_gamepad_init. Read its complete current body and constants: it owns names, base axes/buttons, axis-button exclusions, combiner axes, D-pad buttons, digital shoulders and BRAKE/GAS mappings. Native SDL handles and count publication stay local. This preserves the completed September/DMR1-CHUNK-004 extraction; no second helper is needed
- Normalized controller channels 16..31 bypass the legacy divide-by-256; the mailbox header explicitly defines that domain, while legacy/touch channels retain their scaling. Held nonzero events still dispatch. Event polling drains the mailbox before SDL events, and the idle-saver sleep branch follows event_poll, so sleep does not itself bypass input drain. GQI-0005 still needs actual supported loading-stall producer/full-handler measurements
- event_process ticks graphics/lifecycle/overlay/idle owners, updates the timer, pumps cooperative endgame/observer flyout, runs automation, and polls input before checking front-window changes. The shared endgame/flyout entries retain their own active/game-window/observer guards. The shared fast-replay entry steps only a foreground game and returns false for a frontmost dialog; the draw loop suppresses the replay game window but lets other windows draw. Sleeping single-player idles for 50 ms after input, while multiplayer hidden mode continues processing and skips presentation. No runtime timing or network correctness is inferred from call-site review
- window.h uses the existing shared accessor header, and window.c supplies one private-layout snapshot for the shared public accessors. Preserve completed GQR-0143. Current window_close still notifies before freeing the detached window; BR-0345's separate nonlocal-exit lifetime owner remains open

## Renderer observations and inherited minimization

- gr.c retains a local context-rebuild adapter because ogl_init_state is private: initialize render state, initialize merge programs under OGL_MERGE, then cache level textures. The EGL owner invokes it after replacing the lost context and initializing the shim. Shader deletion skips stale context names through ogl_shader_delete_program. Per-context MSAA, viewport, GPU-query and texture state is reset at the narrow smash hook
- Android mode changes call the shared graphics-safety admission before buffer reallocation, propagate EGL initialization failure, and suppress redundant level precache during restoration. Read the current shared admission/failure/restoration entry points and EGL resume sequence. Preserve this progress without closing BR-0251 or GQR-0174: full prerequisite failures, transaction and context lifecycle validation remain separately owned
- Desktop icon loading now checks the returned surface and frees it after SDL_WM_SetIcon in both OGL and software paths. Desktop shader construction checks the extension function before calling it. These small platform corrections belong at their native call sites
- Circle/disk geometry is regenerated when the computed side count changes; cache destruction clears the pointers, so unchanged remembered side counts do not prevent recreation. Preserve this correction without generalizing the native circle implementation or claiming allocation-failure handling
- Existing shared ogl_2d_batch_draw replaces direct line/rectangle draws, preserving caller array enable/disable structure. This completed 2D primitive extraction is separate from the still-paired textured glyph and automap line machinery owned by GQR-0185. Current GQR-0178 merged-wall cache creation and GQR-0186 unused D1 polymodel cache helper remain actionable; source references show only D2 callers of that helper
- Texture runtime adapters now carry per-unit binding state through the existing shared merged-wall owner. The new skip optimization has a confirmed invalidation gap described below. Existing BR-0304 remains independently current: the compositor changes both source wrap states before selecting/binding the sources. Do not conflate that ordering defect with stale binding state
- Android transient blits reuse one shared texture record within the bounded cache dimensions, upload contents on every call, choose linear level-zero filtering for unscaled output, reset reused anisotropy and avoid incrementing texture count on handle reuse. Desktop retains fresh allocation/free. Keep current size/fallback and palette/upload ordering; this static read does not validate rendered output or every upload failure
- Desktop scene clear saves/restores the scissor box and enable state and confines color/depth clear to the current canvas. Android retains its nested MSAA clear policy, routes error collection to the existing shared owner, and adds staged trace/probe/presentation calls. MSAA trace entry gates GL queries by remaining trace count and category; full probe implementation review remains queued
- The explicit bitmap-name argument retains native fallback lookup when NULL. All five extension lookups now pass their actual filename capacity to the completed GQR-0001 shared builder. PNG upload reinitializes texture metadata for the decoded dimensions/channels even when a cache record exists. Preserve these fixes and D1/D2 texture-root differences; no whole decoder or resource-limit certification

## Audio observations and concurrent scope

- Preserve completed GQR-0159: actual Mix_QuerySpec and mixer-init diagnostics now have one shared owner. Android retains 256 output frames; desktop changes to 2048, or 1024 on Apple. No latency or listening equivalence is claimed for that deliberate buffer change
- Both engines call sound_mixer_convert for source-rate conversion and publish/free its malloc-owned output through SoundChunks. Read the shared body: it initializes outputs, validates length/rates/channel count, bounds rounded output frame count and SDL allocation multiplier, explicitly resamples U8 mono, checks allocation/conversion and publishes only success. This is a shared implementation already, not another extraction candidate
- D1 uses per-sample rate with 11K fallback. D2 conversion uses per-sample rate with 22K fallback; current PIG/SND/D1-asset producers explicitly assign sample rates. D2's trace fallback additionally consults GameArg; no supported zero-rate producer defect was established here
- Sound trace baseline capture follows successful conversion; play tracing precedes Mix_PlayChannel so its hashing/logging cannot delay later volume setup after playback has begun. The trace entry gates repeated play diagnostics by category and bounded report count; conversion baseline hashing is deliberately retained. D1 cached-sound clearing frees only allocated buffers and zeros records; its shared asset-reset caller stops sounds first. This is lifecycle tracing, not live audio quiescence validation
- HMQ now shares HMP conversion, and jukebox extensions add HMQ/MIDI/WAV with a NULL terminator. D2's declaration loses its stale fixed bound. Preserve native filename dispatch and current format support
- The paired digi_mixer.c working copies have concurrent effects-slider changes beyond frozen HEAD. Those edits were read as an ownership boundary, not changed or credited as frozen GQ2 coverage. ## Confirmed BR-0256 reopening and fix boundary

The archived BR-0256 repair deliberately made every requested bind unconditional. Current source restores a cache skip, now indexed by active texture unit. That fixes cross-unit aliasing but does not invalidate the cache after outside mutations. Both xmodel_show bodies bind their own textures directly and return without restoring bindings or invalidating the engine cache; ogl_freetexture deletes a name without invalidating the corresponding cached entries. The GLES shim does not redefine glBindTexture

Ordinary sequence: engine helper binds texture A on unit 0, enhanced-model rendering directly binds B on that unit, then another cached engine request for A takes the equality early return while actual binding remains B. This is a current regression under the same binding-state owner, not a new GQF root. Native deletion followed by name reuse needs the same ownership rule; the deletion case below models the state change rather than exercising a driver allocator

GQR-0238: repair coherent binding ownership across cached engine binds, raw enhanced-model/shared/probe binds, deletion, filter changes and context reset. Keep per-game compilation and native model ownership; retain the optimization only where cache validity is established. The obsolete scalar last_bound_tex is no longer read as a binding value; remove its residual adapter/reset plumbing if the chosen coherent boundary makes it unnecessary. Do not add a parallel cache or claim a one-site workaround covers all mutations

Validation must exercise actual production helpers with stateful GL calls and positive reuse controls, then paired Android rendering with mixed enhanced/native objects and sentinel textures, unit transitions, deletion/reuse, bulk filtering, context restoration and existing merged-wall paths. Verify actual binding and pixels/counters, relevant desktop/Android builds, scoped quality and isolated inherited metrics. The existing structural test must not be the sole oracle. Coordinate GQR-0178/GQR-0185 and BR-0304 without merging independent wrap-state or batching defects

New remediation rating: 56, MEDIUM-HIGH (H/M/B/C/R = 32/0/7/10/7), existing BR-0256 owner. This unit's highest inherited-minimization reference remains GQR-0185 at 84 (32/28/7/10/7); no new savings are counted

Exact harness for reproducibility (GL stand-in, not real GLES):

```c
#include <stdio.h>
#include <string.h>
typedef unsigned int GLuint;
typedef unsigned int GLenum;
#define GL_TEXTURE_2D 0x0de1u
#define GL_TEXTURE0 0x84c0u
static GLuint actual[3];
static int actual_unit;
static unsigned int calls;
static void glBindTexture(GLenum target, GLuint handle) {
    (void)target;
    actual[actual_unit] = handle;
    ++calls;
}
static void glActiveTexture(GLenum texture) {
    actual_unit = (int)(texture - GL_TEXTURE0);
}
struct android_ogl_bind_texture_state {
	GLuint *bound_textures;
	int bound_texture_count;
	int *active_texture_unit;
	int *texbinds;
	int *texbind_reuse;
};

void android_ogl_bind_texture_2d(const struct android_ogl_bind_texture_state *state,
                                 GLuint handle)
{
	GLuint *bound_texture = NULL;

	if (state && state->bound_textures && state->active_texture_unit &&
	    *state->active_texture_unit >= 0 &&
	    *state->active_texture_unit < state->bound_texture_count)
		bound_texture = &state->bound_textures[*state->active_texture_unit];
	if (bound_texture && *bound_texture == handle) {
		if (state->texbind_reuse)
			(*state->texbind_reuse)++;
		return;
	}
	glBindTexture(GL_TEXTURE_2D, handle);
	if (state) {
		if (bound_texture)
			*bound_texture = handle;
		if (state->texbinds)
			(*state->texbinds)++;
	}
}

void android_ogl_active_texture(const struct android_ogl_bind_texture_state *state,
                                GLenum texture)
{
	glActiveTexture(texture);
	if (!state || !state->active_texture_unit)
		return;
	if (texture >= GL_TEXTURE0 &&
	    texture < GL_TEXTURE0 + state->bound_texture_count)
		*state->active_texture_unit = (int) (texture - GL_TEXTURE0);
	else
		*state->active_texture_unit = -1;
}

void android_ogl_reset_texture_bindings(const struct android_ogl_bind_texture_state *state)
{
	if (!state)
		return;
	if (state->bound_textures && state->bound_texture_count > 0)
		memset(state->bound_textures, 0xff,
		       sizeof(*state->bound_textures) * state->bound_texture_count);
	if (state->active_texture_unit)
		*state->active_texture_unit = 0;
}


int main(void) {
    GLuint cache[3];
    int unit = 0, binds = 0, reuse = 0;
    struct android_ogl_bind_texture_state state = {cache, 3, &unit, &binds, &reuse};
    android_ogl_reset_texture_bindings(&state);
    android_ogl_active_texture(&state, GL_TEXTURE0);
    android_ogl_bind_texture_2d(&state, 37);
    android_ogl_bind_texture_2d(&state, 37);
    if (actual[0] != 37 || binds != 1 || reuse != 1 || calls != 1) return 1;
    android_ogl_active_texture(&state, GL_TEXTURE0 + 1);
    android_ogl_bind_texture_2d(&state, 37);
    if (actual[1] != 37 || binds != 2 || calls != 2) return 2;
    puts("PASS control: same-unit reuse and separate-unit first bind");
    android_ogl_active_texture(&state, GL_TEXTURE0);
    glBindTexture(GL_TEXTURE_2D, 99);
    android_ogl_bind_texture_2d(&state, 37);
    printf("external_bind requested=37 actual=%u cached=%u reuse=%d\n", actual[0], cache[0], reuse);
    if (actual[0] != 99 || cache[0] != 37 || reuse != 2) return 3;
    android_ogl_reset_texture_bindings(&state);
    android_ogl_bind_texture_2d(&state, 37);
    if (actual[0] != 37) return 4;
    puts("PASS control: explicit invalidation restores required bind");
    actual[0] = 0;
    android_ogl_bind_texture_2d(&state, 37);
    printf("deleted_binding requested=37 actual=%u cached=%u reuse=%d\n", actual[0], cache[0], reuse);
    if (actual[0] != 0 || cache[0] != 37 || reuse != 3) return 5;
    puts("CONFIRMED: helper trusts stale cache after raw bind or simulated deletion");
    return 0;
}
```

## Platform/input/lifecycle observations

- The paired virtual joystick limit increases from 8 to 16; desktop enumeration clamps the count before SDL_Joysticks indexing. JOY_MAX_AXES/BUTTONS scale with that limit; the local label buffer grows to 64. Keep the native device inventory and individual mapping policy local. Existing event index-admission concerns are not certified by this enumeration clamp
- Android joystick setup now calls the existing shared android_virtual_gamepad_init. Read its complete current body and constants: it owns names, base axes/buttons, axis-button exclusions, combiner axes, D-pad buttons, digital shoulders and BRAKE/GAS mappings. Native SDL handles and count publication stay local. This preserves the completed September/DMR1-CHUNK-004 extraction; no second helper is needed
- Normalized controller channels 16..31 bypass the legacy divide-by-256; the mailbox header explicitly defines that domain, while legacy/touch channels retain their scaling. Held nonzero events still dispatch. Event polling drains the mailbox before SDL events, and the idle-saver sleep branch follows event_poll, so sleep does not itself bypass input drain. GQI-0005 still needs actual supported loading-stall producer/full-handler measurements
- event_process ticks graphics/lifecycle/overlay/idle owners, updates the timer, pumps cooperative endgame/observer flyout, runs automation, and polls input before checking front-window changes. The shared endgame/flyout entries retain their own active/game-window/observer guards. The shared fast-replay entry steps only a foreground game and returns false for a frontmost dialog; the draw loop suppresses the replay game window but lets other windows draw. Sleeping single-player idles for 50 ms after input, while multiplayer hidden mode continues processing and skips presentation. No runtime timing or network correctness is inferred from call-site review
- window.h uses the existing shared accessor header, and window.c supplies one private-layout snapshot for the shared public accessors. Preserve completed GQR-0143. Current window_close still notifies before freeing the detached window; BR-0345's separate nonlocal-exit lifetime owner remains open

- Retain the native libpng read corrections. Android CMake forces PNG OFF and supplies shared/pngfile.c using stb_image; desktop misc conditionally compiles this libpng file. These are separate backend owners, so moving the native correction into Android would not preserve desktop behavior
- The libpng reader checks read/info creation, preserves row_pointers across longjmp with volatile, frees and nulls output pointers on decode failure, expands palette and tRNS before update_info and allocation, handles interlace, checks allocation products/results, and derives output channel flags from transformed metadata. ## Current-source observations

- Retain the 40-to-64-byte diagnostic label expansion. The longest signed 32-bit formatted index requires 46 bytes including NUL; the current enclosing loader additionally caps bitmap count at 100 before this nonnegative loop. No need for an Android wrapper around this local fix
- CFile::Seek now returns a signed zero-success/minus-one-failure status rather than the current file offset, reflecting PHYSFS_seek's boolean result for absolute/current/end origins and returning failure for an unsupported origin. The repository search within both xmodel trees finds only the definitions, no current calls. Retain this native wrapper contract correction without inventing execution coverage or a new extraction; broader CFile input handling remains separate
- Explicit vmat_elem/vpos_elem arrays preserve the nine-component transpose, three-component translation and final forward-vector sign conversion without pointer arithmetic across struct members. The changed transform and translation/show/exists bodies are identical in both engines; the full files differ in the pre-existing placement of the OGLES legacy mipmap call
- SDL.h supplies SDL_arraysize for the typed translator. XM_POLYOBJ and XM_POWERUP select separate tables; negative/out-of-range indices and unknown kinds return -1. show_if_loaded and exists check unsupported/missing models before using the table result. Only model_pyrogl receives the player team-color argument; other enhanced assets receive -1
- Complete static enum evaluation verifies every table value is -1 or an in-range filename index. Every named powerup enum was paired with its actual table entry, shown below; optional unsupported entries fall back. The new tables retain each game's native index order and D2-specific assets. Do not combine these format-specific tables or broadly deduplicate the inherited xmodel implementation
- Current powerup callers use XM_POWERUP, check existence, and fall back to native sprite drawing if enhanced drawing is unavailable; polygon callers use XM_POLYOBJ. Asset load-all iterates the filename array with NUM_XMODELS. This establishes source consistency, not successful loading or rendering of external assets
- BR-0197 remains OPEN: both OGLES model loaders select a mipmapped filter, issue unsupported legacy GL_GENERATE_MIPMAP and omit explicit generation. D1 issues the legacy parameter after upload, D2 before; neither ordering resolves the GLES defect. Archived BR-0196 VBO repair is not reopened or revalidated by this review
- BR-0256/GQR-0238 remains OPEN: the model load/show paths bind textures directly and free_gl deletes them without updating the shared binding cache. The preceding GQ2-0157/0172 production-helper stand-in reproduced the stale-cache failure; this review corroborates the actual model mutation sites, but adds no fresh runtime or GLES pixel evidence. Reuse the existing remediation instead of a duplicate finding

## Current-source observations

- Retain the 40-to-64-byte diagnostic label expansion. The longest signed 32-bit formatted index requires 46 bytes including NUL; the current enclosing loader additionally caps bitmap count at 100 before this nonnegative loop. No need for an Android wrapper around this local fix
- CFile::Seek now returns a signed zero-success/minus-one-failure status rather than the current file offset, reflecting PHYSFS_seek's boolean result for absolute/current/end origins and returning failure for an unsupported origin. The repository search within both xmodel trees finds only the definitions, no current calls. Retain this native wrapper contract correction without inventing execution coverage or a new extraction; broader CFile input handling remains separate
- Explicit vmat_elem/vpos_elem arrays preserve the nine-component transpose, three-component translation and final forward-vector sign conversion without pointer arithmetic across struct members. The changed transform and translation/show/exists bodies are identical in both engines; the full files differ in the pre-existing placement of the OGLES legacy mipmap call
- SDL.h supplies SDL_arraysize for the typed translator. XM_POLYOBJ and XM_POWERUP select separate tables; negative/out-of-range indices and unknown kinds return -1. show_if_loaded and exists check unsupported/missing models before using the table result. Only model_pyrogl receives the player team-color argument; other enhanced assets receive -1
- Complete static enum evaluation verifies every table value is -1 or an in-range filename index. - Current powerup callers use XM_POWERUP, check existence, and fall back to native sprite drawing if enhanced drawing is unavailable; polygon callers use XM_POLYOBJ. - BR-0197 remains OPEN: both OGLES model loaders select a mipmapped filter, issue unsupported legacy GL_GENERATE_MIPMAP and omit explicit generation. ## Ownership and change review

- endlevel.c: retain shared description/bitmap/route validation and local application of native geometry. The shared eight-field parser bounds input before conversion; the route walk checks reciprocal links and finite traversal, handles a direct exterior, and returns the actual opening. Runtime positioning recomputes station/satellite positions from saved direction vectors for that opening. Optional data remains unloaded on failure. No fresh malformed-media reproduction or full validator certification
- The endlevel animation frame fields now reset on each actual rendered entry; flythrough actors are zeroed, camera cleared and failure state reset. This is intentional current behavior. The Sept24 continuation explicitly supersedes the earlier endlevel-history persistence experiment following user clarification: incidental animation timing/FX history is not saved gameplay fidelity. Do not revive that serializer or experimental save versions from the stale historical report
- Flythrough movement subdivides a frame at F1_0/60, preserving the whole frame while tracking a crossed camera-transition segment. Object and side bounds are checked; local path failures end the optional presentation. Remote actors use detached object copies and find_point_seg rather than insertion into gameplay object lists. Observation accessors expose native state without consuming RNG. This is native animation integration, not a blanket opportunity to move existing engine code
- Shared co-op begin/frame/render/end hooks own remote presentation. Exit ages are tied to the current world visit, retries can only move the start earlier, and secret/disconnected/observer peers are filtered. finish_endlevel avoids recursive campaign completion during the coordinator; the local outside shot remains active while awaiting peers. Broader network/barrier correctness, actor catch-up cost and asset admission remain separately queued scopes
- fireball.c/h: retain the network-created-robot capacity guard before RNG/object creation and Net_create_objnums insertion. The exploding-wall type, limit and extern moved to the native header for checkpoint observation; the list still has one native definition and still drives damaging blasts/wall opening. No Android copy of native gameplay layout
- fuelcen.c/h: retain shared mode admission/counting at activation and level-count reset. Refuel cadence remains native: the same 64-bit time gate and assignment now use a file-static field with typed get/set accessors. Fusion cadence in game.c is likewise exposed without changing its original gate; the corrected comment acknowledges awareness/overcharge effects. Existing GQR-0175 restored-clock validation remains independent and open
- The newly added matcen_set_mode/matcen_restore_mode calls expose a real native indexing defect in disable_matcens, detailed below. Shared mode state and counters pass their maintained test, which does not exercise station shutdown
- game.c: the Android profile scene scanner has one shared owner with the same object-count/remote-owner traversal; keep the compact call at the existing simulation profiling point. Hidden idle mode caps pacing at 60 and sleeps even with VSync because no visible swap supplies pacing. Native timing and rendering policy remain at their respective engine boundaries
- The Android game event handler suppresses ordinary input/draw during co-op briefing/endgame while preserving close/activation events, consumes restore-to-menu requests, avoids resuming a transfer-paused clock, and pumps the restore barrier before a draw. Inspecting pause_frame shows it may return zero after pumping even while time_paused still gates simulation; do not mislabel zero as proof of a completed restore. GameProcessFrame rechecks pause/menu requests immediately after multi_do_frame
- D1 replay Space toggles pause and Right requests one step; idle replay input is suppressed, manual step clears after its draw, and both flags reset on the non-replay branch. Native replay observation remains cross-platform. Android capture time scaling is confined by the shared helper to non-multiplayer, non-replay endlevel presentation; its normal defaults return the original frame time
- Main-view drawing checks automap/hidden state before graphics-safety admission and reports a rendered view only after drawing. These hooks retain engine ordering while the shared safety owner handles its settings state. Close consumes pending restore requests, stops audio/replay, leaves multiplayer, frees the Android mission before title music, and resets endgame on CLOSED. Existing BR-0345 nonlocal window-close lifetime issue is not resolved by the longjmp path
- game.h adds the typed cadence/difficulty/time-pause declarations with actual native/shared callers. gamecntl.c uses the shared controller-to-menu key mapping in pause, accepts Enter on Android, uses the canonical auto-abort description, and orients the debug finish-level warp from the exit side normal with COMPACT_SEGS handling. These are local native hooks, not duplicate implementations
- gamerend.c retains the completed texture-label extraction: shared owner selects the canvas/font, draws hires/base labels with the same RGB override and resets that override. Standalone loading boxes notify the introspection probe and clear discarded Android OGL backing before drawing/flipping; overlay boxes retain their existing backing. Native draw geometry remains local

## New ordinary correctness finding: GQF-0253 / GQR-0239

Both native disable_matcens functions iterate i < Num_robot_centers but clear Station[i]. Station contains all fuel/repair/reactor/robot centers in native creation order; matcen_create records the actual station index in RobotCenters[matcen_num].fuelcen_num. There is no invariant that robot centers occupy a station prefix. The newly added mode set/restore wrappers call this function when entering or leaving PAUSED

A valid mixed layout fuel/robot/fuel/robot has two robot centers at station indices 1 and 3. Selecting PAUSED clears slots 0 and 1, leaves robot slot 3 Enabled with its original Disable_time, and changes an unrelated fuel slot. The shared gate blocks new trigger activations, but fuelcen_update_all still dispatches every robot station and robotmaker_proc checks Enabled, not the mode. Thus an already active missed center can continue its ordinary generation path until other native conditions stop it. The probe proves the missed shutdown, not an actual spawned robot or complete game tick

Compiled the unchanged three native functions (byte-identical in D1 and D2) with the actual shared matcen_mode.c, using a stand-in containing only the two accessed station fields. Contiguous robots at slots 0/1 are a passing control. Mixed-layout set and restore both reproduce the missed active slot. These are ordinary supported state transitions, not security, malformed-input or resource-pressure probes

- Production-functions SHA-256: 30052ba8d2fbf174ce609d182e458a754bbdfff277a08618bd55db581d400c1c
- Probe SHA-256: 7e897176bbe67685e4a04fd53bca496d775f06a391a909264dbaa5f76d9d67d0
- Build: MSVC x86 /W4 /O2 /MD /DNDEBUG; no compiler warning; probe and maintained shared-mode test both exit 0
- The probe intentionally exits successfully when it reproduces the defect; this is not evidence the production behavior is correct
- Maintained android/tests/test_matcen_mode.c uses explicit expect/failure returns, so /DNDEBUG does not disable its checks. It passes while missing the engine integration bug

```text
PASS control: contiguous robot centers at station slots 0 and 1 disabled
mixed set paused=1 robot1_enabled=0 robot3_enabled=1 robot3_disable_time=65536 fuel0_enabled=0
mixed restore robot3_enabled=1 robot3_disable_time=65536
CONFIRMED: native pause/restore leave a mixed-layout robot center enabled
PASS: matcen tri-state mode
```

Proposed repair stays in paired native fuelcen.c: disable actual robot stations through their native mapping or a type-filtered station traversal, preserving other station fields and normal mode/count policy. Add meaningful engine-level mixed-order coverage of mode set and restore; preserve D1/D2 differences and test the shared UI/restore callers. Validate actual cessation of an active late-index center, default/one-round transitions, ordinary save/restore and paired builds. Do not create an Android replacement station registry

P2/high confidence, correctness/gameplay. Impact 47 MEDIUM, H/M/B/C/R 23/0/7/10/7, PRIMARY GQR-0239, no inherited line-saving claim. This is a native pre-existing helper defect exposed by branch-added pause/restore semantics, not a claim that the helper itself was introduced in this delta. Searches of existing general/adversarial owners found no duplicate station-shutdown finding

## Full reproducer

```c
#include <stdio.h>
#include <string.h>
#include "matcen_mode.h"
typedef unsigned char ubyte;
/* Stand-in only for the two station fields touched by the native functions */
static struct { int Enabled, Disable_time; } Station[4];
static int Num_robot_centers;
void disable_matcens(void)
{
	int	i;

	for (i=0; i<Num_robot_centers; i++) {
		Station[i].Enabled = 0;
		Station[i].Disable_time = 0;
	}
}

int matcen_set_mode(int mode)
{
	int old_mode = matcen_mode_get();

	if (!matcen_mode_set(mode))
		return 0;
	if (old_mode == MATCEN_MODE_PAUSED || mode == MATCEN_MODE_PAUSED)
		disable_matcens();
	return 1;
}

int matcen_restore_mode(int mode, const ubyte *activation_counts, int count)
{
	int old_mode = matcen_mode_get();

	if (!matcen_mode_restore(mode, activation_counts, count))
		return 0;
	if (old_mode == MATCEN_MODE_PAUSED || mode == MATCEN_MODE_PAUSED)
		disable_matcens();
	return 1;
}
static void setup(void) {
    matcen_mode_reset_game();
    Num_robot_centers = 2;
    for (int i = 0; i < 4; ++i) {
        Station[i].Enabled = 1;
        Station[i].Disable_time = 65536;
    }
}
int main(void) {
    setup();
    if (!matcen_set_mode(MATCEN_MODE_PAUSED)) return 1;
    if (Station[0].Enabled || Station[1].Enabled) return 2;
    puts("PASS control: contiguous robot centers at station slots 0 and 1 disabled");
    /* Valid mixed layout: fuel, robot, fuel, robot; native creation maps robots to slots 1,3 */
    setup();
    if (!matcen_set_mode(MATCEN_MODE_PAUSED)) return 3;
    printf("mixed set paused=%d robot1_enabled=%d robot3_enabled=%d robot3_disable_time=%d fuel0_enabled=%d\n",
           matcen_mode_get() == MATCEN_MODE_PAUSED, Station[1].Enabled, Station[3].Enabled,
           Station[3].Disable_time, Station[0].Enabled);
    if (matcen_mode_get() != MATCEN_MODE_PAUSED || Station[1].Enabled || !Station[3].Enabled || Station[0].Enabled) return 4;
    setup();
    if (!matcen_restore_mode(MATCEN_MODE_PAUSED, NULL, 0)) return 5;
    printf("mixed restore robot3_enabled=%d robot3_disable_time=%d\n", Station[3].Enabled, Station[3].Disable_time);
    if (!Station[3].Enabled || Station[3].Disable_time != 65536) return 6;
    puts("CONFIRMED: native pause/restore leave a mixed-layout robot center enabled");
    return 0;
}
```

## Ownership and disposition

- escort.c coverage is restricted to assigned hunks 169-170, with the enclosing handler and named callers inspected as context. Spawn/dock/deploy messages retain sender, current-owner, master and generation checks. Runtime routing reset clears native selection/path state and only resets the actual companion's path. Menu introspection adapts the existing private menu rather than maintaining a second menu model
- escort.h retains its original public declarations and imports the branch-owned guidebot_extensions.h and shared goal-message interface. Current extension declarations include native/network, Android/route-planner and introspection guards. This is a small inherited boundary; do not inline the growing branch interface back into it
- fireball.c routes native D1 flash, boss blast, drop/replacement and wall-fireball sizing policy through existing native owners. Actor-role helpers exclude the optional D2 companion from D1 enemy behavior. The native drop branch and D2 fallback both check network creation capacity before RNG/object creation. Robot count initialization is called only after successful drop_powerup; its helper leaves non-robot/non-powerup drops alone
- Removing the mission-wide badass-explosion gate is supported by native asset ownership, not by claiming original D1 robots had this D2 field. The D1 robot reader zero-initializes D2 fields and never populates badass; the custom robot reader explicitly zeros it. Optional D2 actors retain their own data-driven behavior. - fuelcen.c/h retains the mode admission/count/reset hooks and native refuel clock accessors. D1 refuel cadence is 1/3 second; D2 keeps its passed 1/4 second value and separate repair-center cadence. D2 insane-difficulty centers retain ordinary nondecrement behavior except that explicit ONE_ROUND consumes the round. Shared scene profiling replaces the duplicate traversal; Android hidden pacing, capture-time adjustment and graphics admission stay at their actual simulation/render boundaries
- The event handler preserves close/activation events during co-op presentation, consumes restore-to-menu requests, and does not resume a transfer/travel-owned pause. Draw pumps restore first, then travel; negative results close and positive results return immediately. The shared travel function was read through its final return, including transfer pumping, pause release and the deferred physical-exit return

## New finding GQF-0254 / GQR-0240: recovery ammo quantity

P2/high confidence, ordinary co-op inventory correctness. A dead player may own a Vulcan weapon with zero or fewer than 196 rounds. allocate_egg explicitly assigns only the real ammo pool to its tagged weapon and preserves the weapon flag, so this is a valid live recovery item. The native collision paths admit a known LIVE item, snapshot the player, call do_powerup and then account for the observed inventory change

D1 reads the synthesized object's count and applies VULCAN_WEAPON_AMMO_AMOUNT on first acquisition without the recovery cap. D2 initially caps the amount, but in D1 mode d1_in_d2_prepare_vulcan_pickup raises it back to 196. The later recovery note only subtracts the minimum of the acquired delta and recorded ammo; it does not undo the player's excess. Thus recovery accounting cannot enforce its stated no-synthesized-ammo contract at these pickup sites

The compiled probe uses unchanged complete pickup switch cases from both engines plus the unchanged shared quantity function and native D1 preparation function. Small stand-ins supply a known item and successful first weapon acquisition; the ammo stub records the requested grant. No real network, game inventory, save or device is used. Cases with recorded 0/10 reproduce a 196 request in both native D1 paths; ordinary D2, recorded 196 and untagged ordinary behavior are controls. MSVC x86 /W4 /O2 /MD /DNDEBUG, final build/run exit 0 with no compiler warnings. The initial harness compile exposed only missing stand-in fields/name shadowing, which were corrected before this result

## Full ordinary pickup reproducer

Probe enum values are symbolic stand-ins, not a serialized-format claim; actual ammo constants and multiplayer masks are taken from paired native headers. Unchanged cases retain their exact source text in the hashed scratch probe; the displayed copy removes trailing whitespace only. Successful first-acquisition and ample receiver capacity are intentional scope limits

```c
#include <stdio.h>
#define GM_MULTI 38
#define GM_MULTI_COOP 16
#define VULCAN_INDEX 1
#define GAUSS_INDEX 6
#define VULCAN_WEAPON_AMMO_AMOUNT 196
#define VULCAN_AMMO_AMOUNT 98
#define CLASS_PRIMARY 0
#define GAUSS_STYLE_DUPLICATING 1
#define OF_COOP_RECOVERY 1
#define POW_VULCAN_WEAPON 1
#define POW_GAUSS_WEAPON 2
#define POW_VULCAN_AMMO 3
#define VULCAN_AMMO_SCORE 0
#define TXT_VULCAN_AMMO "Vulcan"
/* Only fields accessed by the unchanged functions and switch cases */
typedef struct object { int flags, id; struct { struct { int count; } powerup_info; } ctype; } object;
typedef struct coop_recovery_item { struct { unsigned int missiles[10], vulcan; } gear; } coop_recovery_item;
static coop_recovery_item probe_item;
static int Game_mode, native_d1, received;
static struct { int LowVulcan, GaussAmmoStyle; } Netgame;
static int coop_recovery_active(void) { return 1; }
static const coop_recovery_item *find_object(const object *obj) { (void)obj; return &probe_item; }
static int d1_in_d2_use_d1_gameplay(void) { return native_d1; }
static int pick_up_primary(int weapon) { (void)weapon; return 1; }
static int duplicate_primary_uses_single_player_reward(int weapon) { (void)weapon; return 0; }
static int pick_up_ammo(int type, int weapon, int amount) { (void)type; (void)weapon; received += amount; return amount; }
static int pick_up_vulcan_ammo(int amount) { received += amount; return amount > 0; }
static void powerup_basic(int r, int g, int b, int score, const char *format, ...) { (void)r; (void)g; (void)b; (void)score; (void)format; }
static unsigned int take_amount(unsigned int wanted, unsigned int available)
{
	return wanted < available ? wanted : available;
}

int coop_recovery_pickup_count(const object *powerup, int secondary, int amount)
{
	if (!coop_recovery_active() || !(powerup->flags & OF_COOP_RECOVERY)) return amount;
	const coop_recovery_item *item = find_object(powerup);
	if (!item) return 0;
	return (int) take_amount(amount, secondary >= 0 ? item->gear.missiles[secondary] : item->gear.vulcan);
}

int d1_in_d2_prepare_vulcan_pickup(int weapon_index, int new_weapon, int duplicate_reward, int *ammo)
{
	if (!d1_in_d2_use_d1_gameplay() || weapon_index != VULCAN_INDEX)
		return 0;
	if (!new_weapon && duplicate_reward) {
		*ammo = VULCAN_AMMO_AMOUNT;
		return 1;
	}
	if (new_weapon) {
		if (*ammo < VULCAN_WEAPON_AMMO_AMOUNT)
			*ammo = VULCAN_WEAPON_AMMO_AMOUNT;
		if ((Game_mode & GM_MULTI) && !(Game_mode & GM_MULTI_COOP) &&
			Netgame.LowVulcan && *ammo > VULCAN_WEAPON_AMMO_AMOUNT / 2)
			*ammo = VULCAN_WEAPON_AMMO_AMOUNT / 2;
	}
	return 0;
}
#define DROPPED_AMMO(obj, index, amount) coop_recovery_pickup_count(obj, index, amount)

static int d1_pickup(object *obj) {
    int used = 0, special_used = 0, id = POW_VULCAN_WEAPON;
    int ammo, duplicate_uses_single_player_reward;
    switch (id) {
		case	POW_VULCAN_WEAPON:
			ammo = obj->ctype.powerup_info.count;

			used = pick_up_primary(VULCAN_INDEX);
			duplicate_uses_single_player_reward = !used &&
				duplicate_primary_uses_single_player_reward(VULCAN_INDEX);

			//didn't get the weapon (because we already have it), but
			//maybe snag some of the ammo.  if single-player, grab all the ammo
			//and remove the powerup.  If multi-player take ammo in excess of
			//the amount in a powerup, and leave the rest.
			if (!used && !duplicate_uses_single_player_reward)
				if ((Game_mode & GM_MULTI) ) {
					if(Netgame.GaussAmmoStyle == GAUSS_STYLE_DUPLICATING) {
						ammo -= VULCAN_AMMO_AMOUNT;
					} else {
						ammo = 0; // Forgot to tell other players we took ammo, it dups, very bad
					}
				}
			if (used || ((Game_mode & GM_MULTI) && ammo > 0 &&
			             !duplicate_uses_single_player_reward)) {
				if (used) {
					if (ammo < VULCAN_WEAPON_AMMO_AMOUNT)
						ammo = VULCAN_WEAPON_AMMO_AMOUNT;
					if ( (Game_mode & GM_MULTI) && (!(Game_mode & GM_MULTI_COOP)) &&
						 Netgame.LowVulcan && ammo > VULCAN_WEAPON_AMMO_AMOUNT/2)
						ammo = VULCAN_WEAPON_AMMO_AMOUNT/2;
				}
				int ammo_used;
				ammo_used = pick_up_ammo(CLASS_PRIMARY, VULCAN_INDEX, ammo);
				obj->ctype.powerup_info.count -= ammo_used;
				if (!used && ammo_used) {
					powerup_basic(7, 14, 21, VULCAN_AMMO_SCORE, "%s!", TXT_VULCAN_AMMO);
					special_used = 1;
					id = POW_VULCAN_AMMO;		//set new id for making sound at end of this function
					if (obj->ctype.powerup_info.count == 0)
						used = 1;		//say used if all ammo taken
				}
			}

//added/edited 8/3/98 by Victor Rachels to fix vulcan multi bug
//check if multi, if so, pick up ammo w/o using, set ammo left. else, normal

//killed 8/27/98 by Victor Rachels to fix vulcan ammo multiplying.  new way
// is by spewing the current held ammo when dead.
//-killed                        if (!used && (Game_mode & GM_MULTI))
//-killed                        {
//-killed                         int tempcount;
//-killed                           tempcount=Players[Player_num].primary_ammo[VULCAN_INDEX];
//-killed                            if (pick_up_ammo(CLASS_PRIMARY, VULCAN_INDEX, obj->ctype.powerup_info.count))
//-killed                             obj->ctype.powerup_info.count -= Players[Player_num].primary_ammo[VULCAN_INDEX]-tempcount;
//-killed                        }
//end kill - Victor Rachels

			if (!used && duplicate_uses_single_player_reward)
//end addition/edit - Victor Rachels
				used = pick_up_vulcan_ammo(DROPPED_AMMO(obj, -1, VULCAN_AMMO_AMOUNT));
			break;
    }
    (void)special_used; return used;
}

static int d2_pickup(object *obj) {
    int used = 0, special_used = 0, id = POW_VULCAN_WEAPON;
    switch (id) {
		case	POW_VULCAN_WEAPON:
		case	POW_GAUSS_WEAPON: {
			int ammo = DROPPED_AMMO(obj, -1, obj->ctype.powerup_info.count);
			int weapon_index = (obj->id==POW_VULCAN_WEAPON)?VULCAN_INDEX:GAUSS_INDEX;
			int duplicate_uses_single_player_reward;

			used = pick_up_primary(weapon_index);
			duplicate_uses_single_player_reward = !used &&
				duplicate_primary_uses_single_player_reward(weapon_index);
			if (d1_in_d2_prepare_vulcan_pickup(weapon_index, used, duplicate_uses_single_player_reward, &ammo)) {
				used = pick_up_vulcan_ammo(DROPPED_AMMO(obj, -1, ammo));
				break;
			}

			//didn't get the weapon (because we already have it), but
			//maybe snag some of the ammo.  if single-player, grab all the ammo
			//and remove the powerup.  If multi-player take ammo in excess of
			//the amount in a powerup, and leave the rest.
			if (!used && !duplicate_uses_single_player_reward)
				if ((Game_mode & GM_MULTI) ) {
					if(Netgame.GaussAmmoStyle == GAUSS_STYLE_DUPLICATING) {
						ammo -= VULCAN_AMMO_AMOUNT;
					} else {
						ammo = 0; // Forgot to tell other players we took ammo, it dups, very bad
					}
				}
			if (ammo > 0) {
				int ammo_used;
				ammo_used = pick_up_ammo(CLASS_PRIMARY, VULCAN_INDEX, ammo);
				obj->ctype.powerup_info.count -= ammo_used;
				if (!used && ammo_used) {
					powerup_basic(7, 14, 21, VULCAN_AMMO_SCORE, "%s!", TXT_VULCAN_AMMO);
					special_used = 1;
					id = POW_VULCAN_AMMO;		//set new id for making sound at end of this function
					if (obj->ctype.powerup_info.count == 0)
						used = 1;		//say used if all ammo taken
				}
			}

			break;
		}

    }
    (void)special_used; return used;
}

static int run(int engine, int native, int tagged, unsigned int real_ammo, int expected) {
    object obj = {0};
    obj.flags = tagged ? OF_COOP_RECOVERY : 0;
    obj.id = POW_VULCAN_WEAPON;
    obj.ctype.powerup_info.count = VULCAN_WEAPON_AMMO_AMOUNT;
    probe_item.gear.vulcan = real_ammo;
    native_d1 = native;
    Game_mode = 2 | GM_MULTI_COOP;
    received = 0;
    int used = engine == 1 ? d1_pickup(&obj) : d2_pickup(&obj);
    printf("engine=D%d native_d1=%d tagged=%d recorded=%u granted=%d used=%d\n", engine, native, tagged, real_ammo, received, used);
    return received == expected && used == 1;
}
int main(void) {
    if (!run(2, 0, 1, 0, 0) || !run(2, 0, 1, 10, 10)) return 1;
    if (!run(2, 1, 1, 0, 196) || !run(2, 1, 1, 10, 196)) return 2;
    if (!run(1, 1, 1, 0, 196) || !run(1, 1, 1, 10, 196)) return 3;
    if (!run(2, 1, 1, 196, 196) || !run(1, 1, 1, 196, 196)) return 4;
    if (!run(2, 1, 0, 0, 196) || !run(1, 1, 0, 0, 196)) return 5;
    puts("CONFIRMED: native D1 acquisition bypasses recovery ammo provenance; ordinary D2 and full/untagged controls pass");
    return 0;
}
```

## Menu changes and native ownership

Retain the existing completed GQR-0143 snapshot boundary. The native adapter reads private newmenu fields; shared game_menu_introspect_accessors.c supplies all six existing getters through that snapshot and the listbox title adapter. Both Android target source lists include the shared owner. No second private-layout mirror or callback bridge is needed

newmenu_activate_input_menu consolidates the three native activation sites. The Android default-name getter is active only around the save-selection menu, returns a bounded level-based string, and resets afterward. The caller allocates DESC_LENGTH+16 bytes per description and declares text_len=DESC_LENGTH-1, so the helper's terminator at text_len fits this supported producer. Keep native save-description knowledge in state.c; do not move it into launcher code

The touch-motion helper cancels taps after either axis moves at least four pixels. Press resets the cancellation flag; release clears origin coordinates but preserves cancellation for selection, outside-menu dismissal, keyboard and deferred checkbox/radio handling. Listbox storage is zero-initialized and movement requires an active press and valid origin; dragging also cancels pilot long-press tracking. Existing input-menu activation itself remains outside the drag guard; this review does not assert that every mouse-up branch is gated. The assigned activation helper extraction preserves that branch's prior condition

Interaction publishers use actual native visible-item geometry, skip text rows, bound region counts, and publish only the front window. Scroll ownership covers the menu canvas; shared publication copies stack regions while holding its lock, captures the scale, and classifies points after inverse scaling and keyboard offset. Both scaled and unscaled draws publish; close clears interactions. These compact native geometry hooks should remain with private menu state

Controller buttons/axes recurse with a key-command event through the full handler so native callbacks observe the same command. The event type ends translation recursion. Scores use the shared navigation mapping and retain the native Ctrl-R reset confirmation. The optional unscaled diagnostic draw copies menu state and disables its subfunction; the shared probe restores the canvas and frees its reference bitmap. No probe allocation-failure or callback-lifetime safety claim is made; existing BR-0345 remains separate

## Native selection boundary

Keep the compact calls into d1_in_d2_weapons.c. Availability returns -1 for ordinary D2 and a handled flag set for native D1. Cycling, auto-selection and reorder return zero when inactive; primary acquisition and order queries return negative when inactive. Each called hook has exactly one definition in the native owner. InitWeaponOrdering initializes both independent preference domains without replacing ordinary D2 ordering

Native quad selection uses logical index 16 for ranking and queued selection, while the actual inventory and select_weapon use LASER_INDEX. The quad conversion is after the existing dead-player guard and before newdemo recording; already selected lasers return without an unnecessary switch. Ammo acquisition maps the current primary to its native ranking identity. The native availability implementation handles D1 aliases and native ammo/energy requirements; it does not replace the ordinary D2 Gauss/Omega branches

The native cycle and auto-select functions retain their distinct rules. Manual cycling can pass the cutoff unless restricted; automatic best selection stops before it and skips proximity bombs. The inherited D2 best-selection change from continue to break at 255 matches that never-autoselect boundary, while preserving the existing laser fallback/no-secondary behavior. The updated D2 secondary default is a priority reorder with every old member still present exactly once. All four default order domains were checked mechanically, including D1's logical quad entry

These are native game-policy decisions and short integration calls, not duplicated Android feature implementations to extract. Moving them into a generic shared callback system would add interfaces and obscure the selection semantics

## First-pickup behavior and state lifetime

The September 16 backport plan explicitly requires the upstream names and patch structure. Its meaning is a first successful pickup of a different weapon per category per ship, even when ranking or firing policy prevents switching. Current-weapon refills and rejected duplicate/full pickups do not consume the category. Preserve this contract; do not reinterpret the feature as only one actual switch or one pickup of each weapon

Both primary and secondary suppression read the previous category flag before accepting the new pickup. Secondary suppression additionally checks current selected ammo, allowing dry-weapon fallback. Native D1 primary acquisition uses the same flag and delayed logical quad identity. Ordinary D2 keeps its super-laser distinction. The guarded pickup changes leave manual selection, empty-weapon auto-selection and the existing ammo-refill rule separate

The two declarations in weapon.h are used by native ship reset, save/rewind runtime serialization and diagnostics. The inspected gameseq reset is inside the local-player condition. Existing older-save restoration resets pickup/pending state only for a normal restore, while the shared four-integer reader can consume without applying for secret-level return. Keep these flags native; no duplicate tracking object or persistence migration is needed

Read the maintained integration test's explicit require function and ordinary runtime-roundtrip/quad call sites. It calls actual engine pickup functions and the production runtime helper, so this is not merely a source-string test and its checks do not depend on assert/NDEBUG. The historical plan records past successful host/Android builds and integrations; they are historical evidence only. No fresh test execution or full save/secret transition certification is claimed here

## Paired save and ownership review

Retain native save-format knowledge in state.c and its existing typed native/shared codec owners. The shared launcher-thumbnail extraction is still token-identical to both old native bodies after removing the old static linkage and selecting the D1/D2 render signature. Formatting differences alone are normalized; allocation checks, palette conversion, readback, canvas restoration and release order remain. This is completed historical cleanup, not a new savings claim

Both state_write_physics_info and state_read_physics_info compare exactly between engines. Four vectors are written with fixed little-endian vector helpers, while mass/drag/brakes/turnroll/flags use the save byte order. The changed vector reader matches that writer. The explicit physics disk count is four vectors, three int scalars and two short scalars. CT_MORPH uses the same AI union as its native control dispatch; the new serialization cases preserve it. Zero-initializing the player destination before copying player_rw makes omitted runtime fields deterministic; shields_certain is explicitly initialized

Retain completed GQR-0161 secret-area ownership. Identity records use their explicit byte encoding, while the old found-bit reader uses its prior scalar swap contract. Autoselect, cadence and D1 wall-blast extensions are included after the save/rewind adapter so their IO resolves to the proper stream. The readers have consume-only versus apply behavior where required. This is not a claim of whole-save atomicity or arbitrary-input safety; GQR-0175 clock admission, GQR-0191 stuck-object admission and BR-0206 restore semantics remain open

Current format constants are D1 19 for active wall blasts, ordinary D2 41 for Guidebot runtime, and imported D1-in-D2 42 for the bound asset namespace and Guidebot runtime. Cadence first appeared at D1 18 / D2 37. These current extensions are distinct from the abandoned flyout-animation history experiment; do not restore that old serializer or use its version discussion to remove live gameplay state

The save entry rejects an active death/flyout and balances its caller's pause. Restore uses a wrapper to restore window visibility and queue exit to the menu after failed world replacement. The menu request is consumed at an engine event boundary. Preflight checks cooperative metadata before level replacement; mission selection uses the saved asset key or the legacy native name. Remap uses the destination local object index, requires valid saved/live object slots and passes validity bits to the existing shared remapper. Keep these native transition points rather than passing private save state through a new callback system

Runtime and cooperative metadata application retain their ordering: core AI load, refreshed difficulty parameters, runtime state, matcen/music source, reactor/cooperative policy, gear and inventory revisions. Shared remap matches client identity and original slot, rejects double claims and preserves unmatched aggregate statistics. Source rollback validates accepted/discarded gear counts through its existing owner. D2 world-only travel deliberately preserves current party inventory/policy and skips normal absent-player replay. Existing GQR-0239 owns matcen shutdown, and GQR-0236/BR-0235 own interrupted save generation recovery; none are closed here

Restore profile timestamps are local to the operation and used only on its successful completion path. Music source restoration distinguishes mission preference from builtin music without duplicating decoder policy. The unchanged replay collision override was removed because the native cadence extension owns the clock, while the explicit Android rewind override remains. No migration is added

## D1 songs, terrain, briefing and weapon changes

The song list and playback dispatcher add matching HMQ/MIDI/WAV extensions. HMQ follows the existing HMP route; mixer-supported extensions stay under USE_SDLMIXER. Native Windows HMP opening and SDL mixer loading retain ownership. No decoder is copied into songs.c

trigger_exit_flags is a compact bounded native accessor for both authored exit bits, independent of current activation. Actual metadata, route-confirmation and exit-indicator callers use that contract. init_stuck_objects establishes the -1 wall occupancy sentinel and zero count; it does not repair the separate restored-negative-wall issue GQR-0191. Android-only branding preserves desktop identification

Terrain loading now returns success, validates the optional heightmap and coordinates, releases a failed decode, and checks the square bounded grid before replacing height_array. Its caller returns before enabling incomplete endlevel data. Paired load_terrain bodies differ only in an existing commented free/d_free line, verified mechanically. Retain the native terrain loader and shared optional-asset validator; no malformed-media probe or decoder certification was performed

Briefing layout uses the current briefing canvas consistently. The shared aspect helper derives the display correction, initializes a centered 4:3 authored-art canvas, and the robot subcanvas temporarily uses the same aspect before restoring the screen value. Draw clears the screen margins then selects the window canvas; close restores the main canvas before freeing presentation data. Native rescale_x/y already use GWIDTH/GHEIGHT. Text wrap uses line spacing, and overflow requests a new page instead of resetting and overwriting this page

Cooperative progress counts authored $P/$S boundaries only, not local layout overflow. Planning reads the selected native message sections without creating a window, the shared scanner counts authored pages, and presentation loops pump/cancel through the shared owner. Skip inputs publish skip before closing. The native text snapshot is bounded to 2048 characters in a zeroed 2049-byte destination and observes the actual private message stream. Keep the native adapter; broader shared protocol and allocation/lifetime owners require their own review. Existing BR-0345 window lifetime is not closed

Retain upstream first-pickup names and behavior as reviewed in GQ2-0182: per-category state is read before successful different-weapon acquisition updates it; secondary dry-weapon selection remains allowed. The automatic selection loop stops at 255. Removing the primary wrap at MAX_PRIMARY_WEAPONS allows the extra logical quad order entry before the cutoff, while secondary classic selection rejects the 255 marker before availability lookup. This review does not earn completion credit for D2 titles/terrain scopes

## Paired save and ownership review

Retain native save-format knowledge in state.c and its existing typed native/shared codec owners. The shared launcher-thumbnail extraction is still token-identical to both old native bodies after removing the old static linkage and selecting the D1/D2 render signature. Formatting differences alone are normalized; allocation checks, palette conversion, readback, canvas restoration and release order remain. This is completed historical cleanup, not a new savings claim

Both state_write_physics_info and state_read_physics_info compare exactly between engines. Four vectors are written with fixed little-endian vector helpers, while mass/drag/brakes/turnroll/flags use the save byte order. The changed vector reader matches that writer. The explicit physics disk count is four vectors, three int scalars and two short scalars. CT_MORPH uses the same AI union as its native control dispatch; the new serialization cases preserve it. Zero-initializing the player destination before copying player_rw makes omitted runtime fields deterministic; shields_certain is explicitly initialized

Retain completed GQR-0161 secret-area ownership. Identity records use their explicit byte encoding, while the old found-bit reader uses its prior scalar swap contract. Autoselect, cadence and D1 wall-blast extensions are included after the save/rewind adapter so their IO resolves to the proper stream. The readers have consume-only versus apply behavior where required. This is not a claim of whole-save atomicity or arbitrary-input safety; GQR-0175 clock admission, GQR-0191 stuck-object admission and BR-0206 restore semantics remain open

Current format constants are D1 19 for active wall blasts, ordinary D2 41 for Guidebot runtime, and imported D1-in-D2 42 for the bound asset namespace and Guidebot runtime. Cadence first appeared at D1 18 / D2 37. These current extensions are distinct from the abandoned flyout-animation history experiment; do not restore that old serializer or use its version discussion to remove live gameplay state

The save entry rejects an active death/flyout and balances its caller's pause. Restore uses a wrapper to restore window visibility and queue exit to the menu after failed world replacement. The menu request is consumed at an engine event boundary. Preflight checks cooperative metadata before level replacement; mission selection uses the saved asset key or the legacy native name. Remap uses the destination local object index, requires valid saved/live object slots and passes validity bits to the existing shared remapper. Keep these native transition points rather than passing private save state through a new callback system

Runtime and cooperative metadata application retain their ordering: core AI load, refreshed difficulty parameters, runtime state, matcen/music source, reactor/cooperative policy, gear and inventory revisions. Shared remap matches client identity and original slot, rejects double claims and preserves unmatched aggregate statistics. Source rollback validates accepted/discarded gear counts through its existing owner. D2 world-only travel deliberately preserves current party inventory/policy and skips normal absent-player replay. Existing GQR-0239 owns matcen shutdown, and GQR-0236/BR-0235 own interrupted save generation recovery; none are closed here

Restore profile timestamps are local to the operation and used only on its successful completion path. Music source restoration distinguishes mission preference from builtin music without duplicating decoder policy. The unchanged replay collision override was removed because the native cadence extension owns the clock, while the explicit Android rewind override remains. No migration is added

## D2-specific save ordering and presentation policy

Keep native AI, boss and trigger storage sections with their version gates and consume-without-apply behavior on secret return. Trigger writes use TRIGGER_DISK_SIZE rather than the enlarged runtime struct. D1 actor-role selection preserves native boss health, while ordinary D2 retains its existing shield correction. The widened omega time assignment preserves the runtime field width. Afterburner charge is clamped to its gameplay domain

Imported asset identity is written before the saved object array and verified after definitions are loaded but before saved references are installed. The source identity writer reports capture/write failure. Unsupported imported formats or identity mismatch request menu exit, rather than running a partly restored world. Full staging remains BR-0206; this ordering review does not claim it provides rollback

Guidebot mode is explicitly little-endian. The runtime reader uses the canonical stream schema and consume-only validation; actual apply preserves native secret-return semantics. After restore, the companion rebuild can preserve saved runtime, and routing preference/replay/cooperative overrides are applied in their established order. Headless D2 save uses a blank thumbnail rather than requiring a render context. Do not broaden that rule into the separately open headless investigation without actual caller evidence

## New GQF-0256 / GQR-0242: save failures retain the timer pause

P2/high confidence, correctness/save-lifecycle. Two added failure exits in state_save_all_sub close fp and return zero without start_time: failure of d1_in_d2_write_saved_asset_identity and failure of state_write_runtime_state (now returning escort_save_runtime status). The first writer checks capture and both record writes; Guidebot stream writes return false on incomplete IO. These are ordinary writer-error paths, requiring no malformed input or resource-pressure experiment

The desktop state_save_all caller stops time and directly returns the serializer result without a balancing call. Android slot saving likewise stops time and relies on the serializer; state_android_save_to_path cleans the staged output and metadata settings but does not release that pause. Both engines' unchanged stop_time/start_time bodies are identical and implement a nesting counter. D2 gameplay dispatch skips its simulation when the counter is nonzero, so an extra pause can leave gameplay suspended after a reported save failure or consume another owner's later unpause

The compiled probe includes the exact three exit branches plus the complete unchanged native timer functions. Unrelated save serialization is omitted; small writer/close stubs return controlled results. It proves counter behavior at those exits, not a real full save, filesystem error, device freeze or successful repair. The normal writer and close-failure paths balance; a failure before each new return leaves one extra count, including when another pause is already active. Ordinary D2 bypasses the imported-identity writer as expected

Repair the existing native save cleanup contract so every post-pause return releases exactly the save's pause once, preserving nested pauses and checked close/error reporting. Prefer a compact common exit if it simplifies the complete function; do not add a second pause counter or reset all timer state. Recheck the paired shared callers and early setup paths, but do not claim unreachable long-path branches as demonstrated defects. Prior coverage found production slot paths bounded below PATH_MAX

Validation required for implementation: maintained actual native save error injection at both writers, successful and close-error controls, initially unpaused and nested-paused cases, no false publication or stale staging, gameplay continuation after failure, paired Windows/Android builds and scoped quality. Coordinate GQR-0236 data-generation recovery without merging its different root cause. Impact 46 MEDIUM, H/M/B/C/R 23/0/6/10/7; no inherited-saving claim
