```c
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <stdint.h>
#define Assert(x) do { if (!(x)) abort(); } while (0)
typedef int64_t fix64;
static int time_paused;
static int fail_phase, native_mode, closes;
static void timer_update(void) {}
static fix64 timer_query(void) { return 0; }
static int d1_in_d2_use_d1_gameplay(void) { return native_mode; }
static int d1_in_d2_write_saved_asset_identity(void *fp) { (void)fp; return fail_phase != 1; }
static int state_write_runtime_state(void *fp) { (void)fp; return fail_phase != 2; }
static int PHYSFS_close(void *fp) { (void)fp; ++closes; return fail_phase != 3; }
void stop_time()
{
	if (time_paused==0) {
		fix64 time;
		timer_update();
		time = timer_query();
	}
	time_paused++;
}

void start_time()
{
	#ifdef __ANDROID__
	if (time_paused <= 0) {
		crash_breadcrumb_v("start_time underflow ignored at %s:%d", __FILE__, __LINE__);
		time_paused = 0;
		return;
	}
	#endif
	time_paused--;
	Assert(time_paused >= 0);
	if (time_paused==0) {
		fix64 time;
		timer_update();
		time = timer_query();
	}
}

int game_is_time_paused(void)
{
	return time_paused != 0;
}

/* Exact early exits, with unrelated serialization omitted */
static int native_save_exits(void)
{
	void *fp = NULL;
	if (d1_in_d2_use_d1_gameplay() && !d1_in_d2_write_saved_asset_identity(fp)) {
		PHYSFS_close(fp);
		return 0;
	}
	if (!state_write_runtime_state(fp)) {
		PHYSFS_close(fp);
		return 0;
	}
	if (!PHYSFS_close(fp)) {
		start_time();
		return 0;
	}
    start_time();
    return 1;
}
static void require(int result, const char *message) { if (!result) { puts(message); exit(1); } }
int main(void)
{
    int nested, phase;
    for (nested = 0; nested <= 1; ++nested) {
        for (phase = 0; phase <= 3; ++phase) {
            int result, expected;
            time_paused = nested;
            closes = 0;
            native_mode = 1;
            fail_phase = phase;
            stop_time();
            result = native_save_exits();
            expected = nested + (phase == 1 || phase == 2);
            require(result == (phase == 0), "wrong save outcome");
            require(time_paused == expected && closes == 1, "wrong cleanup observation");
            require(game_is_time_paused() == (expected != 0), "timer query disagrees");
            printf("prior_pause=%d failure=%d result=%d closes=%d remaining_pause=%d expected_balanced=%d\n", nested, phase, result, closes, time_paused, nested);
        }
    }
    native_mode = 0;
    fail_phase = 1;
    time_paused = closes = 0;
    stop_time();
    require(native_save_exits() == 1 && !time_paused && closes == 1, "ordinary D2 identity bypass");
    puts("CONFIRMED: both new writer failure exits retain the save pause; success/close failure and D2 identity bypass controls pass");
    return 0;
}
```

## Trigger semantics and native storage

Retain trigger_exit_flags as a bounded native query for both compound D1 exit action bits and ordinary D2 type semantics. Its meaning is independent of activation state. The native owner recognizes encoded source records, reconstructs source ON separately from TF_DISABLED, and returns negative when the caller should use ordinary D2 behavior. Actual activation dispatch occurs before the D2 disabled check, preserving native D1 source semantics rather than imposing D2 one-shot admission

The crossed-wall entry captures segment/side before later movement or network delivery. The shared travel entry uses those explicit coordinates; its legacy-trigger adapter supplies -1/-1, so ordinary legacy delivery cannot accidentally become a physical crossing. Native cross-trigger handling restricts native player execution and clears paired source ON for native one-shots. Route notification runs after an accepted native action; host route-planner builds retain the same hook. Broader cooperative protocol coverage remains separate

Keep d1_saved outside TRIGGER_DISK_SIZE. Editor initialization and each native record read zero the runtime extension. Bulk reads iterate native structs while reading only the disk prefix, then swap the existing scalar/array fields. Older native writers recover original source flags and link number instead of deriving a lossy single D2 action. The versioned extension remains with the native level/save owner; no new format or Android codec is needed

The D2 secret-level normal exit now enters the existing escape sequence. complete_endlevel selects ExitSecretLevelAfterFlyout or ExitSecretLevel for ordinary single-player D2 secret levels; native D1 and normal levels retain their progression. Keep that authored tunnel integration rather than reverting it to immediate return

Trigger messages use one bounded local buffer, the existing plural format and literal HUD entry; cooperative peers receive the formatted message only for local shot-triggered messages without TF_NO_MESSAGE. The existing maintained round-trip test extracts actual production functions and formats, with a simulated peer transport. Its source was inspected but not executed in this review; no network or arbitrary-packet validation is claimed. Diagnostic profiling additions remain covered by existing BR-0294 rather than a duplicate issue

## Wall behavior and adapter ownership

Android WALL_IS_DOORWAY always reaches the native function so the cooperative physical-exit gate runs before outside/no-wall fast returns. The non-Android macro is byte-identical to the frozen predecessor, verified mechanically. The function preserves the same -1/-2/no-wall classifications after the gate

wall_damage remains a live adapter: multi.c still calls it for replicated damage, while wall_hit_process supplies the actual player to wall_damage_from_player. The latter records companion-cage destruction before the blast and propagates the source through the existing door event. Removing the old entry would require changing unrelated native callers and lose the compact unknown-player contract

The native D1 door owner preserves its automatic-door first-doorway object checks, including weapons and fireballs. Source comparison against d1/main/wall.c confirms its repeated first-doorway loop is inherited behavior, not an accidental new linked-part rewrite. Ordinary D2 returns -1 and retains reopening an obstructed automatic door; native D1 returns handled blocked/unblocked status. Native wait time ignores D2's free-door condition and completed-door state preserves native opening state. Keep these game-policy distinctions in the engine. Released flare lifetime also belongs to that native owner

## Presentation resources, text and briefing ownership

The removed D1 briefing tables, robot canvas/session fields, colors and command branches are replaced by the private native session in d1_in_d2_briefing.c, adapted from native D1 titles. The D2 public briefing and ending entries dispatch before constructing a D2 session; the native owner handles D1 level-zero prelude, native ending screens and order forms. All six presentation entry hooks checked here have exactly one native definition. The D2 robot-movie path remains separate

show_title_screen appends the resolved resource into the remaining PATH_MAX buffer while retaining the release HOG-only prefix. The presentation owner distinguishes base archives from custom overrides and mounts each selected base archive under an independent prefix and synthetic archive name. Already-resolved resources retain their path through the same owner; custom overrides keep precedence. Order-form existence checks use the same resolved resource passed to display. The compact resolution helper chooses an available preferred/alternate screen without moving native asset names into Android

Text lifetime is explicitly split: the presentation owner keeps D1 text and saved D2 pointer tables, while engine text.c owns the D2 buffer and separately allocated label. Freeing native D1 text restores saved D2 pointers before returning control to the D2 frees, or clears the table and reports handled for D1-only ownership. d_free nulls its target. The ordinary D2 load records its completed pointer table, and gettext falls back to the built-in string for unavailable D2-only native strings. Keep those ownership boundaries

Briefing geometry uses the current centered authored-art canvas, including bitmap subcanvas dimensions and animation scale; draw clears screen margins then selects the window canvas. Close restores the main canvas before freeing presentation data. Native wrap/overflow now advances by line spacing and paginates instead of overwriting a full page. Authored $P/$S progress is counted once at page/screen transition; layout overflow does not invent cooperative progress. Planning loads and scans the requested native message without creating a window. Input skip and pump/cancel delegate to the existing shared session owner. The bounded text snapshot observes the private D2 stream, so retaining the small native adapter is appropriate. Existing BR-0345 remains open; this review does not certify all window-close interactions

The maintained upstream-compat source includes actual native compound-exit and selected-resource/custom-override fixtures with explicit require checks. These call sites inform the expected contracts; no fresh execution of that large integration or whole native presentation owner is claimed here

## Terrain and identity

Paired load_terrain functions compare exactly after the one historical commented free/d_free spelling change. They reject a missing/invalid optional heightmap, release failed decode data, require a bounded square grid and valid exit coordinates before replacing the live height array, and return success to the endlevel owner. Retain the compact shared optional-asset check and native decoding/terrain semantics. No malformed-media test was run. Android version branding leaves the desktop version branch intact

## Paired controls and menu changes

All 37 kconfig.c diff hunks have identical content between games after excluding only file/diff/hunk headers. Four current native adapters also compare exactly: joystick_axis_time, selection reveal, interaction publication and menu-state accessor. Retain these short adapters around private native state; shared kconfig layouts, button translation, scaling/interaction snapshots and controller command conversion already own reusable policy. Do not move the upstream control tables or create a second state facade merely to remove these call sites

joystick_axis_time preserves the legacy sensitivity/undercalibration expression and adds the independently normalized physical-controller command. The limit is chosen for the destination (half-frame pitch, frame yaw/roll, speed-factor-scaled thrust), so slide/bank modifiers use full destination travel. The shared converter clamps symmetric raw endpoints and widens multiplication to int64_t. Binding capture folds the normalized channel offset back to the legacy axis and converts amplitude to the old threshold domain; ordinary desktop event behavior is guarded unchanged. sampled_frame_time belongs to Android diagnostics

Controls-editor button translation uses stack event storage for the synchronous handler. When capturing a binding, buttons remain bindable except B, which translates to the existing cancel key. Read-only clear/default mutations remain guarded. Selection movement scrolls the selected native row into the current source crop. Interaction publication copies its stack region under the shared snapshot lock and includes the scale transform; close clears both scale and interaction state before freeing the private menu. Existing BR-0269 scaled staging and broader menu lifecycle owners remain separate

Demo-list X/Y use the existing delete/convert key actions; the displayed controller title is static because the listbox outlives select_demo. Main-menu idle publishes deferred save-transfer/briefing failures at a native event boundary. Expected exit is recorded at explicit quit. Android mode changes return before updating Game_screen_mode after failed graphics setup; desktop behavior is preserved

The autoselect option was inserted with consistent index shifts through construction, readback and live color-change callbacks. Mechanical inverse transforms remove only the added option/readback, reverse every later m/menus/ADD_CHECK/citem index, and for D2 remove its explicitly added desktop Guidebot block. Both complete functions per game then match their frozen predecessors token for token. Keep upstream backport naming and layout; no broad menu rewrite is needed. D2's desktop Original/Enhanced controls update the new-game default, with separate Android/desktop array capacities

## Mission selection, asset lifetime and native formats

read_mission_file now uses PATH_MAX with a checked prefix-plus-name concatenation and skips discovery from the currently mounted mission payload. Native load_mission preflights the requested descriptor before releasing the current mission, resolves its real path, copies native mle fields into Current_mission, then activates the prepared mount set. selected and resolved are stack-local only until their path is copied. free_begin/free_end avoid double-reset while transitioning; allocation failure releases the newly active context. Descriptor publication uses the existing typed mission catalog and four-character .msn/.mn2 extensions. This source review is not malformed-catalog certification

The shared asset owner checks ordinary mount/descriptor availability before starting teardown, detaches previous mounts before activation and restores the baseline on activation failure. Native resource reset order and parsing stay in their engine owners. Discovery suppresses mounted payload duplicates; Android name loading rejects ambiguous aliases instead of loading multiple matches. The existing desktop name loop stays unchanged. Directory mounts are paired with free_mission, and failed mission-menu callbacks release the loaded context. select_mission's one-item return continues to describe mission loading, not callback success

The two current-directory entry points have real preview and metadata callers: one supplies an explicit descriptor, while the basename adapter selects the engine extension. Keep descriptor parsing/native Mission ownership here, rather than duplicating it in JNI or Kotlin. Whole shared asset-publication and preview owners have their own coverage; this unit covers their native call contracts

## Replay and diagnostics boundary

Retain the compact shared fast-replay declaration: both SDL event dispatchers call its production definition. Level-entry player preferences are reapplied by the shared replay owner only when replay is loaded, after native progress bookkeeping can reload the pilot. Keep recording data distinct from opt-in diagnostic text. Current diagnostic/shared lifecycle findings are not automatically closed by these local changes

The maintained controller runner and its script describe actual MotionEvent-to-command integration in both games, with raw thresholds and modifiers. Source inspection is context only; it was not rerun, and it does not replace the still-open actual supported loading-stall observation in GQI-0005

## D1 level loading, HUD and startup

Keep native section offsets and format knowledge in gamesave.c. The changed header reads preserve total advancement: the old skipped words are now decoded as walls/triggers/reactor/matcen offsets. level_section_seek allows empty sections and seeks each present section independently, so editor padding need not be interpreted as data. Wall animation application now limits animation interpretation to doors/blastable walls and checks their declared domain. Texture fallback retains overlay orientation bits and records the replaced index before later consumers. Preview-only debug warning suppression does not alter ordinary gameplay warning behavior. No malformed-level probe was run

LoadLevel requests route metadata after successful native load and Current_level_num update, using copied normal/secret path lists only in eligible single-player non-record/replay sessions. Native secret-area preparation and desktop rescan remain distinct. Profiling records phase durations around existing work; it does not reorder loading. Sound trace marks the level before sound sources start. The later shared profiling owner remains separate

Local new-ship initialization resets first-pickup flags and notes recovery alive; level/editor initialization clears stuck-object state. New-game matcen mode resets through its shared owner. Cooperative flyout/endgame/briefing hooks retain native lifecycle points, rejoin disarm and join-wait restart return. Existing GQR-0239 matcen shutdown is not repaired by the reset call, and the shared cooperative protocol is not fully reviewed here

HUD life grants cap at MAX_LIVES and avoid extra-life sound/message when no life is gained. The message uses an explicit string format. The cockpit alpha path frees the derived bitmap's texture, initializes that bitmap and uploads without an incidental draw before rebuilding its subbitmaps. Energy-bar batching surrounds each group of line draws and ends before canvas changes. The Android/OGL numerical display removes only the earlier duplicate; the later call after shield drawing still renders the value. Retain font reset and compact endlevel HUD-name dispatch into the existing shared implementation. Texture binding/cache issues remain GQR-0238, not closed by this upload correction

Startup establishes LeaveEvents before a command-line replay/restore can close a game window, then resumes at the normal event loop on longjmp. A cancelled quit clears expected-exit state. Shutdown disables mission-reset callbacks before native asset teardown

D1 replay-only full-object homing acquisition was removed so it uses the same retained rendered-object list as normal play. Native primary/secondary selection guards return before indexing weapon tables and reset the actual selected slot, without changing drop-bomb selection. D1 branch-added diagnostic hooks now gate detailed replay/activity probes while retaining structured recorder events. BR-0294 remains a broader unfinished owner; no whole diagnostic closure is claimed

## Paired controls and menu changes

All 37 kconfig.c diff hunks have identical content between games after excluding only file/diff/hunk headers. Four current native adapters also compare exactly: joystick_axis_time, selection reveal, interaction publication and menu-state accessor. Retain these short adapters around private native state; shared kconfig layouts, button translation, scaling/interaction snapshots and controller command conversion already own reusable policy. Do not move the upstream control tables or create a second state facade merely to remove these call sites

joystick_axis_time preserves the legacy sensitivity/undercalibration expression and adds the independently normalized physical-controller command. The limit is chosen for the destination (half-frame pitch, frame yaw/roll, speed-factor-scaled thrust), so slide/bank modifiers use full destination travel. The shared converter clamps symmetric raw endpoints and widens multiplication to int64_t. Binding capture folds the normalized channel offset back to the legacy axis and converts amplitude to the old threshold domain; ordinary desktop event behavior is guarded unchanged. sampled_frame_time belongs to Android diagnostics

Controls-editor button translation uses stack event storage for the synchronous handler. When capturing a binding, buttons remain bindable except B, which translates to the existing cancel key. Read-only clear/default mutations remain guarded. Selection movement scrolls the selected native row into the current source crop. Interaction publication copies its stack region under the shared snapshot lock and includes the scale transform; close clears both scale and interaction state before freeing the private menu. Existing BR-0269 scaled staging and broader menu lifecycle owners remain separate

Demo-list X/Y use the existing delete/convert key actions; the displayed controller title is static because the listbox outlives select_demo. Main-menu idle publishes deferred save-transfer/briefing failures at a native event boundary. Expected exit is recorded at explicit quit. Android mode changes return before updating Game_screen_mode after failed graphics setup; desktop behavior is preserved

The autoselect option was inserted with consistent index shifts through construction, readback and live color-change callbacks. Mechanical inverse transforms remove only the added option/readback, reverse every later m/menus/ADD_CHECK/citem index, and for D2 remove its explicitly added desktop Guidebot block. Both complete functions per game then match their frozen predecessors token for token. Keep upstream backport naming and layout; no broad menu rewrite is needed. D2's desktop Original/Enhanced controls update the new-game default, with separate Android/desktop array capacities

## Mission selection, asset lifetime and native formats

read_mission_file now uses PATH_MAX with a checked prefix-plus-name concatenation and skips discovery from the currently mounted mission payload. Native load_mission preflights the requested descriptor before releasing the current mission, resolves its real path, copies native mle fields into Current_mission, then activates the prepared mount set. selected and resolved are stack-local only until their path is copied. free_begin/free_end avoid double-reset while transitioning; allocation failure releases the newly active context. Descriptor publication uses the existing typed mission catalog and four-character .msn/.mn2 extensions. This source review is not malformed-catalog certification

The shared asset owner checks ordinary mount/descriptor availability before starting teardown, detaches previous mounts before activation and restores the baseline on activation failure. Native resource reset order and parsing stay in their engine owners. Discovery suppresses mounted payload duplicates; Android name loading rejects ambiguous aliases instead of loading multiple matches. The existing desktop name loop stays unchanged. Directory mounts are paired with free_mission, and failed mission-menu callbacks release the loaded context. select_mission's one-item return continues to describe mission loading, not callback success

The two current-directory entry points have real preview and metadata callers: one supplies an explicit descriptor, while the basename adapter selects the engine extension. Keep descriptor parsing/native Mission ownership here, rather than duplicating it in JNI or Kotlin. Whole shared asset-publication and preview owners have their own coverage; this unit covers their native call contracts

## Replay and diagnostics boundary

Retain the compact shared fast-replay declaration: both SDL event dispatchers call its production definition. Level-entry player preferences are reapplied by the shared replay owner only when replay is loaded, after native progress bookkeeping can reload the pilot. Keep recording data distinct from opt-in diagnostic text. Current diagnostic/shared lifecycle findings are not automatically closed by these local changes

The maintained controller runner and its script describe actual MotionEvent-to-command integration in both games, with raw thresholds and modifiers. Source inspection is context only; it was not rerun, and it does not replace the still-open actual supported loading-stall observation in GQI-0005

## D2 native weapon and mission policy

All called d1_in_d2 weapon hooks have one definition in the native weapon owner. Negative/not-handled return conventions preserve ordinary D2 execution, with a separate -2 homing sentinel so a handled no-target result (-1) is not confused with fallback. Native D1 preserves directional projectile relation, full quad-bolt damage, fusion scaling, robot/reactor muzzle placement, impact-phase awareness, thrust-dependent speed limiting, edition-appropriate smart children and spreadfire's visible projectile record. These are game semantics, not Android implementation to extract

Native homing acquisition consumes the main-window rendered list in reverse order; complete scans retain their own type/distance/visibility rules. Retention/reacquisition and steering stay in the native owner. The D2 fallback no longer contains D1 branches once dispatch handles that game. Native orientation uses scale 8 with the original fixed-point order; ordinary D2 keeps scale 16. The ordinary D2 replay-only complete-scan branch still exists, so BR-0386 remains open despite the separate D1 correction. This review does not claim new runtime determinism evidence

Omega fire time and its runtime-state field are fix64, matching the game clock. Reset correction runs before the full-charge early return, and fire-overhead calculation ignores future fire times until the shot updates the clock. State.c saves/restores this through its existing time-delta codec, as reviewed in GQ2-0184. GQR-0175 restored-clock admission remains separate. Omega diagnostics are Android-only, check the game logging category, use wall time for throttle and keep counters out of ordinary desktop builds

Mission listing permits a D1-only data installation by checking for a D2 base archive before adding its built-in mission and initializing the optional builtin filename. load_mission_ham delegates base HAM/sound handling to piggy_load_mission_data, including embedded legacy sound headers. The native profile owner releases models when returning to D2 and defers D1 preparation to actual intro/level entry, so selecting a D1 mission does not destroy still-active models. Header comments describe that nonrecursive D2 loading service. Keep these native format/lifetime boundaries

The removed six ConsoleObject diagnostic assignments already occur in input_demo_capture_runtime_state_diag, which is called immediately before the deleted block; their exact block matches the shared source. The homing-bump environment helper was relocated, not removed, and native D1 replay exit delegates to native progression. DXX_GUIDEBOT_LIVE_ESCORT gets the same companion-velocity policy as the Android live engine

The terminal postlevel summary latches coop_endgame_released at creation; desktop initializes false. A released session permits Enter/Space/Escape and authorized Android advance, renders a terminal message and avoids ordinary next-level protocol/countdown. Pending Android advance sets end_time, which the next draw converts to close. Keep the small native window adapter; no whole cooperative endgame/lifetime certification is claimed

## Minimization candidate and owner boundary

CANDIDATE GQF-0257/GQR-0243: the reactor-pause and matcen-mode packet block is exactly identical in both multi.c files, 139 LF-normalized lines each. It is new since the GQ1 head and absent at original attribution. The block contains four local request/state constants and nine functions, of which three already have public native declarations. Moving the complete feature implementation into a narrowly scoped shared multi_gameplay_options.c/.h requires exposing only the two receive entries; the state builders, mode-name helper and broadcast helpers stay private

The implementation uses existing engine declarations for multibuf, player/master state, packet send, reactor timer/state and matcen state. It does not need a callback table, duplicated cache, source-fragment include or private transport export. Both games' common CMake source lists already build shared matcen_mode.c for desktop and Android. Add the new owner to those common lists, not inside an Android-only target block. Keep native packet IDs/length tables and dispatch ordering in the engines, including Endlevel_sequence gates. Do not put networking into the independently tested pure matcen state owner

An in-memory source draft removes the block and adds one header include per game: 138 inherited lines removed per game, 276 total. This is a prospective reduction, not an applied or compiled patch; declarations/build wiring/shared owner add code elsewhere. No claimed inherited path removal. D2 multi.c was read only for this exact paired block, declarations and dispatch/build context; its full GQ2-0191 implementation assignment remains TODO

Preserve seven-byte reactor messages, priority 2, host request routing, cooperative/active-countdown checks and countdown state values. Preserve 3 + MATCEN_MODE_MAX_CENTERS byte matcen packets, zeroed request payload, all activation counts, direct join catchup, mode domains and existing GM_MULTI eligibility. Sender/host checks and HUD calls retain their order and semantics. Matcen transport consolidation does not fix the distinct native station-index bug in GQR-0239

Required fix validation: exercise actual shared request/receive functions for host and client flows, exact valid packet bytes/recipient/priority and join state; verify paired per-game IDs and countdown/mode/count state parity. Run paired Windows and Android build/link and ordinary cooperative state-change integration, scoped quality and isolated inherited metrics. Historical reactor-pause latency tests cover event consumption; they are not an oracle for a future packet extraction

## Robot replication and native ownership

Both changed robot-drop sender bodies compare exactly (37 lines); both receiver bodies compare exactly (63 lines). Retain the inherited native creation/format integration in this review rather than broadly deduplicating old engine algorithms. The sender uses actual created-object IDs and groups up to four matching type/id entries into a 27-byte packet, with explicit little-endian position fields and -1 unused IDs. Each created object is mapped before publishing and the create queue clears after all batches. The receiver checks declared domains before creation, then maps partial successful creation even if the final allocation failed. Removed egg_objnum locals no longer suppress successfully created earlier objects. This preserves the recorded crash repair; no malformed-packet or resource-pressure probe was run

Queued robot position send now checks whether the object still exists as a living robot with a valid segment; receive validates the shortpos segment before extraction. offsetof follows the declared layout. Boss HUD changes replace activation from generic fire/teleport with explicit BOSS_ACTION_HUD_SHOT. Native collision callers publish it and the shared HUD owner validates boss type/signature and keeps the selected live boss. D2 boss gating now maps the actual nonnegative object index returned by gate_in_robot; create_gated_robot explicitly returns -1 on failure and its created index on success. D2 cloak resets native D1 boss-hit state as well as the D2 timestamp. Cooperative companion control stays with the escort owner; its new early return prevents generic robot release on a bump or weapon hit. multi_delete_controlled_robot has real escort callers

The receive counter is diagnostic and observed through introspection; it is not authoritative game state. Existing diagnostic and cooperative-authority owners remain separate. Historical SpewRecovery tests passed nine remote robot eggs, duplication-ledger parity and two rejoins in both engines; that is prior evidence from the September plan, not a fresh execution or proof of every changed path

## Ordinary investigation GQI-0008

The sender seeds 1245 once before object_create_egg creates the full drop, whereas each received four-slot batch independently seeds 1245 before creating that batch. Native drop_powerup consumes simulation RNG for each powerup's three velocity components and, for energy/shields, lifetime. More than four moving/timed powerups can therefore restart the sequence on the receiver. This source observation needs ordinary actual-engine comparison before admission as a material synchronization defect: the existing sender uses source velocity while the synthetic received source has zero velocity, an older independent difference, and robot authority updates may mask robot-egg differences

Use a supported stationary custom robot dropping a bounded nine energy or shield pickups, compare per-remote-object velocity and lifeleft immediately after creation on both peers, and include a four-item control. Trace subsequent synchronization/lifetime behavior and review packet-format constraints before choosing a fix. Existing SpewRecovery checks object counts and recovery rows, not pickup trajectories or lifetime; no fresh runtime mismatch, corruption or exploit is claimed. GQI-0008 is OPEN, not a finding or a deferred security probe

## Protocol interfaces

Keep each game's native message IDs and lengths, with Android versus desktop versions and extensions explicitly distinct. D1/D2 player drop lengths are 65/114 on Android versus 57/106 on desktop; ship status is 54/84 versus 45/70. Cooperative restore is 102 versus 86; save-begin is 44 versus 32 and ready is 12. New reactor/matcen packet definitions match their live writers. Recovery, briefing, travel and endgame retain 160/136/228/160-byte declarations. D2 door source-player, escort spawn/trigger and canonical Guidebot definitions have their own native contracts. No forced common wire schema is justified by similar names

Authenticated-sender and stamped dispatch declarations match native handlers. Shared save barrier/test entry points retain their implementations' platform boundary. GuidebotRouting is an ordinary netgame field; Android briefing/secret-warp preferences stay guarded. Moving the existing difficulty declaration outside an Android guard reflects its desktop implementation rather than adding a new feature

## D1 multiplayer and morph changes

Retain Android baseline-pass gating on newdemo morph recording; desktop recording order is unchanged. New multiplayer reset/frame hooks clear recovery/campaign/pending restore state and apply pending inventory/recovery before autosave eligibility. Travel freeze checks stop world mutations at their native entry points. Closing can remain pending until the lifecycle owner is ready; it must not clear multi_quit_game prematurely. Remote suicide no longer penalizes the local survivor

Direct sends now transmit the caller's buf rather than unrelated global multibuf, validate type before length-table lookup and reject player slots at or above MAX_PLAYERS. Preserve this concrete prior crash fix. Observer/broadcast legacy routines are not generalized by this local repair. Android reappear/drop and remove hooks publish recovery life/quantity state at their existing native mutation points; stale life drops are rejected. Delaying Net_create_loc reset preserves created IDs for recovery bookkeeping. Desktop bytes outside its transmitted packet length do not enlarge the wire format; no buffer overflow was established from those writes

Bigdata scoped dispatch reads the trailer stamp and re-reads current world identity before every submessage because a handler can replace the world. Shared fencing admits session-control messages separately, restricts recovery settlement to the same visit/level even when frozen, and requires an open matching visit for ordinary gameplay. Existing adapters retain their unstamped behavior. Score send/receive hooks respect freeze boundaries; endlevel participation is noted before the native state transition. These are local contracts, not full transport/authentication certification

Save/restore entry points block during briefing/travel/transfer activity, allow the explicitly paused reactor-countdown case and avoid announcing restore completion after native failure. Ship-status processing checks sender/player/weapon domains and uses matching restore/life/hostage fields; cooperative status uses reliable broadcast while other modes retain direct master delivery. Native engine data ownership and shared cooperative policies remain distinct. BR-0294 diagnostics, GQR-0236 save recovery and GQR-0239 matcen state remain open; this review does not close their complete shared owners

Required fix validation: exercise actual shared request/receive functions for host and client flows, exact valid packet bytes/recipient/priority and join state; verify paired per-game IDs and countdown/mode/count state parity. Run paired Windows and Android build/link and ordinary cooperative state-change integration, scoped quality and isolated inherited metrics. Historical reactor-pause latency tests cover event consumption; they are not an oracle for a future packet extraction

## Robot replication and native ownership

Both changed robot-drop sender bodies compare exactly (37 lines); both receiver bodies compare exactly (63 lines). Retain the inherited native creation/format integration in this review rather than broadly deduplicating old engine algorithms. The sender uses actual created-object IDs and groups up to four matching type/id entries into a 27-byte packet, with explicit little-endian position fields and -1 unused IDs. Each created object is mapped before publishing and the create queue clears after all batches. The receiver checks declared domains before creation, then maps partial successful creation even if the final allocation failed. Removed egg_objnum locals no longer suppress successfully created earlier objects. This preserves the recorded crash repair; no malformed-packet or resource-pressure probe was run

Queued robot position send now checks whether the object still exists as a living robot with a valid segment; receive validates the shortpos segment before extraction. offsetof follows the declared layout. Boss HUD changes replace activation from generic fire/teleport with explicit BOSS_ACTION_HUD_SHOT. Native collision callers publish it and the shared HUD owner validates boss type/signature and keeps the selected live boss. D2 boss gating now maps the actual nonnegative object index returned by gate_in_robot; create_gated_robot explicitly returns -1 on failure and its created index on success. D2 cloak resets native D1 boss-hit state as well as the D2 timestamp. Cooperative companion control stays with the escort owner; its new early return prevents generic robot release on a bump or weapon hit. multi_delete_controlled_robot has real escort callers

The receive counter is diagnostic and observed through introspection; it is not authoritative game state. Existing diagnostic and cooperative-authority owners remain separate. Historical SpewRecovery tests passed nine remote robot eggs, duplication-ledger parity and two rejoins in both engines; that is prior evidence from the September plan, not a fresh execution or proof of every changed path

## Ordinary investigation GQI-0008

The sender seeds 1245 once before object_create_egg creates the full drop, whereas each received four-slot batch independently seeds 1245 before creating that batch. Native drop_powerup consumes simulation RNG for each powerup's three velocity components and, for energy/shields, lifetime. More than four moving/timed powerups can therefore restart the sequence on the receiver. This source observation needs ordinary actual-engine comparison before admission as a material synchronization defect: the existing sender uses source velocity while the synthetic received source has zero velocity, an older independent difference, and robot authority updates may mask robot-egg differences

Use a supported stationary custom robot dropping a bounded nine energy or shield pickups, compare per-remote-object velocity and lifeleft immediately after creation on both peers, and include a four-item control. Trace subsequent synchronization/lifetime behavior and review packet-format constraints before choosing a fix. Existing SpewRecovery checks object counts and recovery rows, not pickup trajectories or lifetime; no fresh runtime mismatch, corruption or exploit is claimed. GQI-0008 is OPEN, not a finding or a deferred security probe

## Protocol interfaces

Keep each game's native message IDs and lengths, with Android versus desktop versions and extensions explicitly distinct. D1/D2 player drop lengths are 65/114 on Android versus 57/106 on desktop; ship status is 54/84 versus 45/70. Cooperative restore is 102 versus 86; save-begin is 44 versus 32 and ready is 12. New reactor/matcen packet definitions match their live writers. Recovery, briefing, travel and endgame retain 160/136/228/160-byte declarations. D2 door source-player, escort spawn/trigger and canonical Guidebot definitions have their own native contracts. No forced common wire schema is justified by similar names

Authenticated-sender and stamped dispatch declarations match native handlers. Shared save barrier/test entry points retain their implementations' platform boundary. GuidebotRouting is an ordinary netgame field; Android briefing/secret-warp preferences stay guarded. Moving the existing difficulty declaration outside an Android guard reflects its desktop implementation rather than adding a new feature

## Diff minimization and native AI ownership

RETAIN. The change removes D1 conditionals and a private helper from D2's inherited AI loop after adding actor-specific dispatch into native d1_in_d2_ai.c/.h and its path owner. These implement game behavior and belong in the engine; moving their policy into Android would violate ownership. Named context does not mark the complete added owners reviewed. The current native actor gate handles D1 enemy robots but excludes companions, so the D2 fallback still runs engine actors in D1 missions. route_confirmation_drive_companion has a running/selected-actor gate and an inert fallback implementation; remote cooperative Guidebot ownership still returns before ordinary simulation

The native frame has its own preparation, distance scheduling, boss update, behavior modes, visibility and firing. Removed D1 readiness, timeslicing, random-turn, chase/follow, gun and nearby-fire branches therefore are not evidence of deleted gameplay. The retained D2 path keeps its dual-weapon timers, awareness boost, three-edge propagation, blind-fire and thief rules. All called d1_in_d2 hooks have one current native definition. This entry-boundary review does not establish whole-engine behavioral equivalence or replay parity

The old private random-turn body matches the native helper token for token after its function rename and substituting the native turn service name. The service itself intentionally implements native D1 orientation policy; do not call this a whole-call-chain equivalence proof. The shared awareness producer matches its old complete tokens after restoring the extracted admission parameter as the original local expression, ignoring comments/whitespace. D2 supplies its old single-player/multiplayer-with-robots admission; native D1 deliberately supplies true, while observer filtering, queueing, cloak refresh, agitation and diagnostics stay in the common producer

The native awareness owner delivers four-edge propagation to native enemies and three-edge propagation to engine actors, consumes the event queue once, and selects recipient policy by actor. init_ai_objects clears old mine events before initializing objects. The native world-frame owner completes native boss death in object frames and retains engine-actor global completion, avoiding a second native death update. The 196 Ai_transition_table state entries are identical between current D1 and D2; the new typed lookup keeps the table private and provides assertions on the existing domain

## Initialization, paths and Guidebot integration

Native initialization chooses D1 behavior/mode/path rules; engine fallback retains companion/thief/attack-type initialization. Both feed the existing common physics, timers, skip state and cloak setup. Native boss initialization selects D1 geometry/interval policy, while ordinary D2 retains final-level intervals. difficulty_refresh_runtime_parameters now owns both Gate_interval and Boss_invulnerable_dot refresh; the removed assignment is present there rather than lost. Native D1 ship respawn intentionally retains cloak memory

Guidebot creation now factors native morph creation at a position, requires asset preparation success and offers a player-position entry that checks player/object/segment, copies ship orientation and returns an index or -1. The old cheat entry still uses the local segment center. Enhanced Guidebot door checks reject closed walls and non-flyable illusions even if a controlling switch exists; strategic routing handles that switch first. Native D1 door dispatch uses a distinct not-applicable sentinel and leaves companion/NULL queries in the D2 policy. New header declarations expose live path/placement services without new duplicate state. ESCORT_GOAL_RECALL extends the goal domain consistently

Two Android Guidebot traces observe retry-reset and path-cleared transitions; they do not themselves alter navigation. Removing boss HUD activation from generic attacks/teleports preserves the explicit contact/message policy already reviewed in GQ2-0189. Existing BR-0294 diagnostic gating remains a separate owner

## Native save semantics

Boss_dying_sound_playing is now an int matching the existing four-byte writer and header declaration; unused adjacent byte globals are removed. Version <35 restores deliberately retain the old signed-byte interpretation after endian decoding. The dying-frame adapter passes a local sbyte to the old helper, then updates the int only when it was zero, preserving existing nonzero saved values. Native boss-hit pending state uses explicit markers while ordinary D2 restores GameTime64 plus the saved delta; prior native damage history is cleared

The appended awareness vectors and believed/last-fired positions use PHYSFSX_readVector to match their explicit little-endian writer. Other scalar fields retain their own save-order codec; do not globally change the native format. Maintained test_upstream_compat includes actual AI writer/reader, legacy/current version and boss-sound runtime checks, but it was inspected as source only, not run here. Broader restore admission BR-0206 and restored-clock GQR-0175 remain open; no malformed-save probe was executed

## Diff minimization and paired multiplayer reconciliation

CANDIDATE reference to existing GQF-0257/GQR-0243. The whole assigned D2 multi.c delta is now reviewed, rather than only the named block used in GQ2-0165/0189. Its 139-line reactor-pause/matcen block still matches the paired immutable hash; existing 276-line total draft savings are not counted again. The new owner remains desktop-and-Android with native IDs, lengths and dispatch preserved. The remaining movie, AI format and native gameplay adapters are retained at their native ownership boundaries

Direct send validates type before table lookup, rejects out-of-range slots and uses the caller buffer. Retain this prior repair and the new light-segment guard; no malformed-network probe was run. Recovery reset/frame, life/omega drop and removal hooks mirror the reviewed D1 boundaries. The create queue stays live until recovery drop bookkeeping. Android ship status matches the 84-byte header: restore serial at 70, omega at 74, life at 78, high secondary-weapon bits at 82 and hostages at 83. Desktop retains its 70-byte wire length. Receiver checks weapon domains, afterburner range, sender identity and recovery serial/life admission before state updates

D2 local_death_pending is set before announcing death, cleared after host computation or the client's returned kill, and reset for a new game. The native travel-settlement caller waits for it before inventory reset/respawn. The travel death policy records participants and can defer CONNECT_DIED_IN_MINE while teammates are still escaping. Player activation during travel restores object form but avoids resetting the already merged inventory. Terminal campaign score exit does not restore obsolete connection state. These native hooks preserve lifecycle ordering; this is not a whole cooperative state-machine execution claim

Door packets now carry a signed source-player byte, including -1 for catchup. The cage owner consumes it only for an eligible unresolved releaser around the actual cage before wall destruction. Trigger messages send only notifications actually produced by the activating player's native trigger path; received text uses a bounded terminated local copy and literal %s formatting with callsign. Host relay is allowed by the existing sender check. The maintained trigger test exercises extracted production functions with a transport stand-in; its source was read, not executed, and it is not real UDP validation

Stamped bigdata matches the paired world-fence contract: validate the trailer, re-read current identity per handler, preserve session-control exceptions and pass the original stamp to restore inventory. Endlevel exit is noted even if local Endlevel_sequence already runs. Save/restore retains transition/busy gates, the paused-countdown exception and failure reporting before completion. Native D1 object serialization now handles CT_MORPH and CT_AI through the same owner with savegame=0; its exact native object contract covers D1 enemy robots, preserves network ownership flags, and falls back for engine actors. Save callers use savegame=1 and clear ownership separately

## Movie presentation and format ownership

Keep MVE file knowledge and private MovieHandler state in movie.c. Planning adds a video step without opening a movie; cancellation exits before playback and SysNoMovies marks the step unavailable. Full playback completes the step; an aborted flyout skips that presentation, while an ordinary skipped movie leaves following briefing pages available. The shared briefing owner only mutates progress when presenting and exposes bounded remaining time, so these small native call sites need no additional facade

Movie playback pumps cooperative state even with a pause window on top. Cancellation closes the pause before the movie; normal loop exit also retires a remaining pause. The close callback clears the tracked pause pointer. Movie state remains caller-owned until after the event loop, decoder teardown and file release; MovieHandler does not free it. Intro mouse taps remain eligible while in-game taps require the Skip action. Playback introspection traverses actual window callbacks/data and has a live shared introspection caller. Existing broader BR-0345 window lifetime work remains separate

flyout_movie_duration reads the MVE header and chunk/segment headers, takes the first timer interval, counts display-video records, bounds records/interval/duration and restores the caller's stream position. Timer opcode 2 and display opcode 7 match libmve; libmve's first timer and frame-at-a-time stepping explain the estimate. Movie frame progress advances only when not paused and publishes nonnegative remaining milliseconds. This is metadata estimation, not a second decoder. No malformed media, large-stream or resource-pressure validation is claimed

Robot movie scaling and preparation now use the current canvas dimensions (GWIDTH/GHEIGHT), matching the briefing window canvas; fullscreen movie fitting still uses screen dimensions. init_movie is private and returns the resolution actually mounted. It tries the requested library then the alternate, and the extra-robot owner records that exact filename for close. Replacement closes the previous extra library even when movies are disabled. This removes dependence on a later preference value for unmounting; it does not introduce a second resource registry

The two morph changes match D1 zero-context diff content exactly after removing location headers: only Android render-record eligibility gates newdemo morph recording. Neighboring unchanged includes differ, so a three-context-line comparison is not identical. Keep that compact native observation point. The flyout-safety runner was read as context only and includes other native/malformed-data cases; it was not run as a substitute for movie/cooperative validation

## Ownership and diff minimization

RETAIN. The private INTROSPECT_ON MDATA fixtures seed the native reliable sequence, inject the retry queue, inspect ACK state, cache game-info/sync packets and intentionally suppress selected sends. The PDATA/endlevel fixtures also call native receive paths. Extracting only the large block would export private state or require a source-fragment include; extracting the whole facility would create capture/ACK/drop interfaces for testing. This confirms the explicit September 25 retention decision, without reopening a wholesale transport extraction or claiming any new inherited savings

The small Android lifecycle, recovery, briefing, endgame, navigation, travel and world-visit hooks call existing shared owners. Native socket delivery, player-slot activation, packet layout and object serialization stay beside their engine owners. Android guards retain desktop separation except the intentional D2 native asset/Guidebot integration described below. No blanket upstream D1/D2 deduplication is proposed

## Transport, world fencing and join lifetime

The MDATA sequence fixtures exercise the old 150000 boundary and zero-skipping arithmetic, full 454-byte gameplay bodies plus the 12-byte stamp, and stale/frozen gameplay rejection while retaining session control. Their queue/ACK observations remain source evidence only; no packet fixture was executed. PDATA gating selects the exact retro/short/quaternion wire size before reading its stamp and delegates cooperative world admission to the shared fence. Packet-size dispatch accounts for the extra stamp and reliable/nonreliable header widths. A filled receive buffer diagnostic reports possible truncation, not proven truncation

Join-wait sequence requests and cancellations carry the query token and visit. The shared identity codec replaces duplicated field copies and preserves protocol/game, generation, key length/key, request counter and signature length/signature ordering. Its serialized size is 2 + 16 + 1 + 65 + 8 + 1 + 80 = 173 bytes; native headers append a further 12 bytes for query/visit. Receiver offset restoration preserves the native ADDPLAYER address read. This is static layout accounting, not authentication or interoperability certification

Join deferral checks travel, briefing and save-busy state before ordinary admission. The local reconnect-proof helper retains route selection and native direct/proxy delivery. Welcome staging records the old native and netgame connection states, and cancellation is tied to the current join attempt. The shared obsolete predicate is restricted to uncommitted transfers and detects changed visit/status or transition state; cancellation only restores previous states in the same visit. Gameplay confirmation clears the matching committed attempt

The 17-byte join envelope contains type, session token, query token and visit before the original OBJECT_DATA/SYNC payload. Wrapping requires the current target/address/attempt and a matching visit. The local stack buffer is consumed synchronously by existing send/proxy calls. Object transfer checks obsolescence before sending and waits for recovery readiness before its initial clear. Observer joins do not receive player recovery inventory. Rejoin sets its logical committed flag and stores identity before calling the void game-info sender; this review does not claim an acknowledged or failure-atomic publication boundary. Lobby removal clears the vacated native/netgame slot after shifting

Endlevel writers append per-player exit age and the shared world stamp. The score-catchup owner retains one original packet and only resends it for the matching visit/session and next ordinary level, with role/peer/state checks and a per-peer one-second interval. It does not copy old score data into a new live world. Initial-sync retry deadlines and world-visit high-water state remain in their existing shared owners; their full independent queue assignments are not credited here

## Game-info integration and ordinary static checks

Android full game-info preflight runs before parser state changes. It derives serialized offsets from the native player widths, settings, tokens, generation and visit; validates the expected host/session fields and checks stale cooperative visits using both existing and incoming modes. Native parsing then syncs or observes the visit at its existing lifecycle boundary. The writer's actual settings assignments were counted mechanically: D1 has 31 Android settings bytes, D2 has 36, with exactly two Android-only briefing/warp bytes each. D2 GuidebotRouting is setting index 29, matching shared preflight. These counts do not independently prove every native packet byte or whole-parser behavior

Test-only cached-info mutations and native stale-world fixtures remain beside parser/transport state. Their presence is not a fresh passing run and does not close security, diagnostics, restore or synchronization findings. No malformed-network, adversarial, media or resource-pressure probe was run

## D1-specific assigned boundary

The new address-to-player lookup retains the connected/nonlocal address predicate; the old Boolean service becomes a wrapper. D2 already has this lookup, so its absence from the paired diff is not a missing hook. The initialization domain is explicitly D1. Native D1 object records have no D2 asset footer

The last assigned hunks add join-envelope receive checks and constrain unwrapped OBJECT_DATA/SYNC while a join wait is active. Query/status packets keep their native role, size and route admission. Recognized-player requests enter the reconnect challenge flow before ordinary state routing. The final assigned hunk only introduces reconnect_time; the rest of that proof handler and the later UDP delta belong to GQ2-0164. Dump handling adapts a waiting join to level/endlevel changes. This review does not mark the rest of net_udp.c or the whole proof handler reviewed

## Disposition and limitations

RETAIN, with no new finding/remediation and no new inherited-saving estimate. Provisional impact rating: 0 (H/M/B/C/R = 0/0/0/0/0); proposed new owner: none. Prior private-network-fixture retention is reconfirmed. Existing deferred network extraction and open transport/diagnostic/security findings remain separate, not closed by this scope review

Evidence is assigned source review, named owner/caller tracing, paired hunk comparison, native settings-store counts and exact current/frozen identity checks. No product edits, fresh build, device/network execution or deferred adversarial/security/media/resource-pressure probes. Shared helpers and native headers are named context only, not independently completed queue units. GQI-0005 input-stall and GQI-0008 robot-drop runtime evidence, remaining GQ2 review, accepted fixes and post-frozen concurrent changes remain open

## Ownership and diff minimization

RETAIN. The private INTROSPECT_ON MDATA fixtures seed the native reliable sequence, inject the retry queue, inspect ACK state, cache game-info/sync packets and intentionally suppress selected sends. The PDATA/endlevel fixtures also call native receive paths. Extracting only the large block would export private state or require a source-fragment include; extracting the whole facility would create capture/ACK/drop interfaces for testing. This confirms the explicit September 25 retention decision, without reopening a wholesale transport extraction or claiming any new inherited savings

The small Android lifecycle, recovery, briefing, endgame, navigation, travel and world-visit hooks call existing shared owners. Native socket delivery, player-slot activation, packet layout and object serialization stay beside their engine owners. Android guards retain desktop separation except the intentional D2 native asset/Guidebot integration described below. No blanket upstream D1/D2 deduplication is proposed

## Transport, world fencing and join lifetime

The MDATA sequence fixtures exercise the old 150000 boundary and zero-skipping arithmetic, full 454-byte gameplay bodies plus the 12-byte stamp, and stale/frozen gameplay rejection while retaining session control. Their queue/ACK observations remain source evidence only; no packet fixture was executed. PDATA gating selects the exact retro/short/quaternion wire size before reading its stamp and delegates cooperative world admission to the shared fence. Packet-size dispatch accounts for the extra stamp and reliable/nonreliable header widths. A filled receive buffer diagnostic reports possible truncation, not proven truncation

Join-wait sequence requests and cancellations carry the query token and visit. The shared identity codec replaces duplicated field copies and preserves protocol/game, generation, key length/key, request counter and signature length/signature ordering. Its serialized size is 2 + 16 + 1 + 65 + 8 + 1 + 80 = 173 bytes; native headers append a further 12 bytes for query/visit. Receiver offset restoration preserves the native ADDPLAYER address read. This is static layout accounting, not authentication or interoperability certification

Join deferral checks travel, briefing and save-busy state before ordinary admission. The local reconnect-proof helper retains route selection and native direct/proxy delivery. Welcome staging records the old native and netgame connection states, and cancellation is tied to the current join attempt. The shared obsolete predicate is restricted to uncommitted transfers and detects changed visit/status or transition state; cancellation only restores previous states in the same visit. Gameplay confirmation clears the matching committed attempt

The 17-byte join envelope contains type, session token, query token and visit before the original OBJECT_DATA/SYNC payload. Wrapping requires the current target/address/attempt and a matching visit. The local stack buffer is consumed synchronously by existing send/proxy calls. Object transfer checks obsolescence before sending and waits for recovery readiness before its initial clear. Observer joins do not receive player recovery inventory. Rejoin sets its logical committed flag and stores identity before calling the void game-info sender; this review does not claim an acknowledged or failure-atomic publication boundary. Lobby removal clears the vacated native/netgame slot after shifting

Endlevel writers append per-player exit age and the shared world stamp. The score-catchup owner retains one original packet and only resends it for the matching visit/session and next ordinary level, with role/peer/state checks and a per-peer one-second interval. It does not copy old score data into a new live world. Initial-sync retry deadlines and world-visit high-water state remain in their existing shared owners; their full independent queue assignments are not credited here

## Game-info integration and ordinary static checks

Android full game-info preflight runs before parser state changes. It derives serialized offsets from the native player widths, settings, tokens, generation and visit; validates the expected host/session fields and checks stale cooperative visits using both existing and incoming modes. Native parsing then syncs or observes the visit at its existing lifecycle boundary. The writer's actual settings assignments were counted mechanically: D1 has 31 Android settings bytes, D2 has 36, with exactly two Android-only briefing/warp bytes each. D2 GuidebotRouting is setting index 29, matching shared preflight. These counts do not independently prove every native packet byte or whole-parser behavior

Test-only cached-info mutations and native stale-world fixtures remain beside parser/transport state. Their presence is not a fresh passing run and does not close security, diagnostics, restore or synchronization findings. No malformed-network, adversarial, media or resource-pressure probe was run

## D2 asset and Guidebot integration

The D2 native identity owner emits a fixed 65-byte record: ordinary D2 is zero, native D1 uses 32 or 64 digest bytes, and failed capture is represented as invalid. The checker owns identity/padding interpretation and requires the Guidebot digest when local peers will create those objects. That native format knowledge stays in d1_in_d2, not Android

Object packets add this record after the original nine-byte header, making UPID_OBJECT_HEADER_SIZE 74; clear/final count records add their native nine-byte marker. Writer capacity includes each nine-byte object record header plus object_rw. Receiver performs asset admission before native receive accounting/object mutation, scans every declared record width before processing, treats marker records separately and requires exact consumption. Native object_rw swapping passes the native-format selector. These are source-level boundaries, not executed malformed-object coverage

Full game info appends the same 65-byte identity on desktop and Android. Desktop's explicit full-size calculation includes 34 settings bytes; Android shared preflight uses 36. Guidebot routing contributes its own native byte, while briefing/warp bytes remain Android-only. Native sync asset admission precedes parser writes. The cached-info fixture includes the asset offset and Guidebot mutation, but it was not run

This assignment ends at hunk 58 after the game-info fixture/return integration. Later request handling, join-envelope receive, reliable retry and native network lifecycle changes are GQ2-0230. Do not transfer D1's wider ending boundary into D2 coverage

## Ownership and reliable transport

RETAIN. Complete later native transport deltas preserve the native queue, packet routing, player roster and game-window lifecycle. The stamped gameplay and restore/travel services remain shared feature owners. Identical native function bodies are evidence of paired behavior, not a mandate to broadly deduplicate upstream transport. The September 25 retention decision for private retry/ACK fixtures remains appropriate: the fixture observations are interleaved with queue ownership, packet caching and receive dispatch

Direct and batched Android sends allocate by explicit wire capacity, append the original world stamp and queue the complete stamped body. A pending batch flushes before its stamp changes, so one batch does not mix visits or freeze states. The reliable four-byte identity is preserved across level sync and skips the zero history sentinel. Receive validation and host relay now decode that same four-byte field rather than truncating it to a short. The cached stamp is resent unchanged; current-world validation happens downstream in stamped bigdata, retaining the actual address-derived sender for handler admission

Android normal-player retries advance a persistent modulo cursor before visiting each slot, scan at most the fixed queue size and retain the existing byte-limit break. They do not restart every pass at slot zero. Observer retries retain their separate native scan; this is not a general observer scheduling improvement claim. Retry admission retains WAITING peers only for the shared owner's exact active restore/rollback control messages, using payload length with the stamp removed. Expiry first offers a silent cooperative host to the existing host-loss owner; other native timeout behavior remains. Diagnostic fixture ACK observations do not alter ordinary ACK bookkeeping

The direct sender bypasses spectator gameplay delay for briefing/travel/endgame session-control packets. Other data retains native routing and observer delay. Endlevel forwarding checks the original stamp before delayed delivery. PDATA appends the same stamp in all three native encodings. Shape and route checks precede native history/position changes; rejected same-world frozen packets may refresh liveness and clear initial-sync/join confirmation for an already playing peer, but return before reconnect/position updates. The final native read also returns after liveness when travel owns frozen ships

## Initial sync, joins and native lifetime

Initial sync arms a finite per-peer retry window. A completed reconnect proof dispatches by current STARTING/WAITING/PLAYING state. Within the initial-sync window, PLAYING resends SYNC after updating the peer route and host metadata; otherwise normal welcome/resync applies. Valid PDATA confirms the retry slot. The maintained initial-sync test source covers reset, window endpoint, expiry and confirmation; it was inspected, not executed. Authentication and adverse-network cases are not validated by this source review

The join-wait path pumps its existing shared owner during synchronous menus, carries query/visit in cancellation, retries after a changed target and ends the shared UI on completion/failure. The failure pointer remains owned by the shared wait state: end clears activity, not the pointed-to failure text. Host-native startup resets a prior loopback binding and creates a new session generation. Removed lobby slots are disconnected, and secret travel removes nonparticipant clients before waiting for their next request

Restore polling continues reliable control traffic while the synchronous level loader is active. It reports failure without applying another save or closing Game_wind beneath the active save reader. Level sync preserves receive/retry history during restore and reserves a new visit only for a normal host-led cooperative level change. Socket flush likewise retains queued restore control messages. The shared barrier records failure/pause ownership; the native caller returns to its outer restore cleanup. This tracing does not establish the complete save-generation recovery policy, which remains GQR-0236/BR-0206 work

Native endlevel receive checks role, size, token and source before mutation, routes WAITING to score catchup and reads exit ages only after world admission. Normal frame pumping now services briefing/travel/endgame; D2 also sends endlevel state while ending the campaign. The small lobby change handles Android startup in EVENT_IDLE rather than EVENT_WINDOW_DRAW, before presentation. Controller menu adapters use the existing translated local event without retaining it; desktop menu flow is retained. Matcen/recovery extras use existing native join stages, not a second synchronization registry

## Native ping and D2-specific differences

P2P receive defers the rx_loss store until after the observer-heartbeat path and ordinary player-range check. Direct route updates exclude the host and local authoritative route. Both games' complete ping functions have equal tokens after removing comments/whitespace. This confirms paired source structure, not source authentication or a passing network test

D2 moves capture, hoard, team-hoard and bounty selection ahead of ANARCHY_ONLY_MISSION rejection. Robot modes remain behind that check; their actual native classification explains the order and does not justify replacing menu policy with a generic wrapper. Guidebot defaults use the existing routing owner. D2's added liveness, full-queue, duplicate ACK, delayed ACK, overdue retry and timeout traces are observational; existing BR-0294 diagnostic gating remains open. D2 already had the address-derived sender in the frozen base, so differing bigdata diff shapes do not mean a missing D1 counterpart

## D1 header and capacity accounting

GQ2-0164 also reviews all 14 assigned net_udp.h hunks. Android info capacity includes per-player identity plus generation and ten transition bytes; sequence capacity includes query/visit. Endlevel adds age and stamp sizes, PDATA codecs add the shared stamp and retry stores expand from 454 to 466 body bytes. Explicit Android MDATA maximum is 10 + 454 + 12 = 476 bytes, covering its reliable wire header rather than relying on local bookkeeping struct size. Desktop MDATA still uses sizeof(UDP_mdata_info)

UPID_MAX_SIZE increases from 2048 to 4096 on both platforms, with a compile-time game-info capacity check; this also changes the native half-max retry byte threshold. Do not describe all desktop behavior as unchanged. Android listen buffers add the 17-byte join envelope and use sizeof(packet) in all socket receive calls. New fixture declarations remain Android/INTROSPECT guarded; the pending-count service is Android-only. D2 net_udp.h is named context already read during early review, not an additional completed assignment in GQ2-0230

## Decision and limitations

No new finding/remediation or inherited-saving estimate. RETAIN with existing BR-0294 and save/restore owners left open. Provisional impact rating: 0 (H/M/B/C/R = 0/0/0/0/0); proposed new owner: none. Packet handling, private queues and native lifetime do not gain a simpler boundary from a new facade

Evidence is complete assigned diff reading, exact paired-hunk matching, six complete native function token comparisons and named shared/native context. No product changes, fresh full build, device/network execution or deferred adversarial/security/media/resource-pressure probe. Existing fixture source is not a passing run. Whole added-owner review, GQI-0005/GQI-0008 ordinary runtime evidence, accepted fixes and post-frozen concurrent changes remain required
