## Ownership and reliable transport

RETAIN. Complete later native transport deltas preserve the native queue, packet routing, player roster and game-window lifecycle. The stamped gameplay and restore/travel services remain shared feature owners. Identical native function bodies are evidence of paired behavior, not a mandate to broadly deduplicate upstream transport. The September 25 retention decision for private retry/ACK fixtures remains appropriate: the fixture observations are interleaved with queue ownership, packet caching and receive dispatch

Direct and batched Android sends allocate by explicit wire capacity, append the original world stamp and queue the complete stamped body. A pending batch flushes before its stamp changes, so one batch does not mix visits or freeze states. The reliable four-byte identity is preserved across level sync and skips the zero history sentinel. Receive validation and host relay now decode that same four-byte field rather than truncating it to a short. The cached stamp is resent unchanged; current-world validation happens downstream in stamped bigdata, retaining the actual address-derived sender for handler admission

Android normal-player retries advance a persistent modulo cursor before visiting each slot, scan at most the fixed queue size and retain the existing byte-limit break. They do not restart every pass at slot zero. Observer retries retain their separate native scan; this is not a general observer scheduling improvement claim. Retry admission retains WAITING peers only for the shared owner's exact active restore/rollback control messages, using payload length with the stamp removed. Expiry first offers a silent cooperative host to the existing host-loss owner; other native timeout behavior remains. Diagnostic fixture ACK observations do not alter ordinary ACK bookkeeping

The direct sender bypasses spectator gameplay delay for briefing/travel/endgame session-control packets. Other data retains native routing and observer delay. Endlevel forwarding checks the original stamp before delayed delivery. PDATA appends the same stamp in all three native encodings. Shape and route checks precede native history/position changes; rejected same-world frozen packets may refresh liveness and clear initial-sync/join confirmation for an already playing peer, but return before reconnect/position updates. The final native read also returns after liveness when travel owns frozen ships

## Initial sync, joins and native lifetime

Initial sync arms a finite per-peer retry window. A completed reconnect proof dispatches by current STARTING/WAITING/PLAYING state. Within the initial-sync window, PLAYING resends SYNC after updating the peer route and host metadata; otherwise normal welcome/resync applies. Valid PDATA confirms the retry slot. The maintained initial-sync test source covers reset, window endpoint, expiry and confirmation; it was inspected, not executed. Authentication and adverse-network cases are not validated by this source review

The join-wait path pumps its existing shared owner during synchronous menus, carries query/visit in cancellation, retries after a changed target and ends the shared UI on completion/failure. The failure pointer remains owned by the shared wait state: end clears activity, not the pointed-to failure text. Host-native startup resets a prior loopback binding and creates a new session generation. Removed lobby slots are disconnected, and secret travel removes nonparticipant clients before waiting for their next request

Restore polling continues reliable control traffic while the synchronous level loader is active. It reports failure without applying another save or closing Game_wind beneath the active save reader. Level sync preserves receive/retry history during restore and reserves a new visit only for a normal host-led cooperative level change. Socket flush likewise retains queued restore control messages. The shared barrier records failure/pause ownership; the native caller returns to its outer restore cleanup. This tracing does not establish the complete save-generation recovery policy, which remains GQR-0236/BR-0206 work

Native endlevel receive checks role, size, token and source before mutation, routes WAITING to score catchup and reads exit ages only after world admission. Normal frame pumping now services briefing/travel/endgame; D2 also sends endlevel state while ending the campaign. The small lobby change handles Android startup in EVENT_IDLE rather than EVENT_WINDOW_DRAW, before presentation. Controller menu adapters use the existing translated local event without retaining it; desktop menu flow is retained. Matcen/recovery extras use existing native join stages, not a second synchronization registry

## Native ping and D2-specific differences

P2P receive defers the rx_loss store until after the observer-heartbeat path and ordinary player-range check. Direct route updates exclude the host and local authoritative route. Both games' complete ping functions have equal tokens after removing comments/whitespace. This confirms paired source structure, not source authentication or a passing network test

D2 moves capture, hoard, team-hoard and bounty selection ahead of ANARCHY_ONLY_MISSION rejection. Robot modes remain behind that check; their actual native classification explains the order and does not justify replacing menu policy with a generic wrapper. Guidebot defaults use the existing routing owner. D2's added liveness, full-queue, duplicate ACK, delayed ACK, overdue retry and timeout traces are observational; existing BR-0294 diagnostic gating remains open. D2 already had the address-derived sender in the frozen base, so differing bigdata diff shapes do not mean a missing D1 counterpart

## D1 header and capacity accounting

GQ2-0164 also reviews all 14 assigned net_udp.h hunks. Android info capacity includes per-player identity plus generation and ten transition bytes; sequence capacity includes query/visit. Endlevel adds age and stamp sizes, PDATA codecs add the shared stamp and retry stores expand from 454 to 466 body bytes. Explicit Android MDATA maximum is 10 + 454 + 12 = 476 bytes, covering its reliable wire header rather than relying on local bookkeeping struct size. Desktop MDATA still uses sizeof(UDP_mdata_info)

UPID_MAX_SIZE increases from 2048 to 4096 on both platforms, with a compile-time game-info capacity check; this also changes the native half-max retry byte threshold. Do not describe all desktop behavior as unchanged. Android listen buffers add the 17-byte join envelope and use sizeof(packet) in all socket receive calls. New fixture declarations remain Android/INTROSPECT guarded; the pending-count service is Android-only. D2 net_udp.h is named context already read during early review, not an additional completed assignment in GQ2-0230

## Native AI interface ownership

RETAIN. All 119 header lines declare native D1 actor services at existing simulation, path, damage and save boundaries. All 42 declarations have one native definition. The actor-role API explicitly keeps companions in engine policy; path dispatch distinguishes -2 not-applicable from -1 failure and 0 success, while the separate door contract uses -1 not-applicable. The header documents the version-36 native static AI record threshold separately from the later current save version. Object writing distinguishes network and saved-game ownership; saved local timers, boss hit/damage state and actor frame/path operations stay in native owners. Earlier GQ2-0190/0191 reviewed callers and selected implementations. This header assignment and definition inventory do not complete those added implementation files or prove every documented no-mutation/RNG contract

## Asset identity and existing source-generation finding

RETAIN the native 164-line identity owner. Base hashing uses an explicit schema and length-delimited PIG/palette streams; custom hashing includes the base digest and ordered PG1/DTX/HX1 presence markers and bytes; Guidebot hashing includes its schema, sample rate, source stream lengths/bytes and the deterministic mapping table. hash_word writes explicit little-endian bytes independently of host byte order. Required missing reads fail, optional absence has an explicit zero marker, and stream read/close failure prevents successful digest return

Capture returns a 32-byte native definition digest or 64 bytes with companion identity. Save/demo checks deliberately allow a 32-byte recording to remain usable when optional companion assets later become available; a saved 64-byte identity requires them. Network records instead require symmetric optional availability because each peer may create objects. Their fixed 65-byte record includes length and zero padding, and ordinary D2 uses a zero record. Failed native capture writes the invalid 255 length marker rather than silently identifying ordinary D2

The saved identity adapter uses the existing rewind-file compatibility layer: a native integer length followed by digest bytes, explicit swapped-length handling and checked reads/writes. Native save format eligibility requires the current imported namespace versions; it is not an Android persistence migration. Earlier native save-pause GQR-0242 stays separate from these helpers' correct status returns

Existing GQF-0212/GQR-0198 remains live. The base generation decodes through its PIG descriptor and separate bitmap loader, then reopens source paths for hashing; custom PG1/DTX/HX1 decoders likewise run before the hash pass. Guidebot registration/palette conversion also precedes its path-based hash pass. These named callers confirm that this hash owner alone cannot bind identity to the exact decoded source generation. The accepted remediation already explicitly includes base, custom and optional sources; no duplicate finding or new race/resource probe is admitted here

## Classic-demo identity and event interpretation

Native D1 recordings use game type 4/version 16 and emit a level plus 32/64-byte identity before the first viewer/render/morph object in every frame. Frame/level boundaries clear identity state; object decoding requires successful identity admission before native table indexing. The reader binds the correct level's definitions before checking identity, including backwards entry into a preceding level's last frame. Dump and endian-rewrite paths load native definitions without ordinary presentation. Native header admission checks mission namespace rather than guessing from a D2-compatible version byte; diagnostics retain the native asset error

The trigger reader treats SECRET_THINGY as an optional following event. It reads its truth value when present and otherwise seeks back so the next event is decoded normally. Rewrite preserves the tag/payload exactly once and skips trigger execution. Normal playback checks segment/side/object/wall/trigger domains, and a D2 secret exit without a recorded status is treated as a rejected crossing. Native D1 exits do not require that D2-only status. These branches avoid consulting unbound trigger tables just to decide which bytes follow; malformed-demo probes are deferred

Playback now checks whether seek/start operations retired playback before continuing, and stop clears infile and restores menus when no game window exists. Dump cleanup closes input only if this invocation actually opened it. Caller-owned mounts are reused without being retired; their logical source is checked against the requested mounted directory. Newly acquired mounts are removed only by their owner. The local PhysicsFS API describes exact mounted-path spelling, so this is not a claim that arbitrary path aliases identify the same mount

Endian rewrite publishes only after decode reaches EOF without a bad read and written byte counts agree. Existing backups are preserved; rename failures report incomplete conversion and attempt restoration. These are retained improvements, not complete transactional publication proof: close and rollback outcomes are not all propagated here. Existing BR-0233 output-integrity work remains open. Completed BR-0370 source/output alias and BR-0389 wall-record repairs are not reopened by this review

The maintained classic-trigger runner includes native trigger, asset-identity mission and actual console-export scenarios. Its source was inspected, not executed. No fresh classic-demo compatibility, rewind, filesystem-failure or engine-run result is claimed

## Menu input, drawing and interaction ownership

Android tap cancellation now observes either-axis movement from the press point with a four-pixel threshold, including non-scrolling menus and listboxes. Button release preserves drag_happened for the activation check; the next press resets it. Dragging a pilot list also clears its hold action. Existing scrolling still owns vertical scroll state. Controller page buttons and translated axis keys reenter the full handler so native subfunctions receive the translated key before ordinary key dispatch; they cannot recurse into the joystick case because the event type is KEY_COMMAND

The shared input-menu activation helper keeps three native entry points consistent. Empty Android save slots can receive the existing default-save-name owner, bounded by text_len with a terminator; nonempty slots retain whitespace stripping. It preserves desktop empty-string behavior. The completed shared introspection accessors retain a compact native snapshot adapter with Android wrapped/original-item fields and desktop defaults

Menu/listbox draw publishes at most 64 regions for visible selectable items, plus an optional scroll-owned region. Newmenu geometry temporarily uses the window canvas and restores the previous canvas before publication. Level-complete presentation clears the interaction view; only front-window owners publish and closing clears it. Shared publication synchronously copies regions under its existing lock, so native stack arrays are not retained. This context does not complete the separate shared snapshot/lifecycle assignment or prove all overlapping-window timing

D1 presentation resource routing uses the existing native resolver, which preserves custom source precedence and selects base namespace resources. Menu background reload handles a retired GL handle before naming/loading the replacement texture. The unscaled diagnostic draw copies the menu and removes its subfunction. Existing BR-0294 logging, BR-0345 window lifetime and GQR-0238 GL binding coherence stay separately owned; these hooks do not close them

## Diff minimization and native progression

RETAIN. Native level sequencing, secret save/restore, asset selection and HUD geometry remain engine knowledge. New cooperative/recovery/briefing/profile calls use existing shared owners; another facade would obscure call order without removing an independent policy. The Guidebot extension header is branch-added, not an original-file saving opportunity. No new extraction or correctness finding is admitted

The extracted ammo/energy helper matches the previous complete function tokens after changing its signature to accept player *p and replacing Players[Player_num]. with p->. The public wrapper preserves the original local-player entry. Normal-level resource reset then centralizes key/cloak/invulnerability/map clearing and multiplayer keys. Cooperative advance credits and clears hostages, records last_score, applies that reset to each playing participant and updates object shields/network flags; only the local ship resets weapon timers. Its shared caller invokes it after campaign commit, so aborted travel does not consume the original cargo through this hook

New-ship hooks publish recovery/travel reappearance after native stats initialization and reset first-pickup masks. Native D1 finish-level/death dispatch owns its distinct score/advance behavior and returns handled before D2 secret rules. The shared D1 bonus owner preserves native difficulty-based shield/energy rewards while the fallback retains D2 mine-level arithmetic. Ordinary D2 secret initialization resets per-mine counts and onboard hostages separately from the saved parent mine

The private secret-exit helper distinguishes a normal exit, which may save the current secret, from completed flyout, which already saved the mine before changing pose/control state. The actual endlevel caller selects the latter only for the recorded secret flyout case. Cooperative secret death retains ordinary drop/respawn while an intact mine exists. Terminal secret travel credits onboard hostages once by clearing the field before DoEndGame; briefing/endgame owners gate shared presentation. These local traces do not close GQR-0236/BR-0206 save-generation/restore or BR-0345 window lifetime work

## Level load and replay boundaries

Native D1 assets are prepared before loading/verifying level objects. Ordinary D2 clears prior robot replacements first, then loads its level replacements through the factored file helper. The helper is also used by preview callers and verifies existing robot objects after replacement. Native assets return their ship radius without applying D2 robot replacement files. Android captures the base switch-projectile radius before replacement and restores that metadata override afterward. This retains native format knowledge rather than duplicating it in preview or JNI code

Android secret metadata preparation now follows robot/asset loading. Route metadata is requested only for ordinary single-player/cooperative use without input-demo recording/replay, as the existing escort-owner predicate specifies. Mission filenames and secret-entry arrays are assembled from native state; the JNI owner immediately creates Java strings/arrays and does not retain these stack arrays. This is a lifetime observation, not JNI failure-path validation. Desktop continues its native rescan

Level-load and initialization timing samples use native monotonic phase boundaries under Android guards. They observe loading, presentation, replacements, metadata, textures, network and sound/music without changing native simulation time. The caller preserves actual requested/current level and subtracts separately measured sync from post-load time. Existing BR-0294 diagnostic gating remains separately owned

New game resets matcen state and selects the Guidebot routing session. StartNewLevelSub retires recovery state, applies recorded player configuration and disarms briefing for rejoin. ShowLevelIntro does not consume a replay skip while cooperative presentation owns the intro; native intro assets are prepared through the native owner. StartNewLevel returns on join restart before running the shared briefing. These are source ordering checks, not fresh replay/network execution or whole shared-owner review

## Gauges and health ownership

HUD bitmap scaling now uses the installed native D1 cockpit resolution, falling back to ordinary D2 HIRESMODE. It chooses the smaller screen-axis scale, preserving bitmap aspect in keys, lives and bitmap reticles; non-OGL retains native values. D1 cockpit drawing/window canvases dispatch through its native owner. The old special-case reticle size at one screen center is removed rather than replaced with another resolution exception

Score and bonus life grants clamp to MAX_LIVES, and only play the extra-life notification when the count changes. Gauge dispatch returns immediately when native assets are inactive. It sets canvas/font, clamps displayed negative shields, preserves demo energy/shield/flag notifications and selects full-cockpit versus status-bar drawing. Android/OGL suppresses the earlier duplicate numerical draw, leaving the later common draw. The competitive score branch's duplicated show-score call also exists in inherited D1/D2 presentation; no generic scoreboard extraction is justified by this small copied structure

## Resource and caller ownership

close_cockpit frees each of the two sub-bitmap descriptors and clears it, releases the decoded GL texture, clears the decoded bitmap and resets the source/dimension cache. Named alpha-decoder context owns CPU pixels in a static 1024x1024 array, so close does not omit a heap-pixel free. reset additionally clears old weapon selection, fade state and invulnerability frame. Native asset release calls close before releasing source assets; gauges init/close calls the native reset/close services as well

Window canvas selection uses the native full/status gauge box and inclusive dimensions. Its drawing caller receives literal 0/1 window indices or the gamerend w=0..1 loop. The classic-demo null-viewer path does not reach the native canvas call; malformed demo index handling remains outside this ordinary review. Native window geometry is selected before drawing and the existing shared rendering path owns the resulting subcanvas

Cockpit initialization handles full, status and rear layouts; software mode restrictions return to fullscreen when native bitmap resolution cannot be used. Fullscreen/letterbox use the existing shared fallback. Rear view uses the asset's transparent rectangle. Draw selects the same installed-asset resolution and status height as initialization. Unsupported native draw modes return handled without painting a cockpit. Header declarations have native implementations and introduce no duplicate lifecycle owner

Existing GL binding/batching/diagnostic findings stay separately open. This source review does not claim actual GLES rendering, software pixel parity, allocation-failure execution or full remaining cockpit-file coverage

Mixer output rate zero preserves source samples. Plain SDL output validates nonempty samples and computes rounded durations with a nonempty minimum; conversion allocates a new arena, copies by source-rate index and only then releases the original arena. Equal-rate preparation returns without allocation. The active generation retains bitmap pixels, while SoundBits takes the sample arena and Polygon_models takes model_data. Each transferred ownership pointer is cleared in its prepared source. Release clears matching GameBitmaps data references before freeing generation-owned images; previously transferred model/sample buffers are released by their normal engine owners. ## Custom generation and native semantics

RETAIN. All 527 d1_custom.c lines, all 14 internal AI header lines and both assigned one-hunk changes were read. PG1 then DTX then HX1 apply only to an unpublished generation; a failure makes the caller discard the entire generation. The actual facade frees it on custom/publication failure. No restoration cache or live-table mutation is needed during parsing

HX1 reuses the existing HXM disk reader, then explicitly disables D2-only robot fields and retains the native invalid-primary-weapon fallback. Named D1 custom-reader context consumes but ignores those D2-only fields. Robot/model/joint/object-bitmap replacements are checked together before publication, including references from robots whose own records did not change. Replaced model storage is released, serialized pointer bytes are cleared, and newly owned bytes remain attached to the unpublished generation for cleanup

Custom bitmap parsing retains separate 17-byte PIG1 and 18-byte POG layouts rather than inferring a common serialized struct. DPOG uses its explicit source IDs regardless of descriptive names. PPIG and older formats resolve names against the prepared source generation, without consulting the live D2 registry. Unknown named entries are counted and skipped. Resolved bitmap bytes are staged before commit; the bounded RLE validator remains the existing owner of encoded-row admission, with unsupported large-row encoding rejected

Sound replacements are resolved by prepared source names and staged separately. The packer selects the last duplicate replacement per source slot, allocates a complete replacement arena and retains untouched samples. Bitmap entries commit in source order, with ownership cleared from staging after transfer; therefore later duplicate targets replace earlier ones without retaining their buffers. Both file cleanup and generation cleanup have explicit owners. PG1 precedes DTX, so later DTX overrides are preserved. Maintained source fixtures assert valid layout variants, source namespace independence, duplicate sound precedence and custom-to-stock retirement; these are inspected assertions, not new runtime passes

Custom source hashing runs after successful PG1/DTX/HX1 preparation and reopens the three names. Existing GQF-0212/GQR-0198 owns absent/present and decode/hash coherence; generation staging alone does not close it. Existing completed BR-0375 source-index precedence and BR-0376 bounded RLE remain completed. Their old hybrid D1-to-D2 mapping is now superseded by native source-index publication, not a reason to restore raw live-D2 lookup

The old d2/main/d1_in_d2.h is a deleted branch-added facade, not an inherited-original saving. ## Save translation and native ownership

RETAIN. All 54 assigned translation implementation hunks, the complete R100 header relocation, four digiobj hunks and two DXA diagnostic hunks were reviewed. Native checkpoint structure and restore semantics belong in the engine; moving them to an Android/shared schema would create a second format owner. The renamed implementation is R081 and its header is byte-equivalent after newline normalization

Version acceptance remains native D1 15 through 19. Version 16 adds secret identities, 17 autoselect state, 18 cadence and 19 exploding walls. Named D1 state writer context emits the same trailer order. Appended runtime vectors use the explicit little-endian vector reader, while raw scalar save fields retain the checkpoint's byte-order setting. These gates are distinct from ordinary D2/native-D1-in-D2 save versions and should not be replaced by a single global version assumption

The translator now preserves native AI SUBMODE, full short path index, saved follow-path endpoints, local wait/see/attack clocks and boss hit/dying-sound state instead of dropping or narrowing them. CT_MORPH retains AI fields as well. Ghost validation distinguishes hidden inert reactor ghosts from player-slot ghosts. Restored reactor gun caches are rebuilt from the restored pose, and boss health/physics remain saved native values rather than D2 difficulty-adjusted defaults

Trigger decoding delegates to the existing native trigger owner with its complete source record. Level texture references delegate to native texture policy. World state restores Automap_visited using the native minimum-or-large-mine length and resets the reactor pause. These are format/semantic hooks, not duplicated platform parsing

## Runtime fidelity and commit boundary

Weapon creation frame and prior-hit maps, morph vectors/deltas/timing/control/physics, occupied stuck records, reactor silence and effect state are decoded into unpublished object/runtime storage. Morph validation binds object identity/signature and model substructure; its pointer is rebound to live Objects only after commit. The commit initializes morphs first, so omitted entries do not retain the previous session's morph pointers. Effects reset to the saved loop epoch, apply saved mutable fields while retaining definition flags and then apply bitmap state

The stuck reader accepts -1 as inactive and rejects all other negative walls before live publication. GQR-0191's translator follow-up is therefore resolved as source evidence; its separate paired native footer-reader defect remains open. The serialized occupied count is consumed while the actual active count is reconstructed, preserving native behavior for stale inactive records

Secret state uses the current identity decoder/adaptor or reconstructs older found state from automap. Missing old autoselect state starts with no delayed choice; missing cadence is zeroed; missing exploding walls use inactive segnum -1. Current tails use their shared codecs. All object/world/AI/runtime validation precedes reset_objects and table commit, and each failure frees the prepared allocations. This local staging does not close whole-restore BR-0206/GQR-0236 or broader restored-clock GQR-0175 work

Maintained source tests compare actual native checkpoint dynamic state after import and after importing a legacy save without cadence, then reimport current cadence. They were inspected, not executed. No malformed-checkpoint probes were run in this review

## Sound and diagnostics

Forward sound translation rejects negative IDs before routing extended logical IDs to the optional native generation. Reverse translation tries that generation before the original native lookup; the extension owner handles its own absent/sentinel/range policy. Retain the small dispatch hooks instead of making digiobj mirror optional source mappings

DXA metadata adds Android-only asset-open tracing immediately after a successful open. The PIG/HAM diagnostic additions are separately retained under existing BR-0294. No fresh logging-performance or audio execution claim is made

## Object, rendering and death lifecycle

RETAIN. All 82 assigned inherited hunks were read: object.c 34, object.h 3, physics.c 7, physics.h 1 and piggy.c 1-37. The previously completed GQ2-0177 owns PIG hunk 38. These two exact disjoint hunk ranges cover the full 38-hunk PIG delta without granting whole-file credit to either earlier contextual read

Native hooks select source orientation/fireball sizing, actor-role camera wake, rotation/impact/bounce policy and homing configuration. Native enemy behavior is separated from optional engine-actor Guidebot behavior; this is more precise than the removed whole-game camera/physics exclusions. The physical forcefield query now trusts installed native texture flags. Existing standalone native implementation scopes retain full policy coverage responsibility

Render_object omits flyout peers drawn by their cinematic track, records CPU-only visibility without GPU drawing and gates demo object records to the owning render pass. The removed NDEBUG declaration guard makes the model pointer available to the existing Android release Assert expression, which still evaluates its argument; it does not add a new logging call. These changes preserve the existing CPU/gameplay versus presentation separation

The player-death observer is exactly equal to D1's function, exposing native state without taking over the death sequence. The clock is file-local so observation and travel settlement can use it, and each new death explicitly resets it. Cosmetic death-camera avoidance consumes FX RNG. Deleting the active reactor slot clears its effect reference before reuse

Android cooperative travel settlement uses native death/drop/respawn operations: pending network death and camera readiness defer completion; eggs drop once with the existing cap/message path; cargo clears and new-ship state precedes StartLevel. It deliberately avoids DoPlayerDead advancing a destroyed mine while the caller owns a pause. Its actual shared travel caller consumes the return status. Keep this private native lifecycle access rather than exporting a general death-state mutator. Recovery expiry and ship-status hooks retain their existing shared owners

The packed object adds native AI storage and format-aware swap dispatch. Network callers opt into the current format; save readers pass the stored-version predicate. turnroll and model animation angles use SWAPSHORT consistent with their int16_t fixang types. This is source/type/caller verification, not a fresh cross-endian engine execution

## PIG registry, sounds and semantic bitmap flags

PIG-backed bitmap flags come from stored file metadata, whereas resident replacements use their own live flags. Registry initialization is factored from properties_init so native generations can rebuild the registry without reading ordinary HAM data. Reset releases the prior assets, clears registry/cache/name state, rearms embedded sound header loading and initializes the fallback bitmap. Android table reset also rearms that one-shot; ordinary desktop and Android shared reset use the same registry owner

HAM rereading frees prior model allocations on the Android path. Sound headers record source bit depth/rate. A missing selected S11/S22 bank can select the other bank, update the chosen sample rate, and reopen the plain device backend where necessary. The source directory follows the successfully selected name; piggy_read_sounds opens DEFAULT_SNDFILE under that updated selection. Embedded demo sound headers are now resettable and samples are read for a fresh registry. This narrows the old BR-0377 scenario at source level but does not close its complete supported-edition transition validation

The semantic bitmap flag reader does not page textures or modify POG/render ownership. Native D1 asks its active generation; ordinary D2 reads base PIG headers then explicit POG overrides. Its secret-area caller stores a completeness result and initializes per-texture facts before scanning. Incomplete metadata remains an explicit input to that caller rather than a renderer side effect

The deleted PIG-local D1 header/palette/map helpers have native owners. Five complete relocated functions compare exactly after removing only the new static qualifier where present. The common bitmap decoder additionally supports prepared native source palettes and separate Mac handling, so no whole-decoder equality is asserted. Its already completed bounds work and GQR-0244 unused-frame-entry cleanup remain separate. Existing diagnostic, GL-binding and save-generation findings remain open; no new finding or extraction saving is admitted

## Session facade and native interfaces

RETAIN. All 351 assigned session/weapons implementation/header lines and nine validator changed hunks were read. All 22 facade and 27 weapons declarations have exactly one native definition. This validates interface ownership, not each implementation's complete behavior. Existing native implementation queue scopes remain independent

The facade distinguishes requested content from the committed profile. Mission descriptors or startup selection request D1, while successful asset publication commits D1 and completed D2 loading commits D2. Queries use the committed profile until release clears it. This prevents merely selecting a different mission from changing the currently installed actor/asset semantics

Startup selects the appropriate HOG/PIG availability while preserving loose/mission precedence. Base restoration runs the existing native data initializer, clears palette selection caches and activates presentation. A writable palette-name copy is deliberate because the old path splitter temporarily edits the name. Keep this native knowledge out of Android reset code

Preparation builds a base generation, applies custom level changes, prepares the optional Guidebot extension and publishes before activating presentation. Failures dispose of unpublished storage. D1-to-D1 mission selection defers installation until intro/level preparation; leaving D1 stops audio users, releases cached sound/xmodels/models/extra images, resets the registry and reloads ordinary D2 mission definitions. D2 model reload does not recurse into profile preparation. Release resets native boss/cockpit state before freeing data and clearing the committed profile

The weapons header's negative/handled sentinel contracts distinguish native selection, quad logical indices, collision policy and homing operations from D2 fallback. Its small native typed interface avoids copying player/weapon layout into shared platform code. No extra facade, registry or generic callback mechanism is justified

## Relocated model validation

The validation implementation/header are verified R088/R089 renames. The added texture-count parameter is propagated through both sort branches and subcalls of the existing bounded walker. Textured polygons and rod bitmaps validate their texture references when a nonnegative texture count is supplied; the existing structural entry passes -1 to preserve its original structural-only purpose. The new entry rejects negative requested counts and uses the same bounded traversal budget

Named asset-owner context calls texture validation for model substreams before native publication. The distinct structural versus texture entry points share one walker rather than duplicating parsing. Completed BR-0365 remains completed. This is static ordinary ownership/compatibility review; malformed model and resource-pressure probing remains deferred

## Native flyout integration

RETAIN. All 87 endlevel hunks, the full 62-line goal-policy header, four owner-policy implementation/header hunks and only escort.c hunks 1-9 were reviewed. The large later escort implementation changes are not part of this unit and remain separate queue work

The movie filename helper is shared by playback and metadata callers, preserving no-movie selection for shareware, nonpositive/out-of-range levels and the ordinary registered final level. Completion distinguishes ordinary level finish from D2 secret return. Animated secret exit saves revisitable state before cinematic movement and uses the existing after-flyout return so it does not save the changed cinematic pose again. Existing complete-save/restore and window lifetime owners remain open

Android cooperative presentation sends the existing exit notification and enters the shared flyout owner once. Its presentation callback reenters native setup only while the owner is active, suppressing recursive entry and native completion. finish_endlevel defers gameplay completion until that owner returns. Game-window visibility remains with the cooperative presentation owner during playback. The outside camera remains live while the peer barrier completes; no new network integration pass is claimed

Native animation validates the exit route before moving the player and binds scenery to the opening actually reached. A missing exterior exit or optional scenery leaves animation unavailable, letting the existing completion fallback run. The shared description parser stages all eight fields before native bitmap/terrain installation; data_loaded is cleared first and set only after complete setup. Source direction vectors are retained separately from positioned scenery, so rebinding another exit does not rotate an already positioned location

Transient frame counters and both local fly records reset per sequence. Camera transition detection is latched across substeps. Slow frames consume their entire cinematic movement interval in steps no larger than F1_0/60 after initialization; simulation/world/FX RNG updates remain at their existing frame boundary. Four complete native flythrough/scenery functions compare exactly after whitespace normalization. Keep them with their private native cinematic state; broad original-engine deduplication or new state export is not justified by that equality

Remote cinematic actors occupy the extra fly slots and locate their segment without entering gameplay segment object lists. Local player/camera errors set the flyout-failure flag; invalid segment/side transitions stop the optional animation. Runtime observation uses the existing shared accessor and does not serialize a new flyout history. The September user decision abandoning that history mechanism remains in force

## Guidebot policy and scoped validation

The goal policy stores at most four accepted replan timestamps, expires entries at the interval boundary and resets after clock rollback. It reports the next permitted time when full. Pathability selects an explicit special goal when present, otherwise the current goal; audit deferral requires a prior valid timestamp and an unexpired interval. Named route callers supply F1_0 for the per-second limit and 5*F1_0 for audit-only deferral

New owner-policy helpers detect only newly acquired objective keys, allow metadata requests for single-player/cooperative sessions outside input-demo recording/replay and keep cache polling out of competitive games. The actual cache caller separately suppresses recording/replay. Keep these predicates with the existing policy owner, without teaching callers a second policy table

Only the first nine escort hunks are covered: includes for existing save/route/policy owners, standalone live-escort diagnostic shims, player-ship goal text and native pending dock/spawn/cage fields/prototypes. These declarations do not establish full dock/ownership protocol correctness or coverage of later escort hunks

Fresh maintained test_escort_goal_policy.c compiled under MSVC C11 /W4 /O2 /MD /UNDEBUG and ran successfully with no warnings. Its assertions cover pathability, audit interval boundaries, four-per-interval saturation, exact expiration, next-allowed times and clock rollback. GQR-0004 remains open because explicitly enabling assertions for this probe does not repair the normal release-test oracle configuration. The owner-policy suite was inspected but not run. No full engine, Android, movie or peer flyout run occurred

## Routing tail and native policy

RETAIN. The assigned route tail starts at line 2251, inside the preceding publication function, and ends at line 2746. Earlier route sections are named context only and keep their independent coverage obligations

Explicit Hostages intent retains its command while prerequisite planning is pending. A live hostage is tracked by object index and signature; missing/stale targets select another hostage. A three-second cadence limits ordinary repeated segment planning, while pending resumable work continues. An absent or unsuitable exit/unexplored candidate becomes a physical hostage objective instead of changing the command to SCRAM

Refresh rejects cooperative nonowners, polls the existing cache, consumes coalesced events and keeps dirty work pending while the resumable planner runs. Completion monitoring avoids revalidating a stale incumbent certificate during replacement work, preventing that same failure from restarting the job every frame. Explicit world notifications still invalidate at their source. Audit-only work obeys the five-second governor; other event/certificate work follows the existing decision owner

Semantic exit-goal equality deliberately differs from full shared guidance equality. The adoption result either restores the prior native goal/path, publishes a changed candidate, or clears invalid guidance and directs the companion back to the player. Physical frontier selection preserves the semantic objective while exposing the reachable guidance endpoint and keyed-door hint. Keep these native actor/path operations with the engine and decision comparison in its existing shared owner; no new callback facade or broad relocation is justified

The fallback goal selector is available without the live planner. Explicit commands remain authoritative; pending metadata or non-end-of-level target modes do not silently fall through to key/reactor selection. The existing key order, living reactor scan, boss preference and exit fallback remain native policy. This review does not establish whole-route correctness or complete earlier guidebot_route.c scopes

The full routing mode implementation/header preserve Original=0 and Enhanced=1, mechanically matching Kotlin. Android stores the launcher default atomically and leaves active-session changes on the game thread. Cooperative sessions query synchronized Netgame policy; playback metadata overrides the ordinary default. A live mode change uses escort_reset_routing, including native AI path reset, while restore_mode only resets derived navigation and lets a cooperative host update network policy. That distinction preserves the path/timers loaded from a save. The named integration test covers differing defaults and replay startup as source context only; it was not rerun

Original smoothing preserves conversion of the complete floating-point sum back to fixed point. Both x/y/z triplets in the pinned Redux aipath.c match the extracted helper after only parameter substitution and whitespace normalization. The initial literal comparison correctly failed because it included both upstream occurrences and whitespace; the final check explicitly compares both triplets, without changing the product

## HUD and startup integration

The persistent goal message borrows static engine-owned text, admitted only for a live matching companion signature. HUD preparation reserves its row before boss/queued messages and rendering uses that prepared row. The four-message base capacity minus boss and Guidebot rows remains at least two. Enumerating ordinary visibility combinations and queued counts from the reviewed formulas yields at most six rectangles including guided-view and Android restore status, within the eight allocated. This is static capacity evidence, not a visual rendering test. Existing shared row geometry and native text ownership should remain; no extra HUD abstraction is warranted

Startup delegates native D1/D2 resource choice, palettes and initial bitmaps to the existing native facade. Silent classic-demo dump explicitly selects audio services before asset generation retirement can use them. Movie setup is skipped for native D1; desktop route confirmation suppresses titles and dispatches its existing negative/not-requested, zero/started and positive/error return contract ahead of ordinary replay/menu startup

The setjmp target is established before startup restore can close a game window and longjmp; its return proceeds to the event loop instead of rerunning startup. Android expected-exit state is cleared when window close is cancelled. Mission-assets shutdown is called before game-data teardown; its current implementation disables mission transitions rather than claiming to unmount or free every resource. Retain these compact lifecycle hooks and existing BR-0206 restore/BR-0345 window-lifetime owners. Diagnostic gating remains BR-0294

## Native mine and level decoding

RETAIN. All 54 assigned hunks across seven inherited mine/palette/render/level-loader files were read. The legacy texture mapping is now engine-owned in d1_in_d2_levels.c, with former global inputs made explicit parameters. Mechanical comparison preserves every mapping and orientation branch after those named substitutions and one deliberate diagnostic change from Warning to urgent console output. The obsolete unique-texture predicate and header declarations are removed; no duplicate mapping should be restored in platform code

Compiled mine loading reads both texture references before the native decoder. Native D1 normalizes authored texture slots against native count; fallback conversion remains available without native assets. The helper stages both references and only assigns after validation. Existing D2 decoding remains outside that hook. The editor trigger record uses TRIGGER_DISK_SIZE rather than the expanded runtime structure size; New_file_format_load becomes private to its actual owner

verify_robot_object is exactly the previous robot-property block after whitespace normalization, including handmade comments. Its new replacement-loader caller refreshes robot model/radius/mass/drag without incrementing initial robot counts, resetting object lifetime or initializing a player again. Native D1 reactor/vclip fixups remain in the engine helper. Old D1 AI follow-path fields are retained instead of discarded

The loader now reads the existing section offsets instead of skipping them and seeks walls, triggers, reactor links, matcens and lighting independently. This preserves padding and nonadjacent sections. Empty sections skip seeking; the shared helper checks the starting offset/count, not the entire decoded extent. REWIND_PHYSFS_FILE wraps the same underlying handle and its PhysFS read delegates to that handle, so later direct seeks affect the subsequent wrapped reads. No parser-hardening completion is claimed

Version 29/30 trigger records use the native decoder for D1 levels and preserve the historical D2 single-action priority otherwise. Native D1 keeps its action mask and original type/link storage. Native trigger-link binding returns handled, error or D2 fallback, avoiding duplicate interpretation in the loader. Wall references are checked before animation access; only door/blastable walls consume animation clip data, permitting irrelevant stale editor fields in other types

The final texture repair uses the existing gray-rock fallback before ambient/collision/render consumers, preserving overlay orientation and recording diagnostics. Native D1 clears D2-only lava/water ambience; ordinary D2 still computes it. Read-only preview suppresses an interactive debug warning and successful load notifies the existing secret-area owner. These source observations do not establish malformed-media safety or complete file admission; such runtime probes remain deferred

## Palette and rendering integration

Palette resolution goes through native presentation resource ownership while preserving custom content precedence. The existing logical palette selection/cache behavior remains; MENU_PALETTE selects the committed native profile. Observer cockpit exclusion remains before native D1 cockpit dispatch and D2 fallback

The texture-label overlay extraction matches the former complete body after removing only the local extern and normalizing whitespace. The original debug header remains needed to reset the label count; it is not an unused include. Guidebot overlay draws in the existing HUD sequence. Standalone Android loading frames clear discarded backing before drawing/flipping, and the existing save/restore of palette state is retained. Introspection-only loading instrumentation remains guarded

No further facade or blanket native deduplication is warranted. Existing GQR-0190 merged-label producer, GQR-0238 binding coherence, BR-0294 diagnostics and BR-0345 lifetime owners remain separate. The shared overlay comparison does not close those issues

## Runtime robot references and disk ownership

RETAIN. All 23 assigned hunks across six inherited robot/score/music files and the deletion of the branch-added local secretarea.h were read. The five widened runtime sound references are still decoded as unsigned bytes, preserving values 128-255 rather than sign-extending the reader result

The explicit robot writer remains in its native format owner. It checks all five widened references for every requested record before writing the first record, then writes the original little-endian fields, signed/unsigned byte bit patterns, padding and joint lists. Both HAM writer callers use the helper and report failure. Static ordered comparison covers all 52 reader/writer field groups with MAX_GUNS=8, NDL=5 and N_ANIM_STATES=5; the disk record remains 480 bytes. This is layout evidence, not proof of every I/O outcome

The maintained upstream-compat test contains an exact 480-byte round trip and pre-write rejection for a second record with an extended sound reference. That test was inspected as source only; no fresh execution or malformed-media probing occurred. Keep runtime registry width distinct from disk format, without moving the serializer into Android or reintroducing raw runtime-structure writes

## Scores, shared declarations and song formats

Android score prompts pass the existing endlevel poll only for an active network campaign ending, so terminal status can progress while teammates finish. Ordinary desktop uses the previous null callback. Native score serialization and menu state remain in scores.c. The introspection helper reads existing scores and returns an achievable larger score unless INT_MAX prevents one; it does not rewrite the score file

Controller translation borrows stack-owned key-event data only for the current synchronous handler call. A/B map to existing close actions and Y maps to the existing reset action with its confirmation. Existing reset-window lifecycle remains BR-0345; no new menu framework or direct score-file mutation is justified

Deleting the local secretarea.h leaves the shared header selected through the existing D2 shared include directory. This removes a branch-created duplicate interface, not a historical native engine format. Current expanded shared declarations remain independently reviewable; the deletion is not a claim that every older declaration still exists unchanged

Song-list admission and file playback consistently accept HMQ through the HMP backend and MIDI/WAV under SDL_mixer, alongside existing formats. Both changed source/header line sequences match D1 exactly after excluding diff location headers. The SDL backend also recognizes HMQ; current shared Android music code is concurrent user work and remains untouched. Native filename capacity GQR-0092 remains open; accepted extension aliases do not fix it

Retain native formats and compact feature hooks. No new finding, remediation, broad upstream deduplication or inherited-saving estimate is admitted

## Native interfaces and presentation

RETAIN. All 668 assigned lines across seven branch-added native files were read, including only the final 21 lines of d1_in_d2_levels.c. Its legacy mapping tail retains shareware door offsets and orientation recursion; the complete mapping was named context in GQ2-0201 and is not newly credited here. All 36 declarations in the four assigned headers have exactly one native implementation

The native level header separates authored-level repair from strict saved-record decoding, carries native trigger storage and names handled/error/fallback return contracts. The 65-byte network record is one length byte plus two possible digests, with zero identifying D2. Named implementation context rejects mismatched namespaces and optional Guidebot availability; existing GQR-0198 decoded-source identity remains open. The header does not justify moving native format or asset semantics into shared platform code

Presentation mounts base archives under distinct prefixes so same-named D1/D2 resources do not depend on root HOG order. Initial ordinary D2 preserves existing overrides; profile switching uses native prefixes. Explicit mission/loose resources keep precedence. Menu images use stable per-kind storage and high-resolution availability checks; palette names remain logical cache keys. Missing native high-resolution art does not fall through to a different game's archive

Text preparation reads into owned storage, decodes line/escape syntax and publishes only after the minimum original text count is present. It preserves the native shortened Spreadfire label. Text mapping uses symbolic correspondence, with a specific fallback for the incompatible help-message format string and built-in D2-only labels. Mechanical comparison of all named dxx_gettext macros verifies 599 mapped symbols and 28 fallback symbols with no mismatch; this is not a claim about every unnamed ordinal or translated text content

Profile activation switches cached text pointers and refreshes installed font/menu resources. Headless definition readers return before presentation initialization. D1 free_text restores the D2 pointer bank when owned, allowing text.c to free its own buffer and separate label; D1-only retirement clears pointers and avoids that D2 cleanup. The mounts are retired there. Existing window/resource lifetime owners remain open; no fresh full lifecycle run is claimed

Native title sequencing starts the title music once, selects its own publisher/logo/descent art and checks Android skip preference between screens while clearing the active-intro flag at completion. Keep this resource and private interpreter ownership in the native implementation. Maintained original-text/override/transition tests were read as source context only

## Native D1 object ordering

The object-list adapter returns inactive without touching D2 lists, then uses native D1 segment migration, linked overflow lists, distance ordering and the ClassicDepth fireball/weapon preference. Its private sort storage and fixed historical list size are not an invitation to broadly deduplicate the upstream engines

The complete comparator and object-list builder match current native D1 after explicit list/eye parameters, private linkage and handled-return substitutions. The add helper additionally checks overflow-list bounds before reading its array entry, an intentional difference that the comparison records rather than erases. Historical fixed-capacity and comparator arithmetic behavior is retained; no pressure/overflow probe or safety completion is claimed. D2 render.c invokes this owner before its distinct ordinary ordering

## Native actor dispatch and path construction

RETAIN. All 56 assigned changed hunks in inherited D2 aipath.c were read, with named native, route, recovery and maintained-test context. Five native D1 path entry points intercept applicable enemy/player paths before D2 behavior; companion paths remain with the D2 owner. Removing global D1 conditionals from D2 center insertion, randomization, polishing and snipe behavior follows that actor split. The companion's uncloaked player-return target is refreshed without modifying the native enemies' event-driven awareness cache

The internal path builder carries explicit segment/edge exclusions and route policy. Route callers prepare the existing metadata view and apply passability/recovery-edge policy; ordinary path calls retain native doorway/openability. Guidebot guidance does not inherit a run-from robot's player avoidance. The extra exclusions are confined to the existing builder instead of a second breadth-first search or platform-owned path arena

Route geometry checks use the larger actor/player radius. Waypoint adjustment searches toward the segment center deterministically, preserving door/blastable interaction targets and requiring a clear candidate leg. Blocked-segment recovery distinguishes a final shooting-switch contact, trigger-retractable wall and confirmed narrow solid geometry. Retry is limited by its two avoid slots, accepted only when reaching the original endpoint; otherwise it restores original points and the outer function publishes the original count. That is not a complete arena/RNG transaction guarantee

Both scratch sites still allocate without admission: expanded smoothing storage and recursive retry copies. This confirms existing GQF-0211/GQR-0197, including its current ordinary/companion and prior-path/RNG requirements. No duplicate finding or allocation-pressure run was added. Existing BR-0381 capacity and GQR-0182 geometry ownership remain separate

The public segment-path wrapper's callers are escort and route-confirmation code, so its internal D2 builder does not imply native enemy dispatch was accidentally bypassed. Its returned route success checks the actual endpoint. Native path-arena ownership and compact original public entry points should remain; avoid extracting a facade that would export private AI state

## Following, cursor and steering policy

Objective following is gated by Enhanced mode, a companion robot, an active route goal and AIM_GOTO_OBJECT. A near point across a portal is consumed only for an open connection and a compatible or clear next leg, preventing a nearby room behind a solid wall from being skipped. Geometry adjustment applies to the current approached waypoint only after a close collision and clear repaired approach

Forward companion paths retire their consumed prefix before the signed-byte cursor overflows. Original mode retains byte-sized path prefixes for midpoint/patrol behavior; paths longer than 128 still need the cursor repair. Native serialized cursor width and ordinary robot behavior remain unchanged. Exact endpoint holding belongs only to the active route-confirmation driver, while live escort keeps its normal endpoint behavior

Steering tracks actor pointer/signature, goal and elapsed time to expire contact state. Portal-stall recovery measures actual displacement before steering toward a clear open portal center. Openable-door reversal may brake until the full-radius leg clears; it does not open the door itself. Precision approach is bounded before route-confirmation scaling and bypasses momentum blending; the named scaling owner acts only for its running controlled actor. Original-mode smoothing uses the previously verified Redux expression helper

Debug path validation keeps the observation and Int3 but removes destructive path clearing; PATH_VALIDATION remains disabled under NDEBUG. Android navigation/reset diagnostics remain with BR-0294. Maintained Original-mode 124-point prefix, FirstStrike long-path and Counterstrike waypoint tests were inspected as source only. No fresh simulation, runtime parity or complete recovery correctness is claimed

## Retired hybrid asset facade

RETAIN the completed retirement. The complete 2,239-line deleted source was read, including validation, sound staging, palette remapping, saved D2 gauges/cockpits, robot/weapon decoding, Guidebot copies, effects/vclips/walls and final model publication. Its many active/saved/loaded flags represented independent overlays on D2 global tables. D1 robot behavior/lightcast could be replaced by retained D2 tuning, native bitmap IDs were remapped into reserved/live D2 slots, and native clips were limited by D2 frame counts

The old staged robot generation validated its model and property tables but did not own the entire installed profile. Sound installation and cockpit remapping had separate mutation and restore paths; Guidebot model/joint/bitmap copying retained another parallel ownership graph. Deleting this arrangement is consistent with native D1 definitions and policy. Do not reintroduce a shared-platform owner for these engine structures merely to reduce native line counts

The current session owner prepares base/custom/optional Guidebot data, publishes it through d1_in_d2_publish_asset_data, then commits the profile. RETAIN. All assigned L1-L750 were read, ending at update_boss's ordinary-boss branch. The next scope owns its remaining branch. The 30-byte record write/read/swap operations explicitly select native AI/morph enemies, preserve both original follow shorts and signed cursor, reset save-only remote ownership and clear D2-only runtime fields. ## Firing, perception and complete native frame

RETAIN the native algorithm owner. All assigned L1501-L2248 were read, completing direct/homing firing, perception and native frame dispatch. ## New ordinary test finding: GQF-0259 / GQR-0245

The maintained write_robot_frame_trace sets Weapon_info[0].homing_flag for variant 6 before its weapon initialization loop zeroes every Weapon_info entry, including zero. Thus the intended homing scenario reaches do_ai_frame with homing disabled. Fresh traces confirm all 126 variant-6 cases have exactly the same four frame records as variant 0 in both engines. The passing 1,260-case comparison must not be represented as full-frame homing coverage

Separate test firing code does set the flag after initialization and asserts native homing clock behavior; this finding is confined to the public-frame comparison matrix. Repair scenario setup after common weapon initialization and assert the effective scenario state so accidental overwrite cannot silently restore duplicate coverage. Rebuild both targets, rerun the public-frame comparison and verify a selected deterministic homing case exercises the intended branch while ordinary controls stay unchanged. No engine change or inherited saving is indicated

Admit P3/high test-correctness finding, score 33 LOW (H/M/B/C/R = 12/0/4/10/7): narrow paired test matrix, source and trace evidence, no inherited diff reduction. No product patch was applied. General-quality preparation can carry this small test fix alongside remaining survey work

## Bitmap decoding, generation ownership and legacy mapping

All assigned L1-L750 were read. L750 is the bulk replacement loader declaration; its body belongs to the already completed GQ2-0186 tail, which also owns the existing unused frame-reader GQR-0244. No additional coverage or savings are claimed for that tail

The shared pixel decoder stages allocation, validates source and RLE spans, measures palette-remap expansion, and grows its private buffer before remapping. Mac index swapping and palette preservation are explicit options. Caller-owned arena copies advance only after size admission; individually owned buffers retain their allocation if shrinking fails. The destination GL binding is cleared only when the completed staged bitmap is installed

Native generations decode every D1 source bitmap and retain native indices, including the high width bit needed by 320-pixel cockpit art. Optional feature generations admit the D2 PPIG/version-2 layout, select only requested dependencies, reject missing requested indices and validate RGB6 source palette channels. Both allocate zeroed bitmap/name slots before partial reads and use the same destructor; it releases GL binding before freeing saved CPU data. The identical small allocation/palette block is measured below but retained: decoding/destruction are already shared, format admission and traversal differ, and there is no inherited-file saving

Optional palette conversion operates only on unpublished owned images. It maps nearest colors over 0..253 and reserves transparent indices 254/255, measures RLE growth, handles raw pixels and updates average colors. Partial conversion can fail without restoring earlier converted images because prepare_guidebot_extension frees the unpublished source on failure and assigns base->guidebot only after remap and identity preparation succeed. These callers and their cleanup paths were read; no whole-Guidebot-source coverage is claimed

Five complete legacy helpers match the original branch base after whitespace/comments and private linkage normalization. The sixth text-table reader matches after explicitly removing the unique-texture filter and redundant single-statement braces. This proves the short-line/continuation/truncation and legacy allocation behavior predates the branch apart from the stated texture selection change. Retain those media/parser concerns as follow-up; do not promote them as new branch defects or run malformed fixtures here

Native texture lookup returns the direct source bitmap index; legacy lookup uses the inverse texture table and source RDL/SDL layout before checking D2 destinations. Destroyed-light conversion protects custom/replacement slots, measures arena usage, copies/remaps pixels, saves prior paging metadata, clears GL references and installs the replacement. Reset restores paging only when pointer and offset still identify that exact replacement, then clears all backup records and arena cursors. Preserve this ownership split with piggy; no broad upstream deduplication

## New GQF-0260 / GQR-0246: omitted imported-briefing pagination repair

The October 4 ordinary briefing overlap repair, commit 867c2192171cee7163c8935b418ed9b0638e4fe4, changed both normal engine title sessions but missed this separate D1-in-D2 implementation. Current check_text_pos still advances an automatic wrap by screen->text_uly, while native D1 now advances by the same font-scaled line height as an explicit newline. On the authored first briefing at base resolution, text_uly is 140; a single wrap therefore advances 140 pixels instead of one text line and immediately exceeds that screen's 59-pixel text box

The imported newline branch also retains the old load_briefing_screen plus reset-to-top behavior when vertical text overflows. Because the retained glyph stream is not cleared there, it can redraw new text over earlier text; the normal D1 implementation now lets check_text_pos request a new page. This is a missed propagation of an already established product fix to a branch-added supported session, rather than a new report about untouched upstream code

Current Android D2 android_briefing_text_snapshot accepts only its own briefing_handler callback and therefore reports no active text for the separate imported callback. Existing Enemy Within evidence exercises the normal D2 session, not this one. The generic briefing trace has short command examples and pixel artifacts, but no retained-text overlap oracle for long ordinary native text. It also unconditionally calls malformed-resource tests in its D2 mode, so the full runner is not executed under this continuation's deferred-probe constraint

Admit P2/high ordinary rendering/paired-fix completeness, score 44 MEDIUM (23/0/4/10/7). Carry the normal line advance and page-transition correction into this owner without duplicating shared geometry or moving private interpretation into Android. Add a maintained ordinary public-window test for automatic wrap and multiline pagination, with a direct oracle that text stays in order and does not overlap. A small explicit snapshot adapter may be used if needed, while keeping private state owned here. Verify D1, D2 and imported sessions and actual rendering, plus Windows/Android builds and scoped quality. This report establishes the missing source fix, not a fresh rendered failure. No product patch or inherited-saving estimate

## Native window, resource and profile lifetime

All assigned L751-L1247 were read, completing static bitmap drawing and the entire session/window/public-entry implementation. Robot drawing temporarily applies the shared briefing pixel aspect and restores both aspect and canvas after rendering. It loads the image and palette, retains the named Mac black-index compatibility branch, sets text colors, allocates a scaled private screen record and initializes text position. An error marks the session failed; draw processing closes the window before using failed page state. This is source lifetime evidence, not graphics allocation/failure-injection evidence

The handler returns on CLOSED before touching its null data pointer. Ordinary close clears the current canvas, releases screen/background/robot resources, portrait data, text and the session. Mouse/key/controller handling preserves advance-versus-skip and Android readiness rules. The loop pumps cooperative cancellation and pairs screen-advance begin/end; authored page completions are distinct from automatic layout pages. Existing BR-0345 still owns wider nonlocal window escape behavior; this local normal-close review does not close it

The entry allocates and initializes its private session, handles absent text and failed window creation, preserves briefing/endgame song selection, applies the shared authored canvas, then runs events until the owned window is gone. Planning mode counts native selected messages and frees text/session without creating a window. No full cooperative sequencing or input-lifecycle execution was done here

Public briefing, ending and order-form entries return unhandled only outside the native gameplay profile. D2 titles dispatches to them before its own private session. ## Native gauge, bitmap and weapon-panel behavior

All assigned L751-L1500 were read, completing score-added display and ending within status-bar key drawing. Named L1501-L1508 context completes that boundary; GQ2-0188 already owns the remainder of the cockpit file and all public lifecycle/dispatch services

Complete helper comparisons cover homing warning, native proximity bombs, weapon text, lives, energy/shields, cloak/ship/key drawing, ammo and fade transitions. Ordinary D1 has a BombGauge preference which is absent from D2's player configuration; imported native drawing therefore omits that field access and uses the native proximity slot directly. Keep this explicit platform-neutral native policy rather than reading the D2 smart-mine selector. No new preference mismatch is inferred

Alpha decoding uses a static 1024x1024 pixel buffer, checks its area limit, handles raw/RLE rows, and applies native weapon-window transparency spans. It releases the old decoded GL texture, rebuilds the bitmap/overlays, and remembers source pointer plus dimensions. The deliberate change from function-local cache fields to file-scope fields allows close/reset to invalidate them before native source release. Caller and existing GQ2-0188 evidence confirm overlay descriptors and GL texture are separately freed; there is no omitted heap-pixel free. Pointer/dimension equality alone is not a claim about arbitrary in-place source mutation or context loss

The left/right energy masks retain separate begin/end 2D batches around each line run, with bitmap calls and canvas resets outside. Cloak animation keeps native frame-time and fade behavior; weapon panels retain set/fade-out/fade-in ordering, selected-weapon redraws and ammo/demo notifications. The repeated assignment in fade-out and redundant Vulcan formatting branch are copied native code, not evidence for broad upstream consolidation. Existing GQR-0185 batching, GQR-0238 binding ownership and GQR-0175 restored-clock work remain separate

Status shield-number drawing drops the old background pixel/color fetch because the background is redrawn before gauges. The remaining helper body matches D1; no speculative draw-order or numeric positioning rewrite is admitted. Read-only box parameters and explicit score pointers preserve ownership while avoiding private engine state adapters

The maintained check_profile_cockpit fixture exercises full/status/rear modes, deliberately enables D2 high-resolution capability, checks the D1 status viewport, samples opaque key pixels, checks GL errors and preserves a camera-surround pixel/Viewer. It was read as context only, not run; its one palette/state/resolution selection does not prove every HUD, fade, custom bitmap, software or GLES case. No new source defect survives the scoped comparison, but this is not fresh rendering equivalence

## Optional source selection and dependency ownership

All assigned L1-L750 were read, through the first part of robot publication. The remaining publication/query tail L751-L877 already belongs to completed GQ2-0192; L751-L833 was reread as boundary context, not credited again

The private HAM v3 reader checks fixed disk spans and uses engine record readers. It skips irrelevant wall/gauge and later base ship/cockpit/reactor authority. Crucially, each individual polymodel_read is immediately followed by model_data=NULL, so the serialized pointer never becomes owned memory in this reader. Dependency closure has 13 typed domains and a 0/1/2 absent/pending/visited state. Exactly one companion definition seeds the robot graph, with explicit flare, morph and goal-sound behavior roots. Robot eggs, smart children, weapon afterburner/children, animation joints, model indirection/destruction, texture/effect links and alternate logical sounds add domain-specific references. Bitmap zero and absent sound/model sentinels retain their explicit meanings. Mark-before-expansion and repeated scans allow backward references without processing a visited definition again; native format policy should not become a generic Android graph framework

Model simpler/parent chains and weapon children have their own bounded traversal checks. Joint/model texture ranges select every source entry needed by later contiguous offsets; the ascending runtime assignment preserves adjacency for each fully selected source interval. This is static mapping reasoning, not a fresh arbitrary-media or full-game proof

## Prepared pixels, samples and runtime slots

Selected model streams are allocated and checked through each used submodel. Selected bitmap decoding is delegated to the existing common feature-image owner reviewed in GQ2-0213. The DSND sample reader admits the sample directory, keeps selected offsets/lengths, allocates one packed sample bank and reads only those samples. Its owner frees partial allocations on failed source preparation. Sample names retain the zeroed ninth byte, and source sample-rate selection is explicit

Runtime slots append after the prepared native counts, using domain-specific capacities. All mapping rows start absent, the bitmap fallback is restored to slot zero, and logical extension sounds start at 256 to preserve every original byte slot. Current robot sound fields are widened shorts; weapon sound fields already use shorts. The ordinary robot/weapon/model capacities fit their narrower destination fields. No second live registry or translation cache is introduced

Prepared aliases are checked against native bitmap/sample names; palette conversion happens on unpublished images, followed by source identity hashing. Only complete preparation sets prepared and attaches base->guidebot. The pre-publication validator compares current native base counts to the reserved bases and rejects an already-published extension. Identity still reopens the four source paths after decoding, so existing GQF-0212/GQR-0198 remains live. Reservation/prepared flags and complete hashing do not prove the decoded bytes and reopened bytes are the same generation. This review adds no source mutation, malformed-media or resource-pressure probe

Bitmap and sample registration uses prepared aliases and deterministic mapped slots. Bitmap CPU data remains generation-owned, while model publication transfers its pointer to Polygon_models and clears the source pointer before endian/alignment/init processing. ## Native weapon ordering, acquisition and projectile policy

All assigned L1-L665 were read. The native primary/secondary order is a validated permutation with one cutoff and a distinct logical quad identity. Reader stages a complete candidate before committing through the same domain validator; writer owns the native profile block. Availability preserves direct laser-level/quad aliases, native inventory slots and Fusion's minimum energy. Cycling bounds its walk by order length, preserves the user cutoff rule and maps quads at the native selection point. Automatic selection retains classic wrap ordering versus best-available ordering and proximity exclusion. Shared select_weapon maps logical quads at the boundary for delayed/autoselection, including the already-selected laser case. First-pickup suppression is captured before updating the latch; pending selection retains the best rank while fire is held. Quad status notification remains with its existing outer powerup path
